1549

आस्थि which is changed to अङ्गी ॥ As अङ्गीवान् the name of a particular portion of body; the knee-joints. Otherwise आस्थिवान् ॥ 3. चक्रीवन् is from चक्र which is changed to चक्री, as चक्रीवान् राजा ॥ Otherwise we have चक्रवान् ॥ चक्रीवन्ति सदोहविज्ञानानि भवन्ति is a Vedic example. It means सारस्वते सवेजङ्गमानि सदो हविर्धानानि, न स्वैकभावाधितानि, तानि तव तव कर्तव्याय चक्रयुक्तानि भवन्ति ॥ 4. कश्चीवन् is from कश्चा, there is vocalisation of य and the lengthening is by VI. 4. 2. कश्चीवान् is the name of a Rishi. Otherwise we have, कश्चावान् ॥ 5. क्षणवन् is from लवण which is changed to क्षण ॥ Otherwise we have लवणवान् ॥ Others say, that there is a distinct word क्षण, and the न् is not elided, but changed to ण् ॥ Or that the affix मत् takes the augment नृ ॥ 6. चर्मणवती is from चर्मन्, there is non-elision of न् and its change to ण् ॥ Or मत् has taken नृद augment. The Charmanvati is the name of a river. Otherwise we have चर्मवती ॥

उदन्वानुदधौ च ॥ १३ ॥ पदानि ॥ उदन्वान्, उदधौ, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उदन्वानिष्पुडकशब्दस्य मतानुवन्मानो निपात्यते उदधावर्थे संज्ञायां विषये ॥

13. The word उदन्वान् is irregularly formed, in the sense of “a sea”.

It is derived from उदक ‘water’ with the affix मत् ॥ उदन्वान् is the name of a Rishi, because he controlled the rains, it rained at his command. It also means ocean or that in which water is held, like तटाक &c. The affix कि is added by III. 3 93, and उदक changed to उद by VI. 3. 58, and thus we have उदधि: ॥ Why do we say “when meaning a sea”? Observe उदकवान् घट: ‘a pot having water’. Here the main idea is not that of “holding or containing”, but simply the general fact of possessing water: a human being may also possess water in the same way.

राजन्वान्सौराज्ये ॥ १४ ॥ पदानि ॥ राजन्वान्, सौराज्ये ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ राजन्वानिति निपात्यते, सौराज्ये गम्यमाने ॥

14. Also राजन्वान्, when the sense is of a good government.

The kingdom whose king is good is called राजन्वान् देशः, राजन्वती पृथ्वी ॥ The affix मतुप् is used here in the sense of प्रशंसा or praise. Otherwise राजवान् ॥

छन्दसीरः ॥ १५ ॥ पदानि ॥ छन्दसि, इ, रः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विषये इषणान्ताङ्गेफान्ताचोत्तरस्य मतोषे भवति ॥

15. In the Chhandas इ is substituted for the म् of मत्, when the stem ends in इ (or ई) or र ॥

To take some examples of a stem ending in इ, as बिबती आज्ञानुवाक्या भवति; हरिषो मे इषं स्वा; अधिपति वती जुहोति; चतुरग्निवानिव; आरेवानेतु मा विशात् (आरेवान् from रये with vocalisation). सरस्वतीवान्, भारतीवान्, इधीवांबरः ॥ As all rules have

1550

तुद् AUGMENT.

[Bk. VIII. Ch. II. §. 17]

optional force in the Chhandas, we have no change here सप्रथिमन्तम्, कथिमान्, कर्तिमान्, मूर्ध्नि ते बावापृथिवीम् ॥ Of stems ending in र् we have भीर्वान्, पूर्वान्, आशीर्वान् ॥

अतो तुद् ॥ १६ ॥ पदानि ॥ अनः, तुद् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसीति वतेते उन्नतादुत्तरस्य मतेर्मुद्रागमो भवति छन्दसि विषये ॥

16. The affix मत् gets the augment तुद्, in the Chhandas, after a stem ending in अन् ॥

As अक्षयन्तः कर्णवन्तः सखायः; अस्यन्तं यदनस्यां विभर्त्ति (Rig. I. 164. 4), अक्षयन्ता लाङ्गलेन; शीघ्रवती, मूर्ध्नवती ॥

The word अक्षयन् is thus formed: आशि + मतुप् = अश् + अन् + मत् (अनक् is substituted for the final of akshi by VII. 1. 76) = अक्षयन् (the न् is elided by VIII. 2. 7). Now we add the augment तुद् ॥ If this augment is added to मतुप्, as नतुप् then it becomes a portion of मतुप्, and this न् would be changed to व् by VIII. 3. 9 read with I. 1. 54, and not the letter न्, because न् intervenes. If we add this augment to the end of the stem, then in अक्षयन्ता &c. we cannot change it to व् because of the prohibition in VIII. 4. 37, and the augment being तुक्, the न् would be changed to व् by VIII. 3. 7 in सुपथिन्तरः &c (VIII. 2. 17). The first view, however, is the correct one and the difficulty in its acceptance is obviated by तुदोऽसिद्धत्वात् तस्य च वत्वं न भवति; ततः परस्य च भवति; as shown above.

The तुद् augment being considered as asiddha, is not changed to व्, but the letter following it, is so changed. Thus अक्षयन् (VII. 1. 76) + मत् = अक्ष + मत् (the न् of the stem is elided by VIII. 2. 7). Add the augment तुद् now, and we have अक्ष + मत् ॥ The augment according to VIII. 2. 1, is asiddha, so that according to VIII. 2. 9, व् is substituted for व्, and not for न्, as would have been required by I. 1. 54.

नाद् घस्य ॥ १७ ॥ पदानि ॥ नात्, घस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नकारान्तादुत्तरस्य घसंज्ञकस्य तुदागमो भवति छन्दसि विषये ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ मृरिदान्नम् तुद् वक्तव्यः ॥ वाः ॥ रथिन ईकारान्तादिशो च परतः ॥

17. In the Chhandas, the affixes तर and तम receive the augment तुद् after a stem in न् ॥

The affixes तरप् and तमप् are called प ॥ Thus सुपथिन् + तर = सुपथि + तर (VIII. 2. 7) = सुपथि + मतर (VIII. 2. 17) = सुपथिन्तरः ॥ So also दस्युहन्तमः ॥

Vårt:—The augment तुद् is added to these affixes after मृरिदान्नम्; as मृरिदान्नः (III. 2. 74, the affix is वतिप्).

Vårt:—Long ई is the substitute of the final of रथिन् before तर and तम ॥ The word रथिन् is formed by the affix इति in the sense of मतुप् ॥ The final न् is first elided by VIII. 2. 7, and then for the short ई of रथि the long ई is substituted by the present vårtika. If the long ई were substituted for the final न् of रथिन् as रथि + तर, then this long ई being asiddha, it could not be compounded by ekådesa with the preceding ई into ई, and the form would always remain रथि + तरः ॥ As रथीतरः, and रथीतनं रथीनाम् ॥ Or this ई may be considered to have come after रथि in the sense of मतुप् ॥

BK. VIII. CH. II. § 19 ] CHANGE OF र TO ङ ॥

1551

कृपो रो लः ॥ १८ ॥ पदानि ॥ कृपः, रः, लः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कृपेक्षी रो रेफस्य लकारविषो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ कृपणकृपणकृपीटकपूरादयोपि कपेरेव द्रष्टव्याः ॥

वा० ॥ बालमूललघुसुरालमहसुलीनां वा रोतमापद्यतइति वक्तव्यम् ॥

वा० ॥ कपिलकार्नीनां सताछन्तसोर्या रो तमापद्यतइति वक्तव्यम् ॥

18. For the र of the root कृप्, there is substituted ङ ॥

The र here merely indicates the sound, and includes both the single consonant र and the same consonant of the vowel ङ ॥ So also with ङ ॥ So that for the single र there is substituted ङ ; and for र when a portion of ङ, the ङ is substituted, i. e. ङ becomes ङ ॥ Thus कृप्=क्लप्, as in the sūtra लुटि च क्लपः (I. 3. 93). कल्मा, कल्मारी, कल्मारः ॥ क्लमः, क्लमवाद् ॥

The word कृपा is derived from the root कृप् by vocalisation, as it has been enumerated in Bhidādi class (कपेःसंमसारणं च III. 3. 104). The vocalised root-form कृप् is not to be taken here, as it is ālākshanika form.

Vārt:—The words कृपण, कृपण, कृपीट, कर्पूर &c, are also from कृप् ॥ Or by the Uṇādi diversity, the ङ change does not take place.

Vārt:—Optionally so of बाल &c. As, बालः or बारः, मूलम् or मूरम्, लघु or रघु, अघुरः or अघुलः, अलम् or अरम्, अङ्घुलिः or अङ्घुरिः ॥

Vārt:—Optionally so in the Vedas, or when names, of कपिलका &c, as कपिरकः or कपिलकः, तिलिप्लीकम् or तिलिप्लीकम्, लोमाणि or रोमाणि, पांश्चर् or पांश्चले, कर्म or कल्म, शुक्लः or शुक्लः, कल्मषं, कर्मषं ॥

Some say 'र and ङ are one': and operations regarding र may be performed with regard to ङ ॥

उपसर्गस्यायतौ ॥ १६ ॥ पदानि ॥ उपसर्गस्य, अयतौ ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अयतौ परत उपसर्गस्य यो रेफस्य लकार अ. इ. मे भवाते ॥

19. ङ is substituted for the र of a Preposition, when अयते follows.

Thus पलायते, प्रायते ॥ Here arises the question, does the word अयति qualify the word र, or does it qualify the word Preposition. In the first view, the sūtra would mean, "the र immediately followed by अयति is changed to ङ" ॥ But as a matter of fact, र is never immediately followed by अयति ॥ Thus in म+अयति or परा+अयति, the letter अ and आ intervene respectively. The ekādeśa sandhi of these, will make र immediately followed by अयति; but the ekādeśa, being sthānivat will prevent it. This difficulty however, is overcome by the maxim येन नाध्यवधानं तेन व्यवहितेऽपि वचनप्रामाण्यात्, for otherwise the rule will be useless. For the same reasons, परि+अयते=पलायते, though here य intervenes between र and अयते ॥ In short, the intervention of one letter is considered as no intervention.

In the second view, the sūtra would mean when a Preposition is followed by ayat then its र is changed to ङ, and none of these difficulties will arise

1552

र CHANGED TO ल ॥

[BK. VIII. CH. II. §. 21]

with regard to the above forms. But then would arise a fresh difficulty, for the र् of प्रति would also require to be changed into ल् ॥ Some say, that प्रति is never followed by अयति; while others hold that the form प्रख्यते (प्रति + अयते) is valid. According to the first view, the valid form is प्रख्यते ॥ The स् of the Prepositions दुह् and निह् is changed to र्, but this र् is not changed to ल्, because it is asiddha: thus we have the forms निरयणम्, दुयणम् ॥ But there is a preposition निर् also the र् of which is changed to ल्, as निलयनम् ॥ See VII. 2. 46. According to the Siddhānta Kaumudi, there is a Preposition दुह् also, which gives दुयते ॥

प्रो यङ्कि ॥ २० ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रः, यङ्कि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गु इत्येतस्य धातो रेफस्य लकार आविशो भवति यङ्कि परतः ॥

20. ल् is substituted for the र् of गु in the Intensive.

Thus निजैगिल्यते, निजैगिल्यते, निजैगिल्यते ॥ The root गु takes यह, when the sense of contempt is conveyed, with regard to the action denoted by the root, (III. 1. 24). गहिंति गिलति = जैगिल्यते ॥

Some say that य of the sūtra includes the two roots गु (गिरति Tud. 117) and गु (गुणाति Kry. 28). Others hold that the Tudādi grī is only taken and not the Kryādi. The Kryādi grī never takes the Intensive form, no example of which is to be met in literature.

Why do we say in the Intensive? Observe निगीयते with the Passive affix यक् ॥

अचि विभाषा ॥ २१ ॥ पदानि ॥ अचि, विभाषा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अजादौ प्रख्ये परतो प्रो रेफस्य विभाषा लकाराविशो भवति ॥

21. The र् of grī is optionally changed to ल्, before an affix beginning with a vowel.

As निगिरति or निगिलति, निगरणम् or निगलनम्, निगारकः or निगालकः ॥

This is a vyavasthita-vibhāṣā, the optional forms have particular meanings. Thus गलः meaning 'neck' is always with ल्; while गरः 'poison' is always with र्.

In निगीयते or निगाल्यते, the elision of णि is considered sthānivad, and hence this option, though the actual affix begins with य ॥ Obj.—The sthānivad-bhāva rule is invalid here by VIII. 2. 1. Ans. The rule पूर्वावासिज़् does not hold good with regard to the rules of संयोगाविलोप, लय and णय on the maxim 'तस्य दोषः संयोगाविलोपलयणयेषु' ॥

Or the र् will be *first* changed to ल्, as being antaranga, and then the णि will be elided.

The forms गिरि, गिरः are either from the Kryādi root grī, or *l*-change has not taken place on the maxim धातोः स्वरूपमङ्गे तत्प्रव्यये विज्ञानम् and as the

BK. VIII. CH. II. §. 24 ] ELISION OF FINAL.

1553

affixes श्री and अः are not affixes which are ordained after a verb, but are affixes added to nouns, hence the ल change has not taken place. In fact the words 'an affix beginning with a vowel' in the sūtra, means "a verbal affix beginning with a vowel," and not a noun affix. These are the Dual and Plural of the Nominative case of गृ formed with the affix बिषप ॥

परेश्व धाङ्कयोः ॥ २२ ॥ पदानि ॥ परेः, च, घ-अङ्कयोः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ परि इत्येतस्य यो रेफस्तस्य घशले ङ्कुशले च परतो विभाषा लकार आदेशो भवति ॥

वर्तिकम् ॥ योगे चोति वक्तव्यम् ॥

22. The र् of परि is changed to ख्, before gha and anka.

As परिघः or पलिघः, पर्यङ्कः or पत्यङ्कः ॥ The word घ here means the word-form घ, and not the technical घ of तरप् and तमप् ॥ See III. 3. 84 by which हन् is replaced by घ ॥

Vārt:—So also, it must be stated, before the word योगः ॥ As, परियोगः or पलियोगः ॥

संयोगान्तस्य लोपः ॥ २३ ॥ पदानि ॥ संयोगान्तस्य, लोपः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ संयोगान्तस्य पदस्य लोपो भवति ॥

23. When a word ends in a double consonant, the last consonant is dropped.

As गोमान्, यवमान्, कृतवान् and हतवान् ॥ In श्रेयान्, श्रेयान्, the ह् though subsequent in order, does not prevent the operation of this rule, because it is asiddha (VIII. 2. 66). Thus श्रेयन् + स = श्रेयन् + स (VII. 1. 70), = श्रेयन् (VI. 1. 68) = श्रेयन् (VIII. 2. 66) = श्रेयन् (VIII. 2. 23) = श्रेयान् (VI. 4. 8). But though the रुल् does not debar lopa, it debars the जश् change. By VIII. 2. 39, the final स् required to be changed to a letter of जश् class; ह् prevents it. As यशः, पयः ॥

For रुल् is ordained even where the present संयोगान्तलोप applies and where it does not apply. Thus it is ordained in श्रेयन् where the present sūtra applies, as well as in पयन् where this sūtra does not apply. But the जश्ल् rule (VIII. 2. 39) covers the whole ground of रुल्, hence if जश्ल् rule were not debarred by रुल्, the latter would find no scope. Therefore रुल् debars जश्ल् to justify its existence, but it does not debar संयोगान्तलोपः for it still has scope left to it else where.

In इष्यन् and मष्यन् formed from इषि + अच् and मषु + अच्, by changing इ and व to य and व्, we have इष्य + अच् and मष्य + अच्, where य and व् are final in a pada, and so they require to be elided. It is, however, not done, because यन् substitution is a Bahiranga operation, as it depends upon two words and consequently, is considered asiddha for the purposes of this rule, which depends on one word only.

Why do we say 'of a Pada'? Observe गोमन्तो, गोमन्तः ॥

1554

EL. SIGN OF स् ॥

[ Bk. VIII. Ch. II. § 25

रासस्य ॥ २४ ॥ पदानि ॥ रात्, सस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ संयोजानतपक्षस्य यो रेफरस्तस्मादुत्तरस्यान्तस्य सकारस्य लोपो भवति ॥

24. Of a word ending in a conjunct consonant, only स् is elided, if it comes after र; (but any other consonant coming after र is not elided).

Thus अक्षाः and अन्साः for अक्षार्स् and अन्सार्स् the Aorist of क्षर् and स्वर् in the following passages: गोभिरक्षाः, प्रलञ्चमस्साः ॥ The ईद is not added as a Vedic diversity. See VII. 3. 97.

So also मातुः, पितुः for मातुर्स् and पितुर्स् ॥ Here by VI. 1. 111, the क्+अ of मातु+अस् is changed to इ, which is followed by र् by I. 1. 51.

Though the final स् would have been elided even after र् by VIII. 2. 23, the special mention of स् after र् shows, that this is a niyama rule. So that any other letter than स् following after र् will not be dropped. Thus ऊर्क् from ऊर्ज्+किवप् (III. 2. 177), here इ is not elided, though final in a pada, but is changed to a guttural by VIII. 2. 30, and to क् by VIII. 4. 56. Also अमार्द् from इज् in लह् the तिप् (इ) is elided by VI. 1. 18; there is vriddhi by VII. 2. 114, the ज् is changed to इ by VIII. 2. 36, which is changed to इ VIII. 4. 53 and finally to इ (चर्) ॥

धि च ॥ २५ ॥ पदानि ॥ धि, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ धकारादि प्रत्यये परतः सकारस्य लोपो भवति ॥

*Kārikā*:—धि सकारे सिचो लोपभकारादिति प्रयोजनम् ।

आशाखं तु कथं जशत्वे सकारस्य भविष्यति ॥

सर्वमेवं प्रसिद्धं स्याच्छुति भापि न विद्यते ।

छड्भापि न मूढेभ्ये ग्रहणं सेटि दृश्यति ॥

धसिमसोर्न सिध्येत तस्मास्सिअग्रहणं न तत् ।

छान्मसो वर्णलोपो वा यंयंक्वर्तारमभरे ॥

25. The स् is dropped before an affix beginning with ध ॥

As अलविध्यम्, अलविद्दुम्, अपविध्यम्, अपविद्दुम् for अलविध्यम् and अपविध्यम् ॥ Had this स् (of सिच्) not been elided; then स् would be first changed to इ, and then to a letter of जश् class (VIII. 4. 53), इ would never be heard even optionally, though so required by VIII. 3. 79, but the forms would be always with इ, as अलविद्दुम् &c. ॥

From an *ishti*, the elision of स् is confined to the स् of the Aorist सिच्, and not to any other स् ॥ Thus स् is not elided in चकाद्धि in चकाद्धि पलितं शिरः (हे शिरः पलितं सच्च चकाद्धि शोभस्वेद्यः). It is the Imperative of चकास् the सिप् is changed to हि, and हि to धि (VI. 4. 101), and स् to इ by VIII. 4. 53. Similarly it does not apply to पयस् धावति, where स् is changed to इ and then to इ (VI. 1. 114)

BK. VIII. CH. II. §. 25 ]

ELISION OF स् ॥

1555

=पयो धावति ॥ The elision of स् in सन्धिः from पस् with क्तिन्, and in बन्धान् from मस् in the Imperative with सान्, is a Vedic diversity. But according to Patanjali चकाधि is the proper form; while in पयो धावति the antaranga स् debars this bahi- raṅga स् elision.

Obj.—If so, how do you form आशाप्य, by the elision of स् of शास्; for स् would not be elided? Ans.—The स् is not here elided but changed to जश् letter, by VIII. 2. 39. Obj. If so, स् may always be changed to जश् letter, and there is no need of eliding it; in pronouncing, 'it will make no difference, whether you pronounce with one consonant or two, e.g. आशाप्य or आशाप्य ॥ Moreover by so doing, you will shorten the sūtra VIII. 3. 78, by omitting the word लुह् from it. For the forms like अच्योडुह्म, अद्वोडुह्म, will be evolved regularly by changing स् of सिच् to ष्; and the ष् after it will be changed to ष्, and then ष् changed to इ् by जश्व (VIII. 4. 53). Ans.—So far it will be all right, but in सेद् Aorist we shall never get the alternative forms अलविडुह्म &c, though we may get the form अलविडुह्म (VIII. 3. 79). Therefore, the word सिच् should be taken.

Obj.—If सिच् is to be taken here, then the स् of पस् and मस् will not be dropped, and we shall not get the forms सन्धिः and बन्धां in the passages सन्धिश्च मे सपीतिश्च मे, and बन्धां ते हरीधानाः ॥ Therefore, the present sūtra should not be confined to सिच् only. Ans.—We shall explain सन्धिः by saying, that it is a word derived from सच्, and so also बन्धां from the root बन्ध ॥

[N. B.—The word सन्धिः is generally thus derived; अद्व+क्तिन्=पस्+ति (II. 4. 39)=पस्+ति (VI. 4. 100)=ष्+ति (VIII. 2. 26). Had the present rule been confined to सिच्, the स् could not have been elided by VIII. 2. 26. See VI. 4. 100, where these two forms are developed]. Or we may explain these forms as Vedic irregularity, by which letters are sometimes dropped, and so पस् and मस् have lost their स् ॥ That letters are sometimes dropped in the Chhandas, we see in passages like the following इक्कत्तारमध्यरे for निक्ष्कत्तारमध्यरे; तुभ्येदमने for तुभ्यमिदमने; आम्बानां चहः for नाम्बानां चहः; अच्याधिनी हगणः or अच्याधिनीः सुगणाः ॥

The above discussion is summarised in the following

Kārikā:—धिसकारे सिचोलोपचकाज्जीति प्रयोजनम्, 'This rule is confined to the elision of the स् of सिच् only, for the sake of preserving the स् in चकाज्जि' ॥

आशाप्य तु कर्प? जश्व सकारस्य भविष्यति ॥ 'How then do you form आशाप्य by the elision of स्? The स् is not elided but changed to a जश् letter'.

सर्वमेवं प्रसिञ्च स्याच्, छूति चापि न विद्यते । लुह्वापि न मूर्धन्ये महणं सेटि दुय्यति ॥ 'If this be so, then let जश् come every where, for there is no difference in sound, moreover this will shorten VIII. 3. 78 by omitting the word लुह् from it. The जश् cannot come every where, as the difficulty will be in सेद् Aorist'. पसि भसोर्न सिध्येत, तस्मात् सिच् महणं न तत् । 'The forms सन्धिः and बन्धां could not be formed

9

1556

ELISION OF स् ॥

[BK. VIII. CH. II. § 28]

from घस् and भस् if the elision of स् were confined to सिन्. Hence सिन् should not be read into this sutra.'

छान्दसो वर्णलोपो वा यथेष्टकर्तारमधरे ' The elision of स् in सन्धिः and बन्धः will be explained as a Vedic anomaly, for letters are often dropped in Vedic forms, as in इष्टकर्तारमधरे instead of निष्ठकर्तारमधरे ॥'

झलो झलि ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ झलो, झलि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ झल उत्तरस्य सकारस्य झलि परतो लोपो भवति ॥

26. The स् is elided when it is preceded by a *jhal* consonant (any consonant except semi-vowels and nasals), and is followed by an affix beginning with a *jhal* consonant.

Thus अभिन्न for अभिन्न, अभिन्नाः for अभिन्नाः ॥ So also अचिन्त, अचिन्त्याः, अवाताम्, अवात ॥ The last example may also be explained by VII. 4. 49; the elision of the स् of सिन् being considered as asiddha, the स् of the root is changed to त् ॥

Why do we say 'of a jhal consonant'? Observe अमंस्त and अमंस्याः ॥ Why do we say followed by a *jhal* consonant? Observe अभिन्नाताम्, अभिन्नत ॥

The स् of this sutra refers also to the स् of सिन्; no other स् is elided. As सोममधुन् स्तोता; इषन् स्थानम् ॥ Here the स् of स्तोता and स्थानं, though preceded by a jhal letter त्, could never be elided as they do not form portion of *one* word.

हस्वादङ्गात् ॥ २७ ॥ पदानि ॥ हस्वात्, अङ्गात् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हस्वात्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्य सकारस्थलोपो भवति झलि परतः ॥

27. The स् is elided, before an affix beginning with a *jhal* consonant, when it is preceded by a stem ending in a short vowel.

As अङ्गत्; अङ्ग्याः ॥ Why do we say after a short vowel stem? Observe अङ्गोऽ, अङ्गोऽ ॥ Why do we say 'after a stem'? Observe अङ्ग्याः, अलाविष्टाम्, अलाविष्टः अपाविष्टाम् and अपाविष्टः ॥ Why do we say 'before an affix beginning with a jhal'. Observe अङ्ग्याताम्, अङ्ग्यत ॥

This lopa is also of the सिन्, therefore not here द्विष्टां, द्विष्टाम् ॥ Here to the word द्वि is added the affix छुन् (V. 4. 18), and then the comparative affixes तर and तम with आम् (V. 4. 11). This स् is not dropped.

इट् ईटि ॥ २८ ॥ पदानि ॥ इट्, ईटि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इट उत्तरस्य सकारस्थ लोपो भवति ईटि परतः ॥

28. The स् is dropped after the augment इट्, if after this स् the augment ईट् follows.

Thus the Aorist-stem of त् is अलाविष्ट् (III. 1. 44; VII. 2. 35), the Personal ending त् gets the augment ईट् by VII. 3. 96; and by the present

Why do we say 'after the augment इद'? Observe अकारवीत्, अकारवीत् ॥

स्कोः संयोगाद्योरन्ते च ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्कोः, संयोग-आद्योः, अन्ते, च ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ पश्चान्ते यः संयोगः ह्यति परतो वा संयोगस्तदाद्योः सकारकारयोलोपो भवति ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ ह्यति सङ्गीति वक्तव्यम् ॥

29. The स् or क्, when initial in a conjunct consonant, is dropped, before a jhal affix, and at the end of a word.

A conjunct consonant, having स् or क् as its first member, when coming at the end of a Pada, or when followed by a jhal beginning affix, loses its स् or क् ॥ Thus from the root लस्ज् we have लम्नः and लम्नवान् before the jhal affix स् and लम्नः; the substitution of न् for न् is considered asiddha for this purpose (VIII. 2. 1). So also साधुलक् at the end of a Pada. Similarly मग्नः मग्नवान्, साधुलक् from मस्क् ॥ So also with initial क्, as सद् from लम्नः; so also लहः, लहवान्, काष्ठलक् ॥

Vārt:— It should be rather stated that 'before a jhal affix included in the pratyahāra सङ्' ॥ The सङ् is a pratyāhāra formed with the स् of सन् (III. 1. 5) and the क् of महिङ् (III. 4. 78). It thus includes all the krit affixes, and dhātu affixes i. e. affixes which come after a verb and not the Taddhita or the Feminine affixes. This Vārtika applies to all the preceding sūtras of this sub-division and is of use in the following places.

गिरोऽमोऽभिहिष्टां च ह्यपस्यः काष्ठशकस्थिरः । कुञ्चाधुर्येति मा सैषु सत्वादीनि भवोचिन्ति ॥

So that in गिरः there should not be the optional स् by VIII. 2. 21. In अमोऽभिः, the स् of अमस is not elided before भि as required by VIII. 2. 25. In हिष्टां the rule VIII. 2. 27 does not apply. In ह्यपस्यः the rule VIII. 2. 26 does not apply. In काष्ठशकस्थिरः the rule VIII. 2. 29 is non-applicable. In कुञ्चा the rule VIII. 2. 30 does not apply. In धुर्यः (धुरं बहति) there is not lengthening by VIII. 2. 77. Thus काष्ठशकस्थिरः ॥ Here क् would require to be elided as initial in a consonant, followed by a jhal consonant य ॥ काष्ठशक् is formed by adding कुँप् to शक् ॥ But according to Patanjali, there can be formed no valid word from शक् with कुँप्, a fortiori, no such word can be formed as काष्ठशकस्थिरः ( काष्ठशक्ति निष्ठति ).

In वास्यर्थम्, काव्यर्थम्, the स् and क् are not elided, because य् is a Bahiranga substitute and asiddha, and the word वास्य काव्य are not considered as Pada, ending in a conjunct consonant.

Why do we say 'of स् and क्'? Observe नर्गति, वर्गति ॥

Why do we say 'initial in a conjunct consonant'? Observe पयः शक् ॥

Why do we say 'at the end of a word'? Observe सक्षिता, सक्षकः ॥

चोः कुः ॥ ३० ॥ पदानि ॥ चोः, कुः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ चवर्गस्य कवर्गविषो भवति ह्यति परतः पदान्ते च ॥

30. A Guttural is substituted for a Palatal, before a *jhal* affix, or at the end of a word.

Thus पक्ता, पक्तुम्, पक्तव्यम् and ओदनपक् from पञ्च ॥ Similarly वक्ता, वक्तुम्, वक्तव्यम् and वाक् ॥

In कुण्डा the feminine in शप् of कुण्ड (कुह्) by IV. 1. 4 list, the म् a palatal is followed by च् a jhal letter, and therefore, it should be changed to a guttural. It is not so, because Pāṇini himself uses this word, in this form, in sūtra III. 2. 59. Or because the rule is confined to सह affixes only. Or the root is कुण्ड without र् and with a penultimate न्, and not म् as we find in Dhātu-pātha कुण्ड कौटिल्याली भावयोः (Bhu. 200). With the elision of न् we have निकुचितिः before the किंतु affix (VI. 4. 24) कुचितः in Past Part. and अच्युकुन् ॥ In निकुचितम् we cannot have the optional किंतु of the Nishthā by I. 2. 21, because the elision of the penultimate न् by VI. 4. 24 preceded on the basis of the affix being किंतु, thus कुण्ड+क्त=कुण्ड+त ॥ This elision of न्, will not make the root उदुपथा for the purposes of the application of rule I. 2. 21, on the maxim सन्निपातलक्षणो विधिरनिमित्तं सन्निपातलक्ष्य ॥ In fact, one of the reasons on which this maxim is based, is this very fact, that the elision of न् does not make the root उदुपथा for the purposes of making the affix non-कित् ॥ The affix किंतु takes the augment इद under VII. 2. 9 (vārt). The word कुह् is formed from this root by किंतु affix (III. 2. 59): the final च् is first elided by VIII. 2. 23, and then म् is changed to इद by VIII. 2. 62. The rule VI. 4. 24 thus finds no scope here.

In this view of the case we say कुण्ड is an irregular form of this root kunch, because it is so exhibited in III. 2. 59. There the anusvāra and parasavarṇa change of this न् to म् by VIII. 3. 24 being considered asiddha, there is no palatal म्, and hence there is no guttural change.

हो ढः ॥ ३१ ॥ पदानि ॥ हः, ढः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इकारस्थ इकारादेशो भवति हालि परतः पदान्ते च ॥

31. द is substituted for ह before a jhal letter and at the end of a word.

Thus सोडा, सोदुम्, सोडव्यम् ॥ The इद is not added by VII. 2. 48, जलायाद्, तुरायाद् by ण्वि (III. 2. 63, VI. 3. 137 and VIII. 3. 56) वाडा, वोडुम्, वोडव्यं, प्रछयाद्, विणयाद् (III. 2. 64) from सह and वह, with the affixes त्, तुम्, तिव्य and ण्वि ॥ For the त् of these affixes there is substituted ध by VIII. 2. 40, and this ध is changed to द by VIII. 4. 41, before which is dropped the first द by VIII. 3. 13. For the द in प्रछयाद् either द is substituted by VIII. 2. 39, or द by VIII. 4. 56.

दादेधोतोधैः ॥ ३२ ॥ पदानि ॥ द-आदेः, धातोः, घः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इकारादेशो इकारस्थ इकारादेशो भवति हालि परतः पदान्ते ॥

32. Of a root beginning with द, the ध is substituted for ह, before a jhal letter or when final in a Pada.

BK. VIII. CH. II. §. 33 ]

६ CHANGED TO च ॥

For the final ६ of a ६-beginning root, च is substituted under similar circumstances. As ६ग्धा, ६ग्धुम, ६ग्धव्यम्, काष्ठधक्, ६ग्धा, ६ग्धुम्, ६ग्धव्यम्, ६ग्धुक्, from ६ह and ६ह ॥ For the ६ of the affixes ६ &c. च is substituted by VIII. 2. 40, before which, the च becomes ग by VIII. 4. 53. For the च in काष्ठध् is substituted ग by VIII. 2. 39, or क् by VIII. 4. 56, and ६ becomes च by VIII. 2. 37.

Why do we say "of a root beginning with ६"? Observe ६हा, ६हुम्, ६हव्यम्, ६हिलिद् ॥

The force of the genitive case in धातोः is not to make it in apposition with the word ६हः, but it has the force of denoting a part as related to the whole: so that it means "the word which begins with ६ and forms part of a root, for the ६ of such a part is substituted च." What does follow from it? The letter च is substituted in अधोग् also, which begins with अ ॥ For without the above explanation (धातोरययो यो राधिश्वस्तवयवस्य हकारस्य &c), the च would have come in examples like मास्म धोक्, without the augment अ, but not where there was the augment अ ॥ Moreover, that it is an अवयवयोगा षष्ठी will appear necessary in sūtra VIII. 2. 37.

If it has the force of denoting a 'portion or member', how do you explain the forms ६ग्धा, ६ग्धुम्, for here no portion is taken but the whole word? This will be explained on the maxim of व्यपदेशीवद् भावः "An operation which affects something on account of some special designation, which for certain reasons attaches to the latter, affects likewise that which stands alone, and to which therefore, just because the reasons for it do not exist, that special designation does not attach". (व्यपदेशीवद् एकस्मिन्) ॥ Or we may explain the sūtra, by saying 'that root which begins with ६ in its original enunciation in Dhātupāṭha'? Thus in original enunciation the root is लिद् not beginning with ६ ॥ If a Derivative root be formed from it like ६मिलिद् (६मिलिद्मिच्छति = ६मिलिद्मि), it is a root which begins with ६; the ६ of this Denominative root, however, will not be changed to च, for it is not a root of upadeśa. Therefore, when we add ६किद् to this root, we get ६मिलिद् by VIII. 2. 31, and not ६मिलिक् ॥

वा ६हुमुहणुहणिहाम् ॥ ३३ ॥ पदानि ॥ वा, ६ह, मुह, णुह, णिहाम् ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ ६ह मुह णुह णिह इलेतेषां धातुनां हकारस्य वा प्रकारवेशो भवति हानि परतः पदाने च ॥

33. The ६ of druh, muh, shṇuh, and shṇih is optionally changed to च, before a jhal letter or at the end of a word.

Thus ६हः, ६हा or ६ग्धा, मिख्युक्, मिख्युद्, मुह, उन्मोन्धा, उन्मोवा, उन्मुक्, उन्मुद्, मुह, उत्कोन्धा, उत्कोवा, उत्कुत्कु, उत्कुत्, लिद्, लेङ्धा, लेङा, लिक्, लिद् ॥

The root ६ह would have taken always च by the last sūtra, this makes it optional. The others would not have got च but for this sūtra.

These roots belong to Radhādi sub-class of Divādi gaṇa: and are

taught there in this very order (Div. 89-91). By belonging to Radhādi subdivision, the ६ is optional (VII. 2. 45). Instead of making the sūtra बाहुहारीनाम्, this longer formation of the aphorism indicates that the rule applies to यहूदा also; as शेषुक् or शेषुद् ॥ See VII. 1. 6, for if the roots were taught not specifically but by गण, then the rule would not apply to yañ luk.

नहो धः ॥ ३४ ॥ पदानि ॥ नहः, धः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नहो हकारस्य धकारवेशो भवति ह्यति परे पदानि च ॥

34. The ६ of नह is changed to ध before a jhal letter or at the end of a word.

As नखः, नद्धुम्, नखव्यम्, उपानम्, परीणम् ॥ The ६ of the affixes ६ &c, is changed to ध by VIII. 2. 40; and for the preceding ध is substituted ६ by VIII. 4. 53. उपानम् is formed by VIII. 2. 39, read with VIII. 4. 56. परीणम् is formed by कियन् as it belongs to सम्पदाति class, the lengthening is by VI. 3. 116, and ण-change by VIII. 4. 14. It would have shortened the processes of transformation, had only ६ been ordained in the sūtra, instead of ध; but the ordaining of ध is for the purposes of VIII. 2. 40, by which there should be ध for the participial ६ &c, in नखम्, and that there should not be the change of this Nishṭhā ६ into ६ by VIII. 2. 42. Thus नध+त=नध+ध (VIII. 2. 40)=नध+ध (VIII. 4. 53). But had the substitute been ६, we should have नध+त=नध by VIII. 2. 42.

आहस्थः ॥ ३५ ॥ पदानि ॥ आहः, धः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आहो हकारस्य धकारवेशो भवति ह्यति परतः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ हृद्यो भेदछन्दसि हस्येति वक्तव्यम् ॥

35. For the ६ of the root आह, there is substituted ध before a jhal letter.

As हृद्यात्म, किमत्य ॥ The word आध्य becomes आत्य by VIII. 4. 55. Why has the last mentioned substitute ध not been ordained here, for this ध would also have given the form आत्य by चर change, as the ध is also changed to त; and by so doing there would have been only one sūtra, instead of two i.e. आहवशो ध would have been enough? Making this separate substitute, is for the sake of indicating that the rule VIII. 2. 40, does not apply here. For had VIII. 2. 40, still applied, the substitute ध of the last sūtra would have been enough. The त substitute, however, would have been the best.

The word ह्यति is understood here. Hence there is no change before vowel affixes, as आह, आहवुः, आहुः ॥

Vārt:— In the Chhandas, भ is substituted for the ६ of ६ and मह ॥ Thus भदेमेन संभरति; महस्य गुणाति; सामिधेन्यो जधिरे, उद्गामञ्च निमामञ्च ब्रह्म देवा अवीधृधम् ॥

ब्रह्मसृजसृजसृजयजराजप्राजच्छशो पः ॥ ३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ ब्रह्म, सृज, सृज, सृज, यज, राज, प्राज, छ, शाम, पः ॥

36. For the final consonants of vrasch, bhrasj, srij
mrij, yaj, rāj, and bhrāj, and for the final छ and झ, there is
substituted घ् before a jhal letter, or at the end of a word.

Thus ब्रज्:—ब्रज्, ब्रह्म, ब्रह्म्यम्, मूलवृद् ॥ ब्रज् । ब्रह्म । ब्रह्म्यम् । धनायुध् । सृज् ।
ब्रज् । ब्रह्म । ब्रह्म्यम् । रज्जुमुद् । यज् । माहीं । माहुम् । माहेष्यम् । कंसपरिषद् । यज् । यज् ।
ब्रह्म्यम् । ब्रज्यम् । राज् । सम्राट् । स्वारद् । विराद् । विश्राद् ॥ The झ ending words would have
been changed to जशु-letters and the others to Gutturals; this sutra debars
that by ordaining घ ॥ In मूलवृद् and धनायुध् there is vocalisation by VI. 1. 16, the
झ is elided by VIII. 2. 19, and घ becomes जशु-letter झ, which becomes ङ by
VIII. 4. 56. The word शब्बमाद् is formed by किष्, there is lengthening and
no vocalisation.

The roots राज् and आज् are never followed by a jhal beginning affix,
because such affixes will always take इद augment. These roots are, therefore,
mentioned here, for the sake of the change of their ज to घ, when at the end of
a word. Some, however, form nouns like राष्टिः, आष्टिः with किष् affix from these
roots by III. 3. 94, vart, and इद augment is prevented by VII. 2. 9.

Of roots ending in छ we have मच्छ्:—ब्रज्, ब्रह्म, ब्रह्म्यम्, शब्बमाद् ॥ According
to one view, the letter छ should not be mentioned in this sutra: for by VI.
4. 19, छ is always changed to झ, and this झ will be changed to घ by the present
sutra. Others hold, that the change of छ to झ by VI. 4. 19 is confined before
किष् or किष् affixes, and therefore the mention of छ is necessary in this sutra;
moreover the घ substitution here, and the झ substitution in VI. 4. 19. refer to
the conjunct letter छ (with the augment तुक्). For if it were not so, then
छ alone being changed to घ, the तृ of तुक् would be changed to ङ, and we should
have पृष्टः instead of पृष्टः ॥

Of roots ending in झ we have लिष्:—लेष्टा, लेष्टुम्, लेष्टयम्, लिद्; विश्:—वेष्टा,
वेष्टुम्, वेष्टयम्, विद् ॥

75, अजर्षः ॥ Then the first र is elided अजर्षः (VIII. 3. 14). Then there is
lengthening by VI. 3. 111, and we have अजर्षः ॥

The monosyllable should be such that it should begin with a बश् and
end with a झप् letter, and should be a full root or the portion (अवयव) of a
root. In fact, this word which we found necessary in VIII. 2. 32, is absolutely
necessary here, in order to explain forms like गर्षः from the Denominative root
गर्षम्, by बिष् ॥

Why do we say “a monosyllable beginning with बश् and ending with
झप्?” Observe दामलिङ् from the Denominative root दामलिङ् ॥ For had एकाचः
not been employed in the sūtra, the word धाताः (VIII. 2. 32) would have qua-
lified बश् and the sūtra would have meant “in a root which ended in a jhash,
and which contained a बश् letter as its member; there is jhash substitution for
such बश्”, and the इ of दामलिङ् would be changed then.

Why do we say “for a बश् letter”? Observe कुघ्—कोस्यति here क् is
not changed to घ ॥ Why do we say ending in jhash? Observe दास्यति ॥
Why before स and ध्व ? Observe बोद्धा, बोद्धुम्, बोद्धुम् ॥

Why have we taken ध्व and not merely ध्व? Observe दावलिङ् from इध् in
the यह लुक्, Imperative 2nd Per. singular, the ि being changed to धि (VI. 4.
101). The substitutes are four म, प, इ and ध, and their respective sthānins are
also four, i. e. ब, ग, ङ and द; so that द is the substitute of ङ; but, as a matter
of fact, ङ never so stands at the beginning of a monosyllable, and so there is
no द substitution.

दधस्तथोश्च ॥ ३८ ॥ पदानि ॥ दधः, त, थोः, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दध इति दधाति: कृतविध्वनो निर्विध्यते। तस्य झलन्तस्य बश्: स्थाने भय आविशो भवति तकार-
यकारयोः परत्यकारात् स्थोश्च परतः ॥

38. For the इ of दध (the reduplicated form of
धा) is substituted ध, before the affixes beginning with त, थ, स
and before ध्वम् ॥

The word दध is taken in the sūtra as the reduplicated form of धा
दधाति and not the root दध धारणे of Bhuādi class, as दध intervenes there.
By the word च we draw in the words स and ध्व ॥ Thus धत्तः, धधः,
धत्ते, धत्तव, धध्वम् ॥ By the express injunction of this sūtra, the elided अ is not

BK. VIII. CH. II. §. 40]

THE FINAL LETTERS.

1563

considered as sthānivat. The last sūtra could not have applied to इध for two reasons. 1st. It does not begin with a इध letter, for the real reduplicate is इध, and इ is merely a substitute, and is considered asiddha. 2ndly. The form इध does not end in a jhash consonant, but in a vowel अ, and though this अ is elided before these affixes, yet the lopa would be sthānivat. Hence the necessity of च in this sūtra. See coutra, the vārtika in Mahābhāshya.

The word झलि is understood here, and so also झपन्तस्व; and there can be no affix, but begins with त or य, that can come after इध ॥ Why do we employ then the words 'before त and य'? Had we not used these, the sūtra would have referred to स and ञ only, as being in immediate proximity, and the ञ draws them in. According to Padamanjari the words तयोय could have been dispensed with: for before स and ञ, the ध change would have taken place by the last sūtra, whilst by this sūtra, the same change would have taken place before all other झलु-beginning affixes, and such affixes that can come after इध are त or य-beginning affixes.

The word jhash is understood here also, therefore the rule applies to इध then only, when it assumes the form of इध, by the elision of आ; and hence not here इधाति ॥

झलां जशोन्ते ॥ ३९ ॥ पदानि ॥ झलां, जशः, अन्ते ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ झलां जश आदिशा भवन्ति पश्यान्ते वर्त्तमानानाम् ॥

39. A corresponding ज, व, ग, ड or इ is substituted for all consonants (with the exception of semivowels and nasals) at the end of a word.

As वाग् अच्, भलिङ् अच्, अँगिनिचिङ् अच्, चिङ् अच् ॥ The word भलिङ् is formed by changing the इ of लिङ् to व first, and then changing this व to ड, a jaś-letter.

The word अन्त 'at the end' is used in the sūtra to indicate that the anuvṛtti of झलि ceases. Thus बस्ता, वस्तुञ्, वस्तव्यम् ॥

The exceptions to this have been given in VIII. 2. 30 &c, and VIII. 2. 66. At an avasāna or Pause, a ञ् consonant may be substituted for a झलु by VIII. 4. 56.

झपस्तथोक्तो ञधः ॥ ४० ॥ पदानि ॥ झपः, त-थोः, धः, अधः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ झप उत्तरयोस्तकारयकारयो स्यानि धकार आदिशो भवति ॥

40. ध is substituted for त or थ coming after झ, म, घ, ड or थ (jhash), but not after the root धा (इध) ॥

Thus from लम् we have लब्धा, लब्धुम्, लब्धव्यम्, अलब्ध, अलब्धाः ॥

The भ् of लम् is changed to व by VIII. 4. 53. From दुइ:—दोग्धा, दोग्धुम्, दोग्धव्यम्, अदुग्ध, अदुग्धाः ॥ The इ is changed to प by VIII. 2. 32, and then it is changed to ग by VIII. 4. 53.

10

1564

NISHTHA न CHANGE.

[BK. VIII. CH. II. §. 43]

From लिङ्:—लेवा, लेवुम, लेव्व्यम्, अतीव, अतीवा: ॥ In लेइध &c, the ह is changed to ड by VIII. 2. 31, and ध changed to ड by VIII. 4. 41, before which the preceding ड is elided by VIII. 3. 13.

From बुध:—बोझा, बोझुम, बोझ्व्यम्, अबुज, अबुजाः ॥ For the ध of बुध there is substituted ड by VIII. 4. 53.

Why do we say “but not after the root ध”? Observe धत्तः, धधः ॥

पढोः कः सि ॥ ४९ ॥ पदानि ॥ पढोः, कः, सि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पकारकारयोः ककारविषो भवति सकारे परतः ॥

41. क is substituted for प or ढ before स ॥

Thus for प of विइ we have विवेक्ष्यते, अवेक्ष्यत्, विविक्षति ॥ For ड of लिङ् (लिङ् VIII. 2. 31) we have लेव्यति, अवेक्ष्यत्, लिळिक्षति ॥

For the स of the affix स &c, is substituted प by VIII. 3. 59.

Why do we say “before स”? Observe पिन्डि, लेडि ॥

रदाभ्यां निष्ठातो नः पूर्वस्य च दः ॥ ४२ ॥ पदानि ॥ रदाभ्याम, निष्ठातः, नः, पूर्वस्य, च, दः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ रेफरकाराभ्यापुत्तरस्य निष्ठातकारस्य नकार आविषो भवति । पूर्वस्य चकारस्य ॥

42. After र and द, for the त of the Participial suffix त and तवत्, there is substituted न, and the same substitution takes place also for the preceding द ॥

After रः—आस्तीर्णम्, विस्तीर्णम्, विशीर्णम्, निगीर्णम्, अवगुर्णम् ॥

After दः—भिन्नः, भिन्नवान्, छिन्नः, छिन्नवान् from भिन्न and छिन्न ॥

Why do we say “after र and द”? Observe कृतः, कृतवान् ॥ The word र here does not denote the common sound र, which would include क् also, but the consonant र ॥ But even if र् be taken a common sound-name including र् and क्, yet the क् change does not take place in कृत &c, because between त and the र्-sound, there intervenes vowel-sound इ, for क् is sounded not like pure र्, but र् + a vowel sound.

Why do we say “of the Participial suffix”? Observe कर्ता, हर्ता ॥

Why do we say “for the त”? Observe चरितम्, हरितम् ॥ Here the त of the Nishtha does not follow immediately after र्, the augment इद intervenes.

Why do we say “of the preceding”? The succeeding इ will not be changed. As भिन्नवद्भ्याम, भिन्नवद्भिः ॥

In the word कार्तिः the descendant of कृतः the त of Nishtha is immediately preceded by र्, but no change has taken place, because the Vriddhi, by which क् is changed to कार्, is Bahiranga and consequently asiddha, and for the purposes of न change, the र् so obtained is invalid.

संयोगादेरातो धातोर्यण्वतः ॥ ४३ ॥ पदानि ॥ संयोग-आदेः, आतः, धातोः, यण्वतः ॥

BK. VIII. CH. II. §. 44 ] NISHTHA न CHANGES.

1565

वृत्तिः ॥ संयोगादिष्यो धातुराकारान्तो यण्वान् तस्यादुत्तरस्य निष्ठात्कारस्य नकारवेशो भवति ॥

43. For the त of the Nishthā there is substituted न, after a root ending in आ and commencing with a conjunct consonant, if the latter contain a semi-vowel.

Thus from ब्रा we have ब्रह्मणः, ब्रह्मणवान् ॥ ग्यानः, ग्यानवान् from ग्या ॥ These roots ब्रा and ग्या end in आ, have a conjunct consonant in the beginning, one of which is a semi-vowel र and ल ॥

Why do we say “beginning with a double-consonant”? Observe यातः, यातवान् ॥

Why do we say “ending in आ”? Observe खुतः, खुतवान्; खुतः, खुतवान् ॥

Why do we say “after a root”? Observe निर्यातः, निर्यातः ॥ For the roots here आ and वा do not begin with a conjunct consonant, and that which is a conjunct i. e. र्या and र्या is not a root, hence the rule does not apply.

Why do we say “having a यण or semi-vowel”? Observe स्नातः, स्नातवान् ॥

त्वादिष्यः ॥ ४५ ॥ पदानि ॥ लू-आदिष्यः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ लूम् छेदने इयेतव्यभूति तु वरण इति यावत् वृक्षारेण समापिता स्वादयो गृह्यन्ते । तेभ्य उत्तरस्य निष्ठात्कारस्य नकारवेशो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ कूकारत्वादिष्यः त्रिश्रितावद्वयतीति वक्तव्यम् ॥ वा० ॥ दुर्गोर्दीपञ्चेति वक्तव्यम् ॥

वा० ॥ पूषो विनाशइति वक्तव्यम् ॥ वा० ॥ सिनोतिर्मासकर्मकर्कृकस्येति वक्तव्यम् ॥

44. The त of Nishthā is changed to न, after the roots लू and those that follow it.

These roots belong to Kryādi class, and commence from लूम् छेदने (IX. 13) and end with तु वरणे (IX. 32).

Thus लूनः, लूनवान्, धूनः, धूनवान्, जीनः, जीनवान् from उषा the vocalisation is by VI. 1. 16.

Vārt:—After a root ending in क् or क् and after a root of Luādi class, the त of the affix किंच is changed to न, like as in Nishthā. Thus कीर्णिः, गीर्णिः, शीर्णिः, हूनिः, पूनिः ॥ These are from क् (IX. 26), ग् (IX. 28), घ् (IX. 18), लू and पूम् ॥

Vārt:—The vowel of the roots दु गती (Bhu. 991) and सु (Bhu. 997), are lengthened before the Nishthā which is changed to न ॥ As भादूनः, विगूनः ॥

Vārt:—The न change takes place after पूम् ‘to destroy’ (Bhu. 1015). As पूना यवाः = विनष्टाः ॥ But पूतं धान्ये from पूम् ‘to purify’ (IX. 12).

Vārt:—The same change takes place after the root सि बन्धने of Svādi class (2) when used in a Reflexive sense of becoming a morsel fit for swallowing. As सिनो भासः स्वयमेव i.e. where a morsel by being mixed with curd, condiments &c, becomes rounded of itself, there this form is used. बन्धमानः पिण्डीक्रियमाणो भासो, यदा दध्यादिव्यञ्जन वशेन तथातुकुल्यं प्रतिपद्यते तदाऽयम् प्रयोगः ॥ But

1566

NISHTHA न CHANGE.

[BK. VIII. CH. II. §. 46]

when not used in this sense, we have सिता पाशेन सुकरी ॥ Moreover, the मास must be the object and not the subject of the verb. Therefore not here: सिता मासो देवदत्तेन ॥

ओदितश्च ॥ ४५ ॥ पदानि ॥ ओदितः, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ओकारितो धाति रुसस्य निष्ठातकारस्य नकारादेशो भवति ॥

45. The त of Nishthā is changed to न, after a root, which has an indicatory ओ in the Dhātupātha.

Thus ओलस्जी—लम्नः, लम्नवान्, ओविजी—उद्विग्नः, उद्विग्नवान् ॥ ओप्यायी वृद्धोः—आधीनः, आ पीनवान् ॥

The roots सुक् प्राणिप्रसदे (Div. 24) &c. are considered as ओदित् ॥ Thus, सूनः, सूनवान्; वृह—वृनः, वृतवान्; व्रीह—वीनः, दीनवान्; व्रीह—वीनः, जीनवान्; धीह—धीनः, धीनवान्; मीह—मीनः, मीनवान्; रीह—रिणः, रीणवान्, लीह—लीनः, लीनवान्, श्रीह—श्रीणः, श्रीणवान् ॥

क्षियो दीर्घात् ॥ ४६ ॥ पदानि ॥ क्षियः, दीर्घात् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ क्षियो धातोर्दीर्घादुत्तरस्य निष्ठातकारस्य नकारादेशो भवति ॥

46. The त of Nishthā is changed to न, after क्षि, when the root-vowel is lengthened.

Thus क्षीणाः, क्षीणाः; क्षीणो जाल्मः; क्षीणस्तपस्वी ॥ The vowel of क्षि is lengthened by VI. 4. 60 and 61.

Why do we say 'when the vowel is lengthened'? Observe अभितमसि मामेशोः ॥ The word अभित् is formed with क् in the sense of भाव and means 'imperishable'. The Nishthā being added in the sense of ण्यत्, there is no lengthening of the vowel by VI. 4. 60.

The root क्षि includes the two roots क्षि क्षये and क्षि निवासगत्योः ॥ As क्षितः कामो मया ॥ See also the commentary of Sāyana on अभितो तिः सनेत्रिमं वाजामन्तः सहस्रिणं ॥ (Rig I. 5. 9).

Obj:—The form क्षियः in the sūtra is the Genitive singular of the root-noun क्षी ending in long ई, and will denote the root क्षी ending in long ई according to the maxim प्रकृतिवदतुकरणं भवति 'an imitative name (as क्षी here) is like its original (the root क्षी)'. What is then the necessity of employing the word दीर्घात् in the sūtra? For had the root क्षि with short इ been meant, the form would have been क्षेः ॥

Ans.—The dhātu imitative noun though taking इयह् (VI. 4. 77) as in क्षियः, includes the dhātu ending in short इ also, as in sūtra VI. 4. 59, 60 where क्षि ending in short इ is taken.

Q. If a root ending in short vowel may also be indicated by an imitative name, declined with इयह् augment, then why is the root क्षि exhibited in sūtra I. 3. 19 as णः instead of णियः i. e. the sūtra ought to have been वि पराभ्यां णियः and not वि पराभ्यां णः ?

BK. VIII. CH. II. § 50 ] NISHTHA न CHANGE

1567

Ans. Here the word जि is not used as a dhātu-imitative word, there is no intention here to denote the verbal idea of the particular act connoted by the root जि; on the contrary, it simply expresses the mere form जि ॥

इयो ऽस्पर्शे ॥ ४७ ॥ पदानि ॥ इयः, अ-स्पर्शे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इया-तेरुत्तरस्य निष्ठातकारस्यास्पर्शे नकार आवेशो भवति ॥

47. The Nishṭhā त is changed to न after इये, but not when the Participle denotes 'cold'.

Thus शीनं घृतम्, शीनो वेदः, शीना वसा; but शीतं वर्तते, शीतो वायुः, शीतमुदकम् ॥ The य of इया is vocalised to ई by VI. I. 24.

The prohibition applies when the noun is an adjective and means 'cold'; and not when it means a disease. Therefore we have प्रतिशीनः with न change.

The word स्पर्शे is a guna word formed by घम्, and denotes the particular guna or sensation to be sensed through the organ of touch. In this sense it is derived from the root स्पृश संस्पर्शने ॥ It also denotes a disease, derived from स्पृश उपतापे ॥ There is nothing to show, what स्पर्शे is meant in the sūtra. Explanation is the only refuge here.

अञ्चो ऽनपादाने ॥ ४८ ॥ पदानि ॥ अञ्चः, अन्-अपादाने ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अञ्चतेरुत्तरस्य निष्ठातकारस्य नकारवेशो भवति न चेदपादानं तत्र भवति ॥

48. The Nishṭhā त is changed to न, after अञ्च, but not when it is in connection with an Ablative case.

Thus समक्री शकुनेः पादौ = सङ्गतौ; तस्मात् पशवो व्यङ्गाः ॥

Why do we say 'when not in construction with an Ablative case'? Observe उदकप्रदकं कृपात् = उद्गतं 'drawn out'.

The word व्यक्तम् is from the root अञ्च व्यक्तिमसण कान्तिगतिषु, and not from the root अञ्च; and hence the Nishṭhā is not changed.

दिवो ऽविजिगीषायाम् ॥ ४९ ॥ पदानि ॥ दिवः, अ-विजिगीषायाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दिव उत्तरस्य निष्ठातकारस्य नकारवेशो भवति अविजिगीषायाम् ॥

49. The Nishṭhā त is changed to न, after दिव, when the sense is not that of 'play'.

The word विजिगीषा means "desire of conquest or gain", but here it means "gambling".

Thus आश्वानः = औपारिकः, पारिश्वानः = क्षीणः ॥ Why do we say "when it does not mean to play"? Observe दृष्ट्वा वर्तते ॥ Here the throwing of dice is with the desire of winning or gaining victory (vijigishā) over the opponent.

निर्वाणो ऽवाते ॥ ५० ॥ पदानि ॥ निर्वाणः, अ-वाते ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ निर्वाण इति निस्तुर्वाहतेरुत्तरस्य निष्ठातकारस्य नकारो निपात्यते । न चेदाताधिकरणो वायव्यो भवति ॥

1568

NISHTHA CHANGES

[BK. VIII. CH. II. §. 54]

50. The word निर्वाण is irregularly formed by changing the Nishthā त to न, when the sense is not that of 'wind'.

The word निर्वाण is formed from the root वा, with the preposition निर् and the Participial affix त ॥ Thus निर्वाणो अग्निः, = उपशान्तः, निर्वाणः प्रदीपः, निर्वाणो भिक्षुः = उपरतः ॥

Why do we say when not meaning “the wind”? Observe निर्वालो वातः, निर्वालं वातेन ॥

In the sentences निर्वाणः प्रदीपो वातेन, निर्वाणोऽग्निर्वातेन, the न change has taken place, because the location of the verb वा is in the प्रदीप and अग्नि, and not in the वात, which is merely an Instrument. Hence the above vṛtti uses the words “if the sense of the verb वा does not govern वात in the locative case”.

शुषः कः ॥ ५१ ॥ पदानि ॥ शुषः, कः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शुषेऽन्तोत्तरस्य निष्ठातकारस्य ककारादेशो भवति ॥

51. क is substituted for the Nishthā त after the root शुष् ॥

As शुष्कः, शुष्कवान् ॥

पचो वः ॥ ५२ ॥ पदानि ॥ पचः वः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पचेऽन्तोत्तरस्य निष्ठातकारस्य वकारादेशो भवति ॥

52. व is substituted for the Nishthā त after the root पच् ॥

As पच्यः, पच्यवान् ॥

क्षायो मः ॥ ५३ ॥ पदानि ॥ क्षायः, मः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ क्षेयातोत्तरस्य निष्ठातकारस्य मकारादेशो भवति ॥

53. म is substituted for the Nishthā त after the root क्षे ॥

Thus क्षामः, क्षामवान् ॥

प्रस्त्योऽन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ५५ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रस्त्यः, अन्यत रस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रपूर्वात् स्थायतेत्तरस्य निष्ठातकारस्यान्यतरस्यां मकारादेशो भवति ॥

54. म is optionally substituted for the Nishthā त, after the root स्थै preceded by प्र ॥

Thus प्रस्तीनः or प्रस्तीतः, प्रस्तीनवान् or प्रस्तीतवान् ॥ In the second alternative when म does not come, we first vocalise the root स्था into स्ती, and then add त ॥ Had Samprasāraṇa not taken place first, then the Nishthā त would have been changed to न after स्था by VIII. 2. 43. But when samprasāraṇa is

once made, the root no longer has a semi-vowel and so there remains no occasion for the application of VIII. 2. 43. See VI. 1. 23 for vocalisation.

अनुपसर्गात्कुलक्षीवकृशोल्लाघाः ॥ ५५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अनुपसर्गात्, फुल्-क्षीव-कृश-उल्लाघाः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ फुल् क्षीव कृश उल्लाघ इय्येते निपात्यन्ते न चेदुपसर्गादुचरा भवन्ति ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ उत्कुलसङ्कुलयोरिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

55. The irregular Participles फुल्, क्षीव, कृश and उल्लाघ are formed then only, when no Preposition precedes them.

The word फुल् is derived from the root भिफला विधारणे the त is changed to ल् ॥ The change of अ to उ (VII. 4. 88) and the want of इद augment (VII. 2. 16) are regular. The same change takes place before क्तवतु also, as फुल्वान् ॥

The affix त् is elided after the roots क्षीव, कृश and उत्-लाघ, and the augment इद is prohibited; this is the irregularity in क्षीवः, कृशः and उल्लाघः ॥

Why do we say when not preceded by a Preposition? Observe प्रफुल्लाः, प्रक्षीवितः, प्रकृशितः, प्रोल्लाघितः ॥ In the case of लाघ, prepositions other than उत् are prohibited.

Or the augment इद is added, and then इत् is elided from क्षीवितः &c. See VIII. 2. 3 *vārt*.

*Vārt*:—The forms उत्कुलः and संफुलः should be enumerated. Here त is changed to ल्, though the root has taken a Preposition.

In the word परिकृशः, the word परि is not a Preposition with regard to the verb कृश; परिगतः कृशः = परिकृशः ॥ So that परि is upasarga of the verb गतः understood, hence we have the form कृशः ॥

तुदविदोन्द्रभ्राघ्राहीभ्यो अन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ५६ ॥ पदानि ॥ तुद, विद, उन्द, प्रा, प्रा, हीभ्यः, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तुद विद उन्द प्रा प्रा ही इय्येतेभ्य उत्तरस्य निष्ठात्कारस्य नकार आदिशी भवति अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

*Kārikā*:—वेत्तेत्तु विदितो निष्ठा विद्यतेर्वित् इय्यते ।

वित्तेर्वित्थ विपथ भोगे विपथ विन्दते ॥

56. The Nishṭhā त may optionally be changed to न, after तुद, विद, उन्द, प्रा, प्रा, ही ॥

Thus तुष्टः or तुष्टः, विज्ञः or विज्ञः, सछुतः or सछुतः, प्राणः or प्रातः, प्राणः or प्रातः, हीणः or हीतः ॥

With regard to ही, the न change was not ordained by any rule, and so it is an aprāpta-vibhāshā. With regards to others, the न change would have *always* taken place by VIII. 2. 42 and 43, this makes it optional.

The root विद विचारणे of Rudhādi is to be taken here, and not the other विद roots. Thus the following: *Kārikā*.

NISHTHA

[ Bk. VIII. Ch. II. § 60

The Nishthā of विद्—वेत्ति of Adādi class is विदितः; (2) of विद्—विद्यते of Divādi class is विदः only; (3) of विद् of Tudādi is विदः; (4) of विद् of Rudhādi are both विदः and विदः ॥ The Tudādi विद् has also the form विदः in the sense of भोग by VIII. 2. 58.

वृत्तिः ॥ ध्या ख्या पू मूर्छि मद इत्येतेषां निष्ठातकारस्य नकारवेशो न भवति ॥

57. The Nishthā त is not changed to न after ध्या, ख्या, पू, मूर्छि and मद ॥

Thus ध्यातः, ध्यातवान्, ख्यातः, ख्यातवान्, पूर्तः, पूर्तवान्, मूर्तः, मूर्तवान्, मत्तः, मत्तवान् ॥

This debars the न change prescribed by VIII. 2. 42, 43.

The root मूर्छि is exhibited in the sūtra in its lengthened form; the root मूर्छि is lengthened by VIII. 2. 78, and the च्छ is elided before त by VI. 4. 21.

वित्तो भोगप्रत्यययोः ॥ ५८ ॥ पदानि ॥ वित्तः, भोग, प्रत्यययोः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ वित्त इति विदेर्लाभार्थादुत्तरस्य नृत्य नत्वाभावो निपात्यते भोगे प्रत्यये चाभिधेये ॥

58. The irregularly formed Participle वित्त denotes 'possessions' and 'renowned'.

This is derived from विद्वत् लाने of Tudādi class, the त is not changed to न though so required by VIII. 2. 42.

Thus वित्तमस्य बहु=धनमस्य बहु 'he has much riches'. Because riches are enjoyed (मुख्यते), so they are called भोग or 'enjoyments' par excellence.

In the sense of 'renowned', we have वित्तोऽयं मनुष्यः "this man is renowned or famous". Here वित्तः=प्रतीतः ॥ प्रतायते=प्रत्ययः ॥

Why do we say when having the sense of 'possessions' and 'famous'? Observe विदः ॥

मित्तं शकलम् ॥ ५९ ॥ पदानि ॥ मित्तम्, शकलम् ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ मित्तमिति निपात्यते शकलं चेतन्वति ॥

59. The word मित्त is irregularly formed in the sense of 'a fragment, a portion'.

Thus मित्तं तिष्ठति, मित्तं प्रपतति ॥ This is synonymous with शकल ॥ The root-meaning of मित्त is not very manifest in this word, it may be taken as a rudhi word. The regular form is मित्तं under VIII. 2. 42.

ऋणमाधमण्यं ॥ ६० ॥ पदानि ॥ ऋणम्, आधमण्यं ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ ऋणमिति ऋद्ध्येतस्माद्धातोरुत्तरस्य निष्ठातकारस्य नकारो निपात्यते आधमण्यंविषये ॥

60. The word ऋण is irregularly formed in the sense of 'debt.'

It is derived from ऋ, the त is changed to न ॥ The word अधमण्यं is compounded from अधम ऋणे "he who in a debt transaction holds a lower position"—

i.e. a debtor. This nipātana shows that such irregular Locative compounds may be formed; for here the first member is *not* in the Locative case, but the second member. The condition of being a debtor is आश्चर्यम् or “indebtedness:”

If this is so, then the word उत्तरम्: ‘creditor’ cannot be formed? This is no valid objection. For आश्चर्य is illustrative only of something to be paid hereafter, in consideration of something formely received; and thus includes उत्तरम् also; which also has been so employed by the author himself in धोरुत्तनम् (I. 4. 35).

The word कण् we use in sentences like कण् क्वाति, कण् धारयति ॥

Why do we say when meaning ‘debt’? Observe कण् वक्ष्यामि, नानुतम् ॥

61. In the Chhandas we have the following irregular Participles:—nasatta, nishatta, anutta, pratūrtta, sūrtta, gūrtta.

The words नसत्त and निपत्त are derived from the root सत् preceded by न and नि, and there is not the न change of VIII. 2. 42. Thus नसत्तनञ्जसा ॥ In secular literature we have नसत्तम् ॥ So also निपत्तः in the Vedas, but निपत्तः in secular literature. The word अनुत्तः is from उन् with the negative अन् ॥ The option of VIII. 2. 56 does not apply here. As अनुत्तमा ते मघवन् (= अनुत्तम्) ॥ प्रतुत्तम् is from स्वः or तुव्, as प्रतुत्तं वाजिनम् (= प्रतुत्तम्) ॥ When it is derived from स्वः then ऊन् is added by VI. 4. 20; and when from तुव् then VI. 4. 21 is applied. तुव् is from स्, the क् is changed to उ irregularly, as तुव्/गावः = तुव्/गावः ॥ तुव् is from गुर्, as तुव्/गावः (= तुव्) ॥

किन्प्रत्ययस्य कुः ॥ ६२ ॥ पदानि ॥ किन्, प्रत्ययस्य, कुः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पदयति वर्तते । किन्प्रत्ययस्य सर्वत्र पदानि कुत्समिष्यते । किन्प्रत्ययो यस्माद्यातोः स किन्प्रत्ययः, तस्य पदस्थालोन्त्यस्य कश्चन्विशो भवति ॥

62. A stem formed with the affix किन् under III. 2. 58 &c, substitutes, at the end of a word, a guttural for the final consonant.

The word पदस्थ is understood here. The word किन्प्रत्यय is a Bahuvrihi meaning ‘that stem which has kvin as its affix.’ For the final consonant of such a stem, a guttural is substituted. As घृतस्पृक् (III. 2. 58), हलस्पृक्, मन्तस्पृक् ॥

The sūtra could have been किन्: कुः; the word प्रत्यय is used in the sūtra to show the Bahuvrihi compound; so that the व् of किन् may not be changed to a guttural. Moreover this Bahuvrihi also indicates that the roots which take the किन् affix, change their final to a guttural before other affixes than किन् ॥

11

1572

FINAL CHANGES.

[Bx. VIII. Ch. II. § 64]

Thus the roots सृज् and हृश् take क्ति to form स्रक् and हृक् nouns by III. 2. 59, 60. The guttural change will take place even when these roots are declined as verbs: as, मानो असाक् मानो अद्राक्, where असाक् and अद्राक् are the Aorist of सृज् and हृश् ॥ The augment अद् is not elided, though the मा is added ( VI. 4. 75 ) as a Vedic diversity. The ईद् augment also does not take place as a Vedic irregularity. The augment अम् is added by VI. 1. 58, and the vowel is lengthened by Vṛiddhi by VII. 2. 3. Thus अद्+सृज्+सित्र+तिप्=अस्रक् ( VI. 1. 58 )=अस्रक् (VII. 2. 3 and VIII. 2. 62). Other wise it would have been ष by VIII. 2. 36. So also in दृग्भ्यां, दृग्भि, the श् is changed to a guttural, though the noun दृश् is a क्ति formed noun and not formed by क्ति; and this is so, because the verb दृश् does take क्ति also.

Obj. If this be so, there ought to be guttural change in रञ्जुसृज्भ्यां from the root सृज् with क्ति? Ans. The guttural change however in not desired here.

In gutturalisation, ज is changed to ग, and श to ख, which both become क् by वावसाने ( VIII. 4. 56 )

नशेवी ॥ ६३ ॥ पदानि ॥ नशोः, वा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पदस्थेति वचते ॥ नशोः पदस्थ वा कवर्गादिशो भवति ॥

63. The final of नश at the end of a word is optionally changed to a guttural.

The word पदस्थ is understood here also. As सा वै जीवनबाहुतिः (Maitr. S. I. 4. 13): or सा वै जीवनगाहुतिः ॥ According to Pro. Bohtlingk this latter form is not found in the Samhita.

Here the root नश has taken क्ति in denoting 'condition or state'; by considering it as belonging to संपादति class.

जीवस्थ नाशः=जीवनक् or जीवनम् ॥ The gutturalisation optionally debars the ष change of VIII. 2. 36. When the ष change takes place, this ष is changed to द् by VIII. 2. 39 and VIII. 4. 56.

वृत्तिः ॥ नकारान्तस्थ धातोः पदस्थ नकारादिशो भवति ॥

64. न is substituted, at the end of a word, for the final म of a root.

As प्रथान्, प्रतान्, प्रथान् ॥ These are formed by adding क्ति to the roots शम्, तम् and इम् ॥ The lengthening takes place by VI. 4. 15. The म् being considered as asiddha is not elided.

Why do we say "of म-ending roots"? Observe भित्, छित् ॥

Why do we say "of a root"? Observe इदम्, किम् ॥
