[Bk. VIII. Ch. III. § 17]

the Vriddhi being considered as Bahiranga, and the र् being the result of such Bahiranga Vriddhi, is asiddha, and is consequently not changed to visarga.

The word पश्च is understood here, and the genitive should be construed here as sthana-sashthi, so that for the final र् of a Pada there is visarga, and not for that र् which is not final.

रोः सुपि ॥ पदानि ॥ रोः, सुपि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ र् इत्येतस्य रेफस्य सुपि परतो विसर्जनीयादिशो भवति ॥

16. Visarjaniya is substituted for the र् called र् (and not any other र्), before the Locative Plural case-affix सु ॥

Thus पश्च, सन्धिः, यश्च सु ॥ The word सुपु is here the Locative Plural affix. Though the र् would have been changed to visarga by the last sutra also; the making of this a special sutra is for the sake of niyama. That is, only र् becomes visarga, and not any other र् ॥ Thus गीषु, भृपु, when the र् is not र् ॥ In पश्च &c, the र् becomes र् by VIII. 2. 66.

मोऽमोऽमोऽपुनस्य योऽसि ॥ १७ ॥ पदानि ॥ भो, भगो, अधो, अपुनस्य, यः, अऽसि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भो, भगो, अधो, अपुनस्य, यः, अऽसि ॥

17. य् is substituted for the र् called र्, when it is preceded by भो, भगो, अधो, अ or आ, before an अश् letter (vowels and soft consonants).

Thus भो अच्, भगो अच्, अधो अच्, भो इदाति, भगो इदाति, अधो इदाति ॥ क आस्ते, कश्च आस्ते, ब्राह्मण इदाति, पुरुष इदाति ॥ The य् is elided by VIII. 3. 19, 20, 22 &c. With य्, the forms will be भोयच्, भगोयच्, अधोयच् ॥

Why do we say 'when preceded by भो &c'? Observe अग्निरच्, वायुरच् ॥ Why do we say 'when followed by a letter of अश् pratyāhāra'? Observe वृक्षः, वृक्षः ॥ No, this is no valid counter-example, because no other word follows the visarga; while some word must follow it because the word sanhitā (VIII. 2. 108) is understood here.

*Ans.*—If this be so, then अश् is employed in this sutra for the sake of subsequent sutras. Its employment here is superfluous. For letters other than अश् are ख्र् ॥ Before a ख्र् letter, the र् will be changed to visarga by VIII. 3. 15; and the यन् of this rule will be considered as asiddha for the purposes of VIII. 3. 15, so there will necessarily be visarga. Thus अश् serves no purpose in this sutra, but is for the sake of subsequent ones. Thus in VIII. 3. 22, the word इति must be qualified by the word अश्, namely those consonants only which are in the class अश् ॥ Before any other consonant there will be no elision of य् ॥ Thus वृक्ष वृक्षति = वृक्षवृक्ष ॥ The denominative verb from this will be वृक्षव्रति ॥ A secondary derivative from this root, with the affix

BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 19 ]

य AND य ELISION.

1605

विच् will be वृक्षव् as in वृक्षव् करोति ॥ Here व् would require elision by VIII. 3. 22, before क्, but it is not so because अशि qualifies इति ॥

*Obj.*—If so, why is the word इह् used in that sutra VIII. 3. 22, it would have been better to say इशि सर्वेषाम् instead of इति सर्वेषाम् ॥

*Ans.*—The word इह् is used in that sutra for the sake of the subsequent sutra VIII. 3. 23, which applies to *all* consonants. Had इशि been used in VIII. 3. 22, then in VIII. 3. 23, इति ought to have been used.

Moreover अशि is used in this sutra, so that rules VIII. 3. 18, 19 may not apply to वृक्षव् करोति ॥

This sutra applies to इ called र्, therefore not here प्रातरव्, पुनरव् ॥

व्योलैधुपयन्नतरः शाकटायनस्य ॥ १८ ॥ पदानि ॥ व्योः, लघुपयन्नतरः, शाकटायनस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वकारयकारयोर्मोभगोअचोअवर्णपूर्वयोः पदान्तयोलैधुपयन्नतर आदिशो भवति, अशि परतः, शाकटायनस्याचायस्य मतेन ॥

18. व् and य् (in भगोय &c and after अ or आ, at the end of a Pada) are pronounced with a lighter articulation before an अश letter, according to the opinion of Sākaṭāyana.

That the effort in pronouncing which is very light is called laghu-prayatna - tara. Effort or articulation is a quality of the person who utters and which is the cause of the utterance of a letter. व् and य् of lighter articulation are substituted for the final व् and य् in भोय, भगोय, अचोय, or after an अ or आ ॥ The lighter व् will replace the heavy व्, and so the lighter य् the heavy य् ॥

Thus भोयच, भगोयच, अचोयच, कयास्ते or क आस्ते, अस्मापुंजर or अस्मा उज्जर, असावादित्यः or असा आदित्यः, हावच or हा अच, हावानय or हा आनय ॥

The lighter articulation results from the relaxation of the muscles and the organs employed in speech. The places of pronunciation are palate &c, the organs are the root, the middle and the tip of the tongue. When the contact of the tongue with the various places is very light, the articulation is laghu prayatna - tara. In fact, य् and य् are to be slurred over.

लोपः शाकल्यस्य ॥ १९ ॥ पदानि ॥ लोपः, शाकल्यस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वकारयकारयोः पदान्तयोरवर्णपूर्वयोलैपो भवति शाकल्यस्याचार्यस्य मतेनाशि परतः ॥

19. व् and य् preceded by अ or आ and at the end of a pada, are elided before an अश letter, according to the opinion of Sākalya.

As क आस्ते or कयास्ते, काक आस्ते or काकयास्ते, असा उज्जर or अस्मापुंजर, हावच or हा अच, असावादित्यः or असा आदित्यः ॥

The name of Sākalya is used to make it an optional rule. Therefore, where there is not the lighter articulation of व् and य् by the last sutra, there

1606

व् AND य् ELISION.

[ Bk. VIII. Ch. III. § 21

also in the other alternative the fuller sounds of व् and य् are heard. Thus there are three forms, *heavy* व् and य्, *light* व् and य् and *elision* of व् and य् ॥

When व् and य् are preceded by ओ, then there is elision by the next sutra compulsorily.

ओतो गार्यस्य ॥ २० ॥ पदानि ॥ ओतः, गार्यस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ओकारादुत्तरस्य यकारस्य लोपो भवति गार्यस्याचार्यस्य मतेन आशी पस्तः ॥

20. य् preceded by ओ is elided, according to the opinion of Gārgya, before an अश् letter.

There can be no व् preceded by ओ, so only य् is taken in explaining the sutra. Thus भो अच्, भगो अच्, भो इदम्, भगो इदम् ॥

The making of it a separate sutra, is for the sake of indicating that this is a necessary (*nitya*) rule and not a vibhāshā rule. The name of Gārgya is used simply *honoris causa* (pujārtha). The elision of laghu-prayatna य्, which VIII. 3. 19 would have otherwise caused, is hereby prohibited. So that laghu pratyatnatara य् does come also. As भो अच् or भोयच्, भगो अच् or भगोयच्, अचो अच् and अचोयच् ॥

According to others every kind of य् (whether heavy or light) is to be elided: and भोयच् is not valid in their opinion.

उभि च पदे ॥ २१ ॥ पदानि ॥ उभि, च पदे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अवर्णपूर्णयोः व्योः पादान्तयोर्लोपो भवति उभि च पदे पस्तः ॥

21. व् and य् (preceded by अ or आ, at the end of a pada), and followed by उ, when it is a word, are elided necessarily.

The *particle* उ is a full pada or word. That Particle is meant here by the word उम्, and not the उम्, which is a root obtained by the samprasāraṇa of वेम् ॥ Thus स उ एकविंशतिः, स उ एकाग्रिः ॥

Why do we use the word पदे “उ when it is a pada”? So that the rule may not apply to उम् the form assumed by वेम् by samprasāraṇa as तन्त्रे उतं = तन्त्रयुतम् ॥ Obj. उम् could never have meant the form assumed by वेम्, for the samprasāraṇa of वेम् is उ, the य् is merely indicatory. Moreover the maxim of lakshaṇa-pratipadokta &c, will prevent the inclusion of this उम् resulting from vocalisation, when there is a separate Particle उम् ॥

*Ans.*—The word पदे is used here for the sake of the subsequent sutras like VIII. 3. 32. So that इदम् may come before a *word* beginning with a vowel, and not before a vowel which is an affix. Thus there is no double व् in परमदण्डिना ॥ This is also a *nitya* rule, and not optional. Had it been optional, there would have been no necessity of this aphorism, because VIII. 3. 19, would have been enough.

BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 25]

NASAL.

1607

हलि सर्वेषाम् ॥ २२ ॥ पदानि ॥ हलि, सर्वेषाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हलि परतो मोमगोअयोअपूर्वस्य यकारस्य पदान्तस्य लोपो भवति सर्वेषामाचार्याणां मतेन ॥

22. (The य् preceded by भो, भगो, अधो, or by अ or आ, being final in a pada, is elided) before a consonant, according to the opinion of all Āchāryas.

Thus भो हसति, भगो हसति, अधो हसति; भो याति, भगो याति अधो, याति, वृक्षा हसति ॥ Though the anuvṛtti of व् and य् both is present here, yet we have taken य only to the exclusion of व् ॥ Because after भो, भगो and अधो there is य only, and never व्; and व् can come only when preceded by अ or आ: the only example of which given by Grammarians is वृक्षव् करोति (VIII. 3. 17). Here व् is not elided, because the word अधि qualifies the word हलि of this sūtra.

Q.—But व् should be elided in वृक्षव् हसति, because ह is an अश् letter.

Ans.—There is no such example to be found in any standard author. Moreover Patanjali in his commentary on the Pratyāhāra sūtra लण् says that no words can end in ह, व्, र्, व् or ल् ॥ So that the existence of the very word वृक्षव् is doubtful.

The word sarveshām indicates that VIII. 3. 18, even does not apply, and there is no light articulation, but lopa there too.

मो अनुस्वारः ॥ २३ ॥ पदानि ॥ मः, अनुस्वारः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मकारस्य पदान्तस्यानुस्वार आदिशो भवति हलि परतः ॥

23. The Anusvāra is substituted for म, at the end of a word, before a consonant.

Thus कुण्डं हसति, वनं हसति, कुण्डं याति, वनं याति ॥ The word हलि is understood in this sūtra. Therefore not here, लभय, किमय ॥ The म् must be at the end of pada; therefore not here; गम्यते, रम्यते ॥

नक्षापदान्तस्य हलि ॥ २४ ॥ पदानि ॥ नः, च, अपदान्तस्य, हलि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नाकारस्य मकारस्य चापदान्तस्यानुस्वारदिशो भवति हलि परतः ॥

24. The Anusvāra is substituted for the न् and म, not final in a pada, before all consonants, with the exception of Nasals and semi-vowels.

Thus पर्याप्ति, यथाप्ति, सर्पीषि, धनुषि with न् (VII. 1. 72); and आकंस्यते, आवि-कंस्यते, अधिजिगांसते with म् ॥

Why do we say 'not final in a Pada'? Observe राजन् मुहृश्च ॥ Why do we say 'before a ह्यल् consonant'? See रम्यते, गम्यते ॥

मो राजि समः कौ ॥ २५ ॥ पदानि ॥ मः, राजि, समः, कौ ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ समो मकारस्य मकार आदिशो भवति राजतो द्विपत्ययान्ते परतः ॥

25. म् is substituted for the म् of सम, before the word राज् ending with the affix क्विप् ॥

1608

NASAL.

[ Bk. VIII. Ch. III. §. 28

Thus समाद्, साम्राज्यम् ॥ The substitution of म् for म् is for the sake of preventing the anusvāra change (cf VII. 1. 40). Why do we say 'before राज्'? See संयत् (VI. 4. 40 Vārt). Why do we say 'of सम्'? Observe किं राद् (V. 4. 70). Why do we say 'ending with विवप्'? Observe संराजिता, संराजितम्, संराजितव्यम् ॥

The विवप् is added by III. 2. 61, the ज् is changed to ष् by VIII. 2. 36, which is changed to द् at the end of a word, in संप्राद् ॥ साम्राज्यम् is formed by व्यम् affix, as it belongs to Brāhmanādi class.

हे मपरे वा ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ हे, मपरे, वा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हकारे मकारपरे परतो मकारस्थ वा मकार आविशो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ यवलपरे यवला वा ॥

26. म् is optionally substituted for म्, before द्, which itself is followed by a म् ॥

The म् may be changed to anusvāra or remain unchanged before a word beginning with झ् ॥ Thus किं or किम् झलयति, 'what does he cause to shake'? कथं झलयति or कथमझलयति ॥

Vārt:—Before झ्, झ्, and झ्, the preceding म् may be changed to य, व or न respectively. Thus किं झ्: or किम् झ्: 'what does it matter about yesterday'? किं झलयति or किम् झलयति 'what does he cause to shake'? किं झलाययति or किम् झलाययति 'what gladdens'.

नपरे नः ॥ २७ ॥ पदानि ॥ नपरे, नः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मकारपरे हे परतः मकारस्थ वा मकाराविशो भवति ॥

27. न् is optionally substituted for म्, when it is followed by द् which has a न् after it.

म् becomes न् before a word beginning with झ्; as किम् झलते or किं झलते 'what withholds'. कथमझलते or कथं झलते ॥

ङ्गोः कुक् टुक् शरि ॥ २८ ॥ पदानि ॥ ङ् गोः, कुक्, टुक्, शरि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ङ्कारणकारयोः पवनतयोः कुक् टुक् हयेतावागमी वा भवतः ॥

28. The augment क् is added to a final ङ्, and the augment द् to a final ञ्, before a sibilant, optionally.

Thus प्राङ्क् शेते, or प्राङ् शेते; प्राङ्क् पञ्चः or प्राङ् पञ्चः, प्राङ्क् साये or प्राङ् साये ॥
पञ्च शेते or पञ्च शेते ॥

The augments are कुक् and टुक् with an indicatory क्, showing that they are to be added to the end of the prior word (I. 1. 46), and not to the beginning of the second word. In sanhita reading, it would have made no difference practically, whether these augments were added to the end of the first, or the beginning of the second. But they are added to the end of the first, in order to indicate that VIII. 4. 63, will take effect. Thus we have प्राङ् छेते also. This छ् change of ञ् would not have taken place, had the augment क् been added to

BK. VIII. CH. III §. 30]

NASAL.

1609

श् of शेते; because in श्=छोटि (VIII. 4. 63) the क्षय letter must be at the end of a pada. So that if क् were added to श् of शेते, as क्शेते, here too श् follows a क्षय letter, but this क्षय letter (क्) is not at the end of a pada, so श् will not be changed to छ (VIII. 4. 63). Thus श् is not changed to छ in the body of a word, like विरप्शिन् though ष is a क्षय letter, पुरा कुरस्य विस्पो विरप्शिन् ॥ विरप्शिन्= महन्, formed with the Preposition वि added to the root रष, with the Uṇādi affix शिनि ॥

Moreover in प्राङ् साये, the स is not changed to ष by VIII. 3. 59. Had the augment क् been added to साये, as क्साये, the स would have been changed to ष, as प्राङ् साये, for then VIII. 3. 111, would not have applied, as स was no longer at the beginning of a pada.

Moreover in वण्ड् साये, the स् is not changed to ष because of the prohibition of VIII. 4. 42. Had इ् been the augment of साये, as द्साये, then there would have been the change of स् to ष by VIII. 4. 41.

डः सि घुद् ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ डः, सि घुद् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ डकारान्तात्पवादुत्तरस्य सकारादेः पदस्य वा घुडागमो भवति ॥

29. After a word ending in ड्, there may optionally be added the augment ष to a word beginning with स् ॥

Thus भलिद् स्याये or भलिद् साये, मधुलिद् स्याये or मधुलिद् साये ॥

The word डः is to be construed as Ablative singular, and not Genitive singular of ड्, because of the maxim उभयनिर्देशे पञ्चमी निर्देशो बलीयान् ॥

Q.—Why it is घुद् and not घुक्, in other words, why is this augment added to the beginning of the second word and not to the end of the first?

Ans.—This is done in order to prevent the ष्टु change by VIII. 4. 41. But being at the beginning of the second word, VIII. 4. 42 would prevent this change. भलिद्+साये=भलिद्द्साये, (VIII. 4. 41) but the correct form is भलिद् स्याये ॥ For the ह of भलिद् is ह substituted by VIII. 2. 31, which becomes ड् by VIII. 2. 39, for the ध of the augment, त is substituted by VIII. 4. 55, and for ड् there is इ by the same rule.

नइच् ॥ ३० ॥ पदानि ॥ नः, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नकारान्तात्पवादुत्तरस्य सकारस्य वा घुडागमो भवति ॥

30. After a word ending in न्, घुद् is optionally the augment to a word beginning with स् ॥

Thus भवान् स्याये, महान् स्याये or भवान् साये, महान् साये ॥ The ध of the augment becomes त् by VIII. 4. 55. This त् is asiddha (VIII. 2. 1), and therefore न् is not changed to इ by VIII. 3. 7. This is the reason why the augment is exhibited as घुद् and not तुद् ॥ In sūtra VIII. 3. 29 तुद् would have done as well but not so here. This view of the Kāśikā, however, is not approved by Padamanjari. The न् can never be changed to इ here, because त् is followed

1610

NAMUT.

[BK. VIII. CH. III. § 32]

by स which is not an अम् letter. The word अम्परे is understood in VIII. 3. 7. In fact, तुद् would have been a better augment.

शि तुक् ॥ ३१ ॥ पदानि ॥ शि, तुक् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नकारस्य पश्चात्तस्य शकारे परतो वा तुगागो भवति ॥

31. The augment त may optionally be added to a word ending in न, when a word beginning with श follows.

Thus भवान् च्छते ॥ The augment is added to the end of the preceding word, and not to the beginning of the second word, in order to change श into छ ॥ In fact, the augment षुद् added to the second would have been as good as तुक्, namely both are त; but then छ change would not have taken place.

*Obj.*—If this be so, then why न् is not changed to ण, since it is no longer final in a pada, when तुक् is added to it, in कुर्वन् च्छते ॥

*Ans.*—This is to be thus explained. The sūtra स्तोः दधुना दधुः (VIII. 4. 40) should be divided into two parts, in order to prevent ण change. Thus the first part will be स्तोः दधुना, which will mean that स and तु followed by श and चु will not cause the change of न to ण ॥ The next sūtra will be दधुः, which will mean that the preceding स and तु are changed to श and चु respectively.

डमो हस्वादचि डमुणित्यम् ॥ ३२ ॥ पदानि ॥ डमः, हस्वात्, अचि, डमुद्, नित्यम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हस्वात्परो यो डम् तदन्तात्पवादुत्तरस्याचो डमुदागो भवति नित्यम् ॥ डगनेभ्यो यथासंख्यं डगना भवति ॥

32. After a word ending in ड्, ण or न which is preceded by a light vowel, the same consonant ड्, ण or न is added invariably at the beginning of the next word, which commences with a vowel.

The word डमः is in the Ablative singular here; and हस्वात् qualifies डमः; and डम् itself qualifies the word पदस्य understood, and thus there is tadanta-viddhi. Though the word पदस्य (VIII. 1. 16) is in the Genitive singular, yet it should be converted here into Ablative singular, because of its connection with डमः ॥ अचि is in the Locative singular, but should be construed as Genitive singular here: it is exhibited in the 7th case for the sake of brevity, and of the subsequent sūtras. डम् is a pratyāhāra meaning ड्, ण and न; and so also डमुद् is a pratyāhāra containing the three augments डुद्, णुद् and तुद् ॥

In other words ड् is augment after ड्, ण after ण and न् after न्; or that these letters are doubled practically. Thus डुद् is the augment after a word ending in ड्, as पश्यङ्कास्ते ॥ णुद् is the augment after a word ending in ण, as

BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 33 ]

व SUBSTITUTION.

1611

वर्णणास्ते ॥ तद् is the augment after a word ending in न्, as कुर्वन्नास्ते, कुर्वन्नयोचत्, कु-षन्नास्ते, कुषन्नयोचत् ॥

Why do we say 'ending in ङ, ण or न'? See त्वमास्ते ॥ Why do we say 'preceded by a light vowel'? Observe प्राङ्गास्ते, भवानास्ते ॥ Why do we say 'followed by a vowel'? Observe प्रत्यङ्करोति ॥

The Mahabhashya thus comments on this aphorism :—

*Vārti:*—इन्द्रादि पदादिमहणम् 'The इन्द्र augment is added to a vowel which stands at the beginning of a word'. So that in इन्द्र+आ (Ins. Sing.), तद् is not added to आ, because it is not the beginning of a Pada. Then should this vārtika be held to be necessary? No, because the word पदात् is understood here: so तद् will not come in इन्द्र+आ ॥ But then it will come in परमन्द्र+आ ॥ Because it is a compound of two nouns, and though the case-affixes have been elided, yet इन्द्र+आ is here a Pada by reason of pratyaya lakshaṇa; and hence there should be तद् here added to आ ॥ Ans. This is no valid objection. इन्द्र+आ is not here a Pada, on the maxim उत्तरपदत्वे चापदादिविधीलुमता लुप्तं प्रत्ययलक्षणं न भवति 'When an affix has been elided by लुङ् or लुप्, the pratyaya-lakshaṇa rule will not apply, when the object of it is to give the designation of Pada to the second member of a compound, with the exception of the rule applying to the beginning of a Pada'. Thus in परमन्द्र+आ the word इन्द्र+आ is not treated as a पद, because the rule to be applied is to the *end* here. But the second member of a compound is treated like a pada, when a rule is to be applied to the beginning of a Pada. Thus in वधिसेची, the second member सेच् is considered as a Pada for the purposes of the rule सात पदाद्योः (VIII. 3. 111), and the स is not changed to ष ॥ This view proceeds upon the supposition that the word पदात् governs this sūtra. But the anuvṛtti of पदात् ceased with VIII. 1. 27, as we stated before. How are we then to get out of this difficulty? Are we to make the above vārtika necessary? No: because the anuvṛtti of पदे from VIII. 3. 21 runs into this sūtra. So that the sūtra means अजादि पदे इन्द्र+आ भवति ॥ 'The augment इन्द्र+आ is added to a vowel with which a Pada commences'. Not therefore to the case-affix आ in इन्द्र+आ ॥

मय उभो वो वा ॥ ३३ ॥ पदानि ॥ मयः, उभः, वः, वा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मय उत्तरस्य उभो वा वकारादेशो भवति अचि परतः ॥

33. व् is optionally the substitute of the Particle उ, when it is preceded by a मय consonant (all consonants with the exception of semivowels, sibilants, ह and ञ), and is followed by a vowel.

Thus शषु अस्तु वेदिः or शम्बस्तु वेदिः, सद् उ अस्य रेतः or सद्स्य रेतः, किम् उ आवपनम् or किम्बावपनम् ॥ The उ is a Pragrihya by I. 1. 14, and therefore would have remained unchanged, this ordains व् optionally. This व् being considered asiddha, the म् is not changed to anusvāra in किम्बावपनम्, शम्बस्तु &c, by VIII. 3. 23.

16

1612

VISARGA SANDHI.

[BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 36]

When this ङ is followed by इति, and preceded by a मय consonant, then by I. 1. 17, it is optionally प्रगुहा, and it may be replaced by ङ् ॥ When it is not a pragrihya, then it is changed to ङ् by यणादेश (VI. 1. 77), or to ङ् by the present sutra. In the case of यणादेश ङ्, there is anusvāra by VIII. 3. 23, as किमिति ॥ When it is a Pragrihya, then it is changed to ङ् by the present sutra as किमिति or किमु इति ॥ So also with ङ् substitute, where the ङ् will be nasal: as किमिति, or ङ् will remain unchanged, as किम ङ् इति ॥ Thus we have five forms with इति ॥

विसर्जनीयस्य सः ॥ ३४ ॥ पदानि ॥ विसर्जनीयस्य, सः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ विसर्जनीयस्य सकार आविशो भवति खरि परतः ॥

34. स् is the substitute of a visarga, when a hard consonant (खर्) follows.

The word खरि is understood here. Thus वृक्षदण्डादयति, वृक्षदण्डादयति, वृक्षष्ठकारः, वृक्षष्ठकारः, वृक्षष्ठकारः, वृक्षष्ठकारः, वृक्षष्ठिनोति, वृक्षष्ठिनोति, वृक्षष्ठीकते, वृक्षष्ठीकते, वृक्षष्ठरति, वृक्षष्ठरति ॥

By VIII. 3. 15, the र् was changed to visarga before a hard consonant, or at the end of a Pause. In the present sutra, no special cause being mentioned, the स् change would take place, not only before a hard consonant, but at the Pause also, i. e. in वृक्षः, वृक्षः also. This however, is not the case, because the word संहितायाम् governs this sutra; so the स् change will be in Sānhitā only, and not in Pause, moreover we read the anuvṛtti of खरि here and so prevent the स् change in Pause.

शप्पेरे विसर्जनीयः ॥ ३५ ॥ पदानि ॥ शप्पेरे, विसर्जनीयः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शप्पेरे खरि परतो विसर्जनीयस्य विसर्जनीयादिशो भवति ॥

35. The visarga is the substitute of visarga, when it is followed by a hard consonant (खर्) which itself is followed by a sibilant (शर्) ॥

The word शप्पेरे is a Bahuvrīhi, meaning that which is followed by शर् ॥ In other words, when a sibilant follows a hard consonant, the preceding visarga remains unchanged. Thus शशाः शूरम्, पुरुषः शूरम्, भजिः प्लाताम्, वासः शौमम्, पुरुषः स्वरः, धनाधनः शौमणधर्मणीनाम् ॥

Though the sutra could have been shortened by saying शप्पेरे न; yet the longer form is used, in order to indicate that the jihvāmūliya and upadhmaniya changes also do not take place, in cases like भजिः प्लातम्, वासः शौमम् ॥

वा शरि ॥ ३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ वा, शरि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ विसर्जनीयस्य विसर्जनीयादिशो वा भवति शरि परे ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ खप्पेरे शरि वा लोपो वक्तव्यः ॥

36. The visarga is optionally the substitute of visarga, when a sibilant follows.

BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 38]

VISARGA SANDHI

1613

As वृक्षः श्वेते or वृक्षश्वेते, वृक्षः श्वेते or वृक्षश्वेते, वृक्षः पण्डे or वृक्षपण्डे, वृक्षः साये or वृक्षसाये ॥ Cf. VIII. 4. 40, 41, for श्व and ष ॥

*Vārt*:—When the sibilant is followed by a hard consonant, there is optionally the elision of the preceding visarga. As वृक्षा स्थातारः or वृक्षाः स्थातारः or वृक्षास्थातारः ॥

कुप्रोः कः प्पी च ॥ ३७ ॥ पदानि ॥ कुप्रोः, कः प्पी, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कर्वपपर्वयोः परतो विसर्जनीयस्य यथासंख्यः कः प् इत्यतावादिशो भवतः ॥

37. × क and × प are optionally substituted for the visarga, when followed by a hard guttural or a hard labial.

Thus वृक्ष × करोति or वृक्षः करोति, वृक्ष × खन्तति or वृक्षः खन्तति, वृक्ष × पचति or वृक्षः पचति, वृक्ष × फन्तति or वृक्षः फन्तति ॥ The क and प in × क and × प are for the sake of pronunciation only. The substitutes are the Jihvamūliya and the Upadhmā-nīya : two lost sibilants belonging to the class of क and प respectively.

When the rule VIII. 3. 34. does not apply, then this sūtra will apply; and will debar that. But VIII. 3. 35. will not be debarred. As वासः क्षीणम्, अङ्कः क्षीणम् ॥ There is no vipratishedha between VIII. 3. 35. and 37, because of the asiddhahood of one with regard to the other. (VIII. 2. 1). In fact, every rule in these three chapters stands by itself, and ignores the *existence* of the subsequent rule. Hence VIII. 3. 35 would not have been debarred by VIII. 3. 37.

To get this, some divide this sūtra into two :—(1) कुप्रोः “The visarga is the substitute of visarga before a guttural or labial which is followed by a sibilant.” (2) × कः प्पीच The jihvāmūliya and upadhmāniya are substitutes of a visarga before a guttural and a labial in every other case.”

सोपदादौ ॥ ३८ ॥ पदानि ॥ सः, अ-पदादौ ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सकार आविशो भवति विसर्जनीयस्य कुप्रोपपवायोः परतः पाशकल्पककाम्येषु ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ सोपवावावित्यनव्ययस्येति वक्तव्यम् ॥ रोरेव काम्ये नाम्यस्येति नियमार्थं वक्तव्यम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ उपध्मानीयस्य कर्वप परतः सकार आविशो भवतीति वक्तव्यम् ॥

38 स is the substitute of a visarga before an affix beginning with a hard guttural or labial.

The word अपवाशे means “when the guttural and labial are not at the beginning of a *word*,” in other words, when they stand at the beginning of an affix. This is possible only before the affixes पाश, कल्प, क, and काम्य ॥ Thus पयस्पाशम् (V. 3. 47); पयस्कल्पम्, यशस्कल्पम्, (V. 3. 67), पयस्कं, यशस्कम्, (V. 3. 70); पयस्काम्यति, यशस्काम्यति (III. 1. 9).

Why do we say ‘when not at the beginning of a word’? Observe पयः कामयते, पयः पिबति ॥

*Vārt*:—Prohibition must be stated, when the visarga belongs to an Indeclinable : as, प्रातः कल्पम्, पुनः कल्पम् ॥

1614

VISARGA SANDHI

[ Bk. VIII. Ch. III. § 40

*Vārt* :—The visarga which comes from ह is only changed to स before काम्य, and not any other visarga. As पयस्काम्यात, and यशस्काम्यति ; but not here, गीःकाम्यति भूःकाम्यति ॥

*Vārt* :—स is the substitute of the Upadhmāniya when followed by a guttural. The root ऊज् (आजवे Tud 20) has Upadhmāniya as its penultimate : though it is written in the Dhātupāṭha as ऊज् the व् only represents the प् of ॠ, and is not to be pronounced. This ॠ is changed to स, when the final ॠ is changed to a guttural, as ऊ स ग, and then this स् is changed to इ, as in अभ्युद्गः, समुद्रः ॥

These words, however, may be derived from the root गम् with the Prepositions अभि, उत्, and सम् उत्, by adding the affix ऊ ॥

इणः पः ॥ ३९ ॥ पदानि ॥ इणः, पः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अपवादाविति वच्यते । इण उत्तरस्य विसर्जनीयस्य प्रकारादेशो भवति कुप्तोपवादयोः परतः पाशकल्पककाम्येषु ॥

39. प् is the substitute of that visarga, which is preceded by इ or ऊ and is followed by an affix beginning with a hard guttural or a labial.

The word अपवादो is understood here also. The affixes meant are the same पाश, कल्प, क, and काम्य ॥ Thus सर्पिपाशम्, यज्ञपाशम्, सर्पिष्कल्पम्, यज्ञष्कल्पम्, सर्पिष्कम्, यज्ञष्कम् ; सर्पिष्काम्यति, यज्ञष्काम्यति ॥

Why do we say 'by an affix'? Observe अग्निः करोति, वायुः करोति, अग्निः पचति, वायुः पचति ॥

The affix should begin with a guttural or a labial. Therefore not here, सर्पिष्ठे, यज्ञष्के ॥

In the succeeding sūtras, the anuvṛtti of स from VIII. 3. 39 and of इणः पः from this, are both current. The visarga will be changed to प् if preceded by इ or ऊ, otherwise it will be स ॥

According to some, this sūtra ordains प् in the room of the स् taught in the preceding sūtra, and not of visarga : and so also in the following sūtras.

नमस्पुरसोगत्योः ॥ ४० ॥ पदानि ॥ नमस्-पुरसोः, गत्योः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नमस्पुरस् इत्येतयोर्गीतिसंज्ञकयो विसर्जनीयस्य सकारादेशो भवति कुप्तोः परतः ॥

40. For the visarga of नमस् and पुरस् there is substituted स् before a hard guttural or a labial, when these words are Gati (I. 4. 67 and 74).

Thus नमस्कर्त्ता, नमस्कर्त्तुम्, नमस्कर्त्तव्यम् ; पुरस्कर्त्ता पुरस्कर्त्तुम्, पुरस्कर्त्तव्यम् ॥

Why do we say 'when they are Gati'? Observe पूकरोति, पुरो करोति, पुरः करोति ॥ Here पुरः is a noun, Accusative Plural of पूः ॥

नमस् is Gati by I. 4. 74, and पुरस् is Gati by I. 4. 67. The anuvṛtti of अपवादो ceases.

BK. VIII. CH. III §. 42 ]

VISARGA SANDHI.

1615

इदु-उपधस्य चाप्रत्ययस्य ॥ ४१ ॥ पदानि ॥ इदु-उदु-उपधस्य, च, अ-प्रत्ययस्य ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ इकारोपधस्य उकारोपधस्य चाप्रत्ययस्य विसर्जनीयस्य प्रकार आवेशो भवति कुप्तैः परतः ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ पुण्यहृद्भोःप्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥

41. प is substituted, before a hard guttural or a labial, for the visarga which is preceded by इ or उ, and is not part of an affix.

This applies to the visarga of निर्, दुर्, बहिर्, आविस्, चतुर् and प्रादुस् ॥
Thus निष्कृतम्, निष्पीतम्, दुष्कृतम्, दुष्पीतम्, बहिस्, बहिष्कृतम्, बहिष्पीतम्, आविस्, आविष्कृतम्, आविष्पीतम्, चतुष्कृतम्, चतुष्कृतम्, चतुष्कृतम्, चतुष्कृतम्, प्रादुष्कृतम्, प्रादुष्पीतम् ॥

Why do we say 'when not belonging to an affix'? Observe अभिः करोति, वायुः करोति ॥ How do you explain मातुः करोति, पितुः करोति? For here in पितुः &c, the स् of the affix is elided by VIII. 2. 24, and the र् of पितुर्+ स् is changed to visarga; this is not the visarga of an affix, and ought to be changed to प ॥

Ans.—The inclusion of the word आतुष्पुत्रः in Kaskādi class (VIII. 3. 48) indicates by implication, that प change does not take place of this visarga in पितुः, मातुः &c: the only exception being आतुः ॥ The reason of this may be that the visarga here does not follow a simple उ, but an ekādeśa उ (VI. 1. 111).

Vārt:—Prohibition must be stated in the case of पुम् and मुहुस्; as पुंस्कामा, मुहुस्कामा ॥

Vārt:—बुद्धिमुतानां पत्यं वक्तव्यम् । The visarga is changed to प even when इ or उ are vriddhied; as नैष्कृतम्, वैष्कृतम् ॥

Vārt:—प्लुतानां तादौ च ॥ The visarga is changed to प even when इ or उ are pluta, and then before dentals as well as gutturals and labials. Thus निष्पतुलम्, दुधपतुलम् (VIII. 2. 86 for pluta). दुधपुतुलम्, वहीधुतुलम् ॥

These last two vārtikas may be dispensed with, because Vriddhi and Pluta are Bahiranga change, and so the visarga will be changed to प in these cases also by the sūtra itself; except so far as त is concerned.

तिरसोन्यतरस्याम् ॥४२ ॥ पदानि ॥ तिरसः, अन्यरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तिरसो विसर्जनीयस्यान्यतरस्यां सकारादेशो भवति कुप्तैः परतः ॥

42. The visarga of the Gati तिरस् is optionally changed to स before a hard guttural or a labial.

Thus तिरस्कर्त्तां, तिरस्कर्त्तुम्, तिरस्कर्त्तव्यम्, or तिरः कर्त्तां, तिरः कर्त्तुम्, तिरः कर्त्तव्यम् ॥
The word गतेः is understood here also. Therefore no option is allowed here, तिरः कृत्वा काण्डं गतः, where तिरस् does not mean 'disappearance'. (I. 4. 72).

द्विस्त्रिधृतुरिति कृत्वोर्थे ॥ ४३ ॥ पदानि ॥ द्विः-त्रिः-चतुर्, इति, कृत्वोर्थे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प इति संबद्धते । द्विस् विस् चतुर् इत्येतेषां कृत्वोर्थे वर्त्तमानानां विसर्जनीयस्य प्रकार आवेशो भवति अन्यतरस्यां कुप्तैः परतः ॥

1616

VISARGA SANDHI.

[BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 43]

43. प is optionally the substitute of the visargas of दिस्, चिस् and चतुर् when they are used as Numeral adverbs, (before a hard guttural and labial).

The affix शुच् (स) is added to the three words dvi, tri and chatur in the sense of kṛtvasuch by V. 4. 18.

As हि: करोति or हिङ्करोति, चि: करोति or विङ्करोति, चतुः करोति or चतुष्करोति, हि: पचति or हिङ्कचति, चि: पचति or विङ्कचति, चतुः पचति or चतुष्कचति ॥

Why do we say 'when used in the sense of kṛtvasuch or Numeral adverbs'? Observe चतुष्कपालम्, चतुष्कण्टकम्, where प is compulsory by VIII. 3. 41. चतुष्कपालेषु संस्कृतः (IV. 2. 16 and IV. 1. 88). This sūtra is an example of ubhayatra-vibhāshā. With regard to चतुष्क the visarga is a non-affix visarga, and hence VIII. 3. 41, would have made प compulsory, this makes it optional. With regard to दिस् and चिस् the visarga is that of an affix (सुच् or स् V. 4. 18), and hence VIII. 3. 41, would not have applied. Thus with regard to चतुष्क it is a Prāpta-vibhāshā, and with regard to दिस् and चिस् it is an Aprāpta-vibhāshā.

Why have we used the words 'dvis, tris and chatur'? Objector's answer: so that the rule may not apply to पंचकृत्वः करोति, the visarga of kṛtvasuch (V. 4. 17) is not changed to प ॥

The anuvṛtti of ङ and ङ is understood here from VIII. 3. 41: so that the visarga must be preceded by ङ and ङ for the application of this rule. In पञ्चकृत्वः the visarga is preceded by अ, and so there is no applicability of this rule.

In fact, by reading the anuvṛtti of इदुपधा into this sūtra, and qualifying the visarga by the further epithet of 'belonging to a word that has the sense of kṛtvasuch'; we may dispense with the words हिङ्कश्चतुरिति from the sūtra. The simple sūtra कृत्वोर्थे would have been enough. For there are no other Numerals that have a penultimate ङ or ङ, except these three. The chief objection to this view is, that in चतुष्क the visarga is not the affix शुच्, but a portion of the word (See V. 4. 18): so the rule would not apply to chatur, if this word were not expressly mentioned.

The various objections and their solutions are given in the following verses.

कृत्वसुचर्थे पलं ब्रवीति कस्माचतुष्कपालं मा
पलं विनापया भुवतु सिद्धं तच्च पूर्वेण ॥
सिद्धे ह्यर्थे विधत्ते चतुष्क पलं यद्यापि कृत्वोर्थे ॥
कुत्वे कृत्वोर्थेये रेफस्य विसर्जनीयो हि ॥
एवं सति लिप्तानीं हिङ्कश्चतुरित्यनेन किं कार्यम् ॥
अन्त्यो हि नेदुपधः कृत्वोर्थः कश्चिदव्यस्ति ॥
अक्रियमाणे महणे विसर्जनीयस्तदा विशेष्येत ॥

BK. VIII. CH. III. § 43 ]

VISARGA SANDHI.

1617

चतुरो न सिध्याति तथा रेफस्य विसर्जनीयो हि ॥
सस्मिंस्तु क्रियामाणे युक्तं चतुरो विशेषणं भवति ॥

प्रकृतं पत् तदन्तं तस्यापि विशेषणं न्याय्यम् ॥

*Kārikā* :—कृत्वसुचर्य पत् ब्वीतिं कस्मात्? Why does the author teach पत् when these words have the sense of Numeral-adverbs? In other words, why the word कृत्वोयें is used at all in the sūtra? There is no necessity of using it at all, because दिस्, विस् are clearly adverbs as they are formed by the affix सुच् (V. 4. 18) and चतुर being read in their company will also denote the *adverb* chatur, in which सुच् has been elided (V. 4. 18). So that all these three words are सुच्-formed, and all सुच्-formed words have the sense of Kṛtvasuch. One answer to this is that the rule of साहचर्य does not always hold good, as in दीधीवैदिकम् (I. 1.6), the words दीधी and वैदी are verbs, while इद is an augment. Though therefore दिस् and विस् are kṛtvortha words, yet चतुर need not be so: and may be a simple Numeral. *Ans.* चतुक्मालि मा पत् विभाषया भूत ॥ The word कृत्वोऽयें is employed to indicate that there should be no optional पत् in चतुक्मालि ॥ The पत् here is compulsory by VIII. 3. 41. *Q.* नतु सिद्धं तत्र पूर्वेण ॥ Well this would be valid by the previous sūtra (VIII. 3. 41). That is, let in चतुक्मालि also there be optional पत्, as चतुक्मालि and चतुक्मालि ॥ Now rule VIII. 3. 41 will apply to चतुक्मालि and will change this visarga to प, so that with regard to चतुक्मालि, we shall have *always* प ॥ *Ans.* सिद्धं ह्ययं विधत्ते चतुरः पत् यद्यपि कृत्वोयें, लुप्ते कृत्वोयें रेफस्य विसर्जनीयो हि ॥ If VIII. 3. 41 be considered as applying here (siddha), then when the affix सुच् is elided after चतुर, and the र is changed to visarga, then the adverb चतुः also ends with a non-affix visarga, and will come under the compulsory पत् rule of VIII. 3. 41; for though we may have optionally two forms as चतुः करोति and चतुक्मोति, by the present sūtra, yet in the former the visarga would be changed to प by VIII. 3. 41. Hence the necessity of employing the word कृत्वोऽयें ॥ *Q.* But we say that the र in the adverb चतुर is that of सुच्, thus चतुर+स=चतुर+र (VIII. 2. 66)=चतुर+र (the first र is elided by VIII. 3. 14)=चतुर; and that this र when changed to visarga, will be an affix-visarga and so VIII. 3. 41 will not apply to the *adverb* चतुर ॥ *Ans.* No. For उ would require to be lengthened by VI. 3. 111. and the form would be चतुर ॥

एवं सति विद्वानां हिङ्गिअतुरित्यनेन किं कार्यम् ॥ If this be so, then what is the purpose served by using the words दिस् विअतुरिति in the aphorism? The simple sūtra कृत्वोऽयें would have been enough. Because (अन्योहि नेदुरुपः कृत्वोयें कदिचरव्यस्ति) there are no other numeral adverbs than these three which have a penultimate र or उ ॥

अक्रियामाणे ग्रहणे विसर्जनीयस्तथा विशेष्येत ॥ If we do not use the words dvis, tris, chaturiti in the sūtra, then the word kṛtvorthe would qualify the word visarga, and the sūtra would mean “the visarga of an affix which has the sense of kṛtvasuch is changed optionally to प” ॥ The result of this will be

1618

VISARGA SANDHI.

[BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 44]

that ( चतुरो न सिध्यति तथारकस्य विसर्जनधिः ) it will not apply to चतुः where the visarga is that of र् and not of the affix सुच् ॥

Therefore by using dvis &c, the word कुलोर्धे would qualify चतुर् (तस्मिन् तु क्रियामणे युक्तं चतुरो विशेषणं भवति) ॥

Ans.—प्रकृतं परं तदन्तं तस्यापि, विशेषणं नान्यम् ॥ Though we may not use dvis &c, the word kṛtvortha will not qualify visarga, but will qualify the word पर् whose context runs here; and the rule of तदन्त will apply; so that the sūtra कुलोर्धे will mean, परस्य कुलोर्धे वर्तमानस्य यो विसर्जनीयः, तस्य सकारः प्रकारो व ॥ “The visarga of that word which is employed in the sense of a Numeral adverb, is optionally changed to स् or प् before a guttural or a labial, provided that such visarga is preceded by इ or उ”.

The above is the opinion of Patanjali, who considers the words dvis &c, as redundant. The Kāśikā however controverts this opinion. According to him, if these words were not used in the sūtra, then the mere sūtra कुलोर्धे would be insufficient for the visarga of चतुः though used as an adverb, the पर् will be compulsory by VIII.3.41; for the present sūtra will be considered as asiddha or non-existent for the purposes of VIII. 3. 41, (See VIII. 2. 1). But this however may be answered by saying that the rule of पूर्ववर्तिमन्त्रक applies in these chapters, with this modification, one subject-matter is considered as asiddha with regard to another subject-matter gone before; but one aphorism is not considered asiddha with regard to a previous aphorism, when belonging to the same subject matter. (प्रकरणं प्रकरणमसिद्धं न योगे योगः) ॥ Therefore the present sūtra VIII. 3. 43, would not be considered asiddha with regard to VIII. 3. 41. Or the present sūtra may be considered as an apavāda to VIII. 3. 41: and an apavāda is never asiddha with regard to an utsarga.

इसुसोः सामर्थ्ये ॥ ४४ ॥ पदानि ॥ इस्-उसोः, सामर्थ्ये ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इस् उस् इलेतयोर्विसर्जनीयस्यान्यतरस्यां प्रकारादेशो भवति सामर्थ्ये कुत्तोः परतः ॥

44. For the visarga of words ending in इस् and उस्, before a hard guttural or labial, there is optionally substituted प्, when the two words stand in correlation with one another.

The प् is understood here. Thus सर्पिकरोति or सर्पिः करोति, यजुः करोति or यजुःकरोति ॥

Why do we say ‘when the two words are correlated’? Observe तिष्ठतु सर्पिः, पिब स्वप्नकम्, where सर्पिः is not in construction with पिब, but with तिष्ठतु ॥

The word सामर्थ्ये here means व्यपेक्षा or mutual relation of two words; and not “having the same meaning”, or it may mean both. In fact सामर्थ्ये is equivalent to आकाङ्क्षा i. e. the syntactical want of another word to complete the sense. It does not here mean ‘compound’. For it being a परविधिः the word समर्थः is

BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 46 ] VISARGA SANDHI.

1619

understood here (समर्थः प्रविधिः II. I. I.). The employment of the word सामर्थ्य here indicates that it is a different samarthya from that of II. I. I. It does not denote एकार्थीभावः or ऐकार्थ्यं which is the samarthya of compounds where two or more words denote one object. The samarthya here means vyapekshā, which is thus defined मानभूतयोः, पदार्थयोः यौ शब्दौ वर्तते, तयो यौ योगः "the syntactical union of two words expressing two different ideas".

नित्यं समासे अनुत्तरपदस्थस्य ॥ ४५ ॥ पदानि ॥ नित्यम, समासे, अनुत्तरपदस्थस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इदुसोरिति वर्तते । समासविषये इदुसोर्विसर्जनीयस्य अनुत्तरपदस्थस्य नित्यं बलं भवति कृष्टोः परतः ॥

45. The visarga of an इस or उस-ending word, which is not preceded by any other word, is invariably changed to प in a compound, when followed by a hard gut-tural or labial.

The words इस and उस are understood here. Thus सर्पिकुण्डिका, धनुष्कपालम्, सर्पिष्पानम्, धनुष्कलम् ॥

Why do we say when it is not preceded by another word? Observe परमसर्पिः कुण्डिका, परमधनुः कपालम् ॥ The option even of the last sutra does not apply to these examples.

Q.—The word सर्पिस is derived from the root सुप् by adding the Uṇādi affix इति (Uṇ II. 109), and यजु. by the Uṇādi affix इति (Uṇ II. 117), therefore on the maxim प्रत्ययमहणे &c, the word इदुसोः would denote the mere forms सर्पिस and यजु. and not forms like परमसर्पिस &c. then what is the necessity of employing the word अनुत्तरपदस्थस्य in the sutra?

The very employment of the word anuttara-pada-sthasya in this sutra, is an indicator (jñāpaka), that the restriction of the following maxim does not apply with regard to the affixes इस and उसः प्रत्ययमहणे यस्मात् स विहितं स्तदादे-स्तदन्तस्य महणम् "an affix denotes, whenever it is employed in Grammar, a word-form which begins with that to which that affix has been added and ends with the affix itself". This maxim not applying, we have परमसर्पिकरोति or परमसर्पिः करोति by the previous sutra VIII. 3. 44.

Q.—Why is not there option in the case of compounds also by the previous sutra?

Ans :—Because the word सामर्थ्य there means व्यपेक्षा, and therefore does not apply to compounds.

अतः कृकमिकंसकुम्भपात्रकुशाकर्णीष्वनव्ययस्य ॥ ४६ ॥ पदानि ॥ अतः, कृकमि-कंस-कुम्भ-पात्र-कुशा-कर्णीषु, अन्-अव्ययस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अकारादुत्तरस्य अनव्ययविसर्जनीयस्य समासेऽनुत्तरपदस्थस्य नित्यं सकारोदशो भवति कृकमि कंस कुम्भ पात्र कुशा कर्णी इत्येतेपुरतः ॥

17

1620

VISARGA SANDHI. [BK. VIII. CH. III. § 47]

46. For the visarga of a word ending in अस, with the exception of an Indeclinable, स is substituted in a compound, when a form of क् and कम, or the words कंस कुम्म, पात्र, कुशा and कर्णी follow, and the first word is not preceded by another word.

Thus क्:—अयस्कारः, पयस्कारः (III. 2. 1) कम्:—अयस्कामः, पयस्कामः, कंस:—अयस्कंसः, पयस्कंसः, कुम्मः, अयस्कुम्मः पयस्कुम्मः ॥ So also अयस्कुम्मी पयस्कुम्मी, on the maxim प्रातिपदिकमहणे लिङ्गविशिष्टस्यापि महणे भवति ॥ पात्र:—अयस्काचम्, पयस्काचम्, अयस्काची, पयस्काची ॥ कुशा:—अयस्कुशा, पयस्कुशा ॥ कर्णी:—अयस्कर्णी, पयस्कर्णी ॥ The form शुनस्कर्णः belongs to Kaskādi class (VIII. 3. 48).

Why do we say अतः “a visarga preceded by short अ, or the visarga of the word ending in अ”? See गीःकारः, धृःकारः ॥ Why do we say ‘preceded by short अ’? Observe भाःकरणम् ॥ The form भास्करः belongs to Kaskādi class (VIII. 3. 48). See also III. 2. 2.

Why do we say “with the exception of an Indeclinable”? Observe दवःकारः, पुनःकारः ॥

The word समासे is understood here also. Therefore not here; यशः करोति पयः करोति, यशोः कामयते ॥

The word अनुत्तरपदस्थस्य is also to be read in this. Therefore not here, परमपयः कारः, परमपयः कामः ॥

Q. The word कंस need not have been taken, because it is a form of the root कम्, since it is derived from कम् by adding the Uṇādi affix स (III. 62 Uṇ)?

Ans.—The employment of कंस indicates the existence of the following maxim:—उणादयोऽव्युत्पन्नानि प्रातिपदिकानि “Words which end with उण् &c. are crude-forms that do not undergo or cause such operations as would depend on their etymological formation.”

अधः शिरसी पदे ॥४७॥ पदानि ॥ अधः-शिरसी, पदे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अधम् शिरस् इत्यतयोर्विसर्जनीयस्य समासेऽनुत्तरपदस्थस्य सकार आवेशो भवति पदशब्दे परतः ॥

47. For the visarga of अधम् or शिरस् when not preceded by another word, and followed by the word पद in composition with it, there is substituted स् ॥

Thus अधस्पदम्, शिरस्पदम् ॥ अधस्पदी, शिरस्पदी ॥

The word समासे is understood in this, therefore not here अधः पदम् ॥

The word अनुत्तरपदस्थस्य is also understood here. Therefore not in the following परमशिरः पदम् ॥

The word अधस्पदम् is a compound formed under Mayūravyansakādi class.

BK. VIII. CH. III §. 49] VISARGA SANDHI.

1621

कस्कादिषु च ॥ ४८ ॥ पदानि ॥ कस्कादिषु, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कस्क इत्येवमावपि च विसर्जनीयस्य सकारः पकारो वा यथायोगमावेशो भवति कुर्वीः परतः ॥

48. स or ष is substituted for the visarga, before a hard guttural and labial in the words कस्क and the rest.

This is an Apavāda to Sūtra VIII. 3. 37. ष is substituted after ष or ष, and ष everywhere else. Thus कस्कः, 2. कौतस्कृतः (with अणु of कुत आगतः), 3. आतुष्पुत्रः (VI. 3. 23) 4. शुनस्करणः (VI. 3. 21) 5. सद्यस्कालः, 6. सद्यस्की (from की 'to buy' with the affix बिष्वप्, because it belongs to Sampadādi class.) 7. साद्यस्कः (from सद्यस्की in the sense of तन्नभेवः क्तुः), 8. कस्कान् (the ष is by VIII. 3. 12), 9. सर्पिष्कुण्डिका, 10. चतुष्कपालम्, 11. धनुष्कपालम् 12. बहिष्कुलम्, 13. यजुष्पावम् ॥ "The words 9 to 13 are exceptions to VIII. 3. 45, so that there might be ष, even when सर्पिस् &c are preceded by another word. Thus परमसर्पिष्कुण्डिका ॥ The counter-example then to VIII. 3. 45 will be परमसर्पिः फलम् ॥" This is the opinion of the Pārāyaṇikās. But in the Mahābhāshya, the counter-example under VIII. 3. 45 is परमसर्पिः कुण्डिका ॥ Another reason why these words are listed here, is that ष change will take place, even where there is no correlation or vyapekshā. As तिष्ठतु सर्पिष्कुण्डिकां आनय ॥ So also when there is correlation, as इदे सर्पिष्कुण्डिकायाः ॥ Here सर्पिस् is an incomplete word. The ष change, will take place even where there is no compounding. Where there is no compounding, and there is complete want of correlation, even there the ष will invariably come. And where there is correlation, but no compounding there the ष would have been optional by VIII. 3. 44, but it becomes invariable here, on account of these words being so listed. Thus we have these cases : (1) Without correlation, as तिष्ठतु सर्पिष्कुण्डिकामानय ॥ (2) Where there is correlation, as इदे सर्पिष्कुण्डिकायाः ॥ (3) Where there is composition, as सर्पिष्कुण्डिका ॥ (4) Where there is no composition and no correlation even, as, in example (1). (5) Where there is correlation but no compounding as in example (2). In all these cases there is ष invariably in case of these words. 14. अयस्काण्डः, 15. मेवस्पिण्डः ॥ अविहितलक्षण उपचारः कस्कादिषु द्रष्टव्यः ।

Every change of visarga to स or ष, must be referred to Kaskādi class, if not governed by any other rule. Thus this is an Akṛtigaṇa. Upachāra is the name of स and ष which replace the visarga.

The Pārāyaṇa is of two sorts, Dhātu-Par, and Nāma-Par. Those who devote themselves in committing to memory and reciting these are Pārāyaṇikas.

छन्दसि वा प्राग्नेडितयोः ॥ ४९ ॥ पदानि ॥ छन्दसि, वा, अ-प्र-आग्नेडितयोः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विषये विसर्जनीयस्य वा सकारादेशो भवति कुर्वीः परतः प्रशब्दे आग्नेडितं वर्जयित्वा ॥

49. स may optionally be substituted for the

1622

VISARGA SANDHI.

[BK. VIII. CH. III. § 51]

visarga before a hard guttural and labial, in the Chhandas; but neither before प्र, nor before a doubled word.

Thus अयः पाचम्, or अयस्वाचम् ॥ This is an example of non-compounds. In compounds, the स change is compulsory by VIII. 3. 46: because the option of the present sutra is asiddha there, and it finds its scope in cases other than compounds. If the maxim प्रकरण प्रकरणसिद्धे न योगे योगः be applied, then the two sutras VIII. 3. 46 and VIII. 3. 49 belong to the same प्रकरण and one is not asiddha with regard to the other. Then we could give examples of compounds also under this sutra: but then such compounds will also be governed by VIII. 3. 46, and so the स would be compulsory.

विश्वतस्याचम्, or विश्वतः पाचम्, here the word विश्वतः is an Indeclinable and hence the rule VIII. 3. 46, does not apply to it. उरु णः कारः or उरु णः स्कारः ॥ Here नः is substituted for असदः, and then the न is changed to ण by VIII. 4. 27. The word कारः is a घञ् formed word.

Why do we say 'not before प्र and a doubled word'? Observe अग्निः प्र विद्वान् (Av. V. 26. 1), पुरुषः पुरुषः परि ॥

In सूर्यदिग्वीरिकेशः पुरस्तात् (Rig. X. 139. 1), स नः पावकः (Rig. I. 12. 10), the स change has not taken place, as all rules are optional in the Vedas.

कःकरत्करतिकृधिकृतेष्वनदितेः ॥ ५० ॥ पदानि ॥ कःकरत्-करति-कृधि-कृतेषु, अन्-अदितेः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कःकरत्-करति-कृधि-कृत इच्यतेषु परतः अनदितेविसर्जनीयस्य सकारविदो भवति छन्दसि विधेय ॥

50. The visarga is changed to स in the Chhandas, before कः, करत्, करतिं, कृधि and कृतः but not so the visarga of अदितिः ॥

Thus विश्वतस्कः ॥ कः is the Aorist of कृ, the ऋ has been elided by II. 4. 80: the ऋ of कृ is gunated before the affix तिप्, thus we have कर्तृ, the न is elided by VI. 1. 68; and the augment अद is not added by VI. 4. 75. Similarly विश्वतस्करत् ॥ Here also कर्तृ is the Aorist of कृ, with अद् by III. 1. 59. पयस्करति, here करति is the लद् of कृ; शप् is added instead of अ, as a Vedic anomaly. उरणस्कृधि, here कृधि is the Imperative of कृ, the सि is changed to हि, the vikaraṇa is elided, and हि changed to धि by VI. 4. 102. See VIII. 4. 27, for the change of न to ण ॥ सवस्कृतम्, here कृतम् is Past Participle of कृ ॥

Why do we say 'but not of अदितिः'? Observe यथा नो अदितिः कर्तृ (Rig. I. 43. 2).

पञ्चम्याः परावध्यर्थे ॥ ५१ ॥ पदानि ॥ पञ्चम्याः, परौ, अध्यर्थे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसिद्धेव । पञ्चमीविसर्जनीयस्य सकारविदो भवति परौ परतः अध्यर्थे ॥

BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 55 ] VISARGA SANDHI.

1623

51. The visarga of the Ablative case is changed to स् before परि meaning 'over'.

The word Chhandas is understood here also. Thus दिवस्परि प्रथंन जज्ञे (Rig X. 45. 1) अग्निहिंसवतस्परि ॥ दिवस्परि, महस्परि ॥

Why do we say 'of the Ablative'? Observe आहिरिव भोगैः पर्येति बाहुम् ॥ Why do we say 'before परि'? See एभ्येवा एतल्लोकेभ्यः प्रजापतिः समैरयन् ॥ Why do we say 'when परि means 'over'? See दिवः पृथिव्याः प्रयोज उद्भूतम् (Rig. VI. 47. 27). Here परि has the sense of 'on all sides'.

पातौ च बहुलम् ॥ ५२ ॥ पदानि ॥ पातौ, च बहुलम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पातौ च धातौ परतः पञ्चमीविसर्जनीयस्य बहुलं सकार आदिशो भवति छन्दसि विधेय ॥

52. स may diversely be substituted for the visarga of the Ablative before the verb पातु in the Chhandas.

Thus दिवस्पातु, राजस्पातु ॥ Sometimes, the change does not take place, as परिषदः पात ॥

पञ्च्याःपतिपुत्रपृष्ठपारपदपयस्पोषेषु ॥ ५३ ॥ पदानि ॥ पञ्च्याःपति-पुत्र-पृष्ठ-पार-पद पयस्-पोषेषु ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ षष्ठीविसर्जनीयस्यसकारादेशो भवति पति पुत्र पृष्ठ पार पदपयस् पोष इत्येतेषु परतः छन्दसि विधेय ॥

53. For the visarga of the Genitive, there is substituted स् in the Vedas, before पति, पुत्र, पृष्ठ, पार, पद, पयस्, and पोष ॥

Thus वाचस्पति विद्वक्कर्माणमुतये, (Rig. x. 81. 7), दिवस्पुत्राय सूर्याय, दिवस्पुत्रे धावमानं सुपर्णम्, अगन्म, तमसस्पारम्, इडस्पदे समिध्यसे, सूर्यं चक्षु दिवस्पयः, रायस्पोषं यजमानेषु धत्तम् ॥

Why do we say 'after a genitive case'? See मतुः पुत्रेभ्यो हायं व्यभजत् ॥

इडाया वा ॥ ५४ ॥ पदानि ॥ इडायाः, वा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इडायाः षष्ठीविसर्जनीयस्य वा सकार आदेशो भवति पञ्चादिषु परतदण्डसि विधेय ॥

54. स is optionally substituted for the visarga of इडायाः, before पति &c, (VIII. 3. 53.) in the Chhandas.

Thus इडायाः पतिः or इडायास्पतिः इडायास्पुत्रः । इडायाः पुत्रः । इडायास्पृथम् । इडायाः पृष्ठम् । इडाया स्पारम्, इडायाः पारम् । इडायास्पदम् । इडायाः पदम् । इडायास्पयः । इडायाः पयः । इडायाः पोषम् । इडायास्पोषम् ॥

अपदान्तस्य मूर्द्धन्यः ॥ ५५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अ-पदान्तस्य, मूर्द्धन्यः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अपदान्तस्येति मूर्द्धन्य इति चैतदधिकृतं वेदितव्यम् । आपादपरिसमाप्तेः ॥

55. Upto the end of the Pāda, is throughout to be supplied the following: 'A cerebral letter is substituted always in the room of ———, when this letter does not stand at the end of a word'.

1624

SANDHI.

[ Bk. VIII. Ch. III. § 57

Here ceases the Padādhikāra which commenced with VIII. 1. 16. The two words अपशान्तस्य 'not final in a pada', and मूर्धन्यः 'cerebral' exert a governing influence on all sūtras upto the end of this chapter. Thus VIII. 3. 59, teaches "of an affix and a substitute". The whole of the present sūtra should be read there to complete the sense: i. e. "a cerebral sound is substituted always in the room of the स of an affix and of the स which is a substitute, when it does not stand at the end of a word". Thus सिधेव, सुष्पाप, आग्रुपु, वायुपु ॥

Why do we say 'not final'? See अभिस्तव, वायुस्तव ॥ Though the anuvṛtti of व was understood here, yet the employment of the word 'cerebral' is for the sake of व; as अकृतव, चकृते (VIII. 3. 78).

सहेः सादः सः ॥ ५६ ॥ पदानि ॥ सहेः, सादः, सः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सहेद्वीतोः साङ्कुपस्य यः सकारस्तस्य मूर्धन्य आविशो भवति ॥

56. व is substituted for the स in साह, when this occurs in the form of साद (साद) ॥

Thus जलापाद, तुरापाद, पूतनापाद ॥ साद is derived from सह by the affix ण्व (III. 2. 63), there is vriddhi of the penultimate, the व is changed to व (VIII. 2. 31), and the upapada is lengthened (VI. 3. 137).

सादः सः would have been enough, for there is no other form साद except this derived from सह; why then the word सहः is used in the sūtra? There is another form साद not derived from सह ॥ Thus सह ङेन वर्तते = सडः, सडस्य अपश् = साडिः ॥ He in whose name there is the letter ङ is called सडः; as वड ॥

Why do we say 'in the form of साद'? The rule will not apply when the form is साह, as जलासाहम्, तुरासाहम् ॥ Why do we say सः "for the स"? So that the आ of साद may not be changed to cerebral: the ङ is already cerebral.

इण्कोः ॥ ५७ ॥ पदानि ॥ इण् कोः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इण्कोः स्थितवधिकृतं वैविध्यम् । इत उत्तरं यदृश्यामः इणः कवर्गोच्येवं तद्वैतितव्यम् ।

57. From this, upto the end of the chapter, should be supplied in every sūtra, the following:—"when a vowel (with the exception of अ or आ), or a र or a guttural precedes".

The word इण् is a pratyāhāra formed with the second ण् of लण् ॥ It includes all vowels and semivowels except अ and आ ॥ Of the semi-vowels र is only efficient: so that only is taken in the translation. कु means the letters of the क class. Thus इण्कोः is supplied in VIII. 3. 59, to complete the sense. Thus सिधेव, सुष्पाप, अभ्रिपु, वायुपु, कर्तृपु, हर्तृपु, गीर्पु, पूर्पु, वाशु, स्वशु ॥

Why do we say "when preceded by इण् or कु"? Observe वास्त्यति, असौ ॥ Here the affix स of स्वाति, and the substitute स in असौ (VII. 2. 106) are not changed to व ॥

BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 59]

५ CHANGE.

1625

तुम्बिसर्जनीयशब्द्यवायेपि ॥ ५८ ॥ पदानि ॥ तुम्, विसर्जनीय-शब्द्यवाये, अपि ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ तुम्ब्यवायेपि विसर्जनीयव्यवायेपि शब्द्यवायेपि इण्कोहस्तस्य सकारस्य मूर्धन्यदेशो भवति ॥

58. The substitution of प् for स् takes place then also, when the augment न् (तुम्), the visarjanīya or a sibilant occurs between the said इण् and कु letters or the स् ॥

The word व्यवाय 'separation, intervention' applies to every one of the words तुम्, &c. Thus (1) when तुम् intervenes, as सर्पिषि, यज्ञिषि, हर्षिषि (VII. 1. 72, VI. 4. 10). (2) When a visarjanīya intervenes, as सर्पिषु, यज्ञषु, हर्षिषु (VIII. 3. 36) (3) When a Sibilant intervenes, as सर्पिषु, यज्ञषु हर्षिषु ॥

The पत् takes place, when तुम् &c intervene singly and not when they intervene collectively. Therefore not here, निस्से, निस्से from the root निस् 'to kiss.' Here there is the intervention of two, namely, तुम् and स् (III. 4. 91).

The word इण्कोः is in the Ablative case, and it required that the स् should follow immediately after it. Hence the necessity of the present sūtra for the intervention of certain letters.

आदेशप्रत्यययोः ॥ ५९ ॥ पदानि ॥ आदेश, प्रत्यययोः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ आदेशो यः सकारः प्रत्ययस्य च यः सकार इण्कोहस्तस्य मूर्धन्यो भवति ॥

59. प् is substituted for that स् which is a substitute (of the प् of a root in Dhātupāṭha by VI. 1. 64), or which is (the portion of) an affix, under the above mentioned conditions (VIII. 3. 57, 58), of being preceded by an इण् vowel or a guttural.

The word cerebral is understood here from VIII. 3. 55, as well as स् ॥
The sūtra ādeśa-pratyayoḥ is in the Genitive case. The force of the Genitive however is different in the word ādeśa, from what it is in pratyaya. In the first it is samānādhikaraṇa-shasthī, in the latter avayava-yogāshasthī. That is that स् which is an ādeśa, and that स् which belongs to an affix. If we took it as avayavayogā shasthī in both places, then the sūtra would mean "of that स् which is a portion of a substitute, or of an affix," and there would arise the following anomaly. In doubling a word by VIII. 1. 1, one view is that two are substituted in the room of one (See VIII. 1. 1). Thus विसंबिसं, मुसलंगुसलं ॥ Here the स् in these words, is a portion of a substitute, and would be changed to प्, if we translate the sūtra as above.

If we take the other view, and translate the sūtra as "of that स् which is a substitute or an affix", we land on the following anomaly. We must have forms like कारस्थति and हरिस्थति, and not the correct forms करिष्यति, हरिष्यति;

1626

प CHANGE.

[ Bk. VIII. Ch. III. §. 60

for here स is not an affix, but a *portion* of an affix. In fact, with regard to affixes, the sūtra would be confined to those affixes only which consist of a single स, such as सिप् in the Vedic subjunctive केद् ॥ That this is the proper interpretation of the sūtra is indicated by the sūtra VIII. 3. 60, (the next aphorism). The substitute पस् is taken in this sūtra. If therefore, the force of Genitive in आवेशस्य was=आवेशस्य यः सकारः and not=आवेशः यः सकारः, then there would have been no necessity of including the substitute पस् in the sūtra, for then the present sūtra would have covered the case of पस् also. Similarly, if the force of the Genitive in प्रत्ययस्य was=प्रत्ययः यः सकारः, and not=प्रत्ययस्य यः सकारः; then there would have been no necessity of excluding the affix सात् (V. 4. 52) from the operation of the present rule by VIII. 3. 111, because it is not an affix consisting of a single letter स् ॥

Having surmised this, we shall now give illustrations. First of that स् which is a substitute. It can only be the स् which replaces the प् of a root in Dhātupātha. Thus सिपेव, सुष्पाप ॥ Of an affix, we have अम्रिपु, वायुपु, कर्तृपु, हर्तृपु; वक्षत् in इन्द्रो मा वक्षत्; and वक्षत् in स देवान् वक्षत् ॥

Q.—In the case of वक्षत् and वक्षत्, the स् is not the *portion* of an affix, but the *whole* affix itself: the present sūtra should therefore not apply to this स् ॥

Ans.—Here we apply the maxim व्यपदेशिवद् एकस्मिन् ॥

These words (वक्षत् and वक्षत्) are from the roots वच् and यज्, in केद् with सिप्, the इ is elided by III. 4. 97, the augment अद् (III. 4. 94), the affix सिप् by III. 1. 34; the च् of वच् is changed to a guttural, and the ज् of यज् to प् and then to a guttural.

The Uṇādi word अक्षर (अश्+सर Uṇ III. 70) complies with this rule, but not so the word क्सर (Uṇ III. 73) formed with the same affix सर ॥

शासिवसिधसीनांच ॥६०॥ पदानि ॥ शासि-वासि- घसीनाम्, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शासि वसि घसि इयेतेषां च इण्कोहस्तस्य सकारस्य मूर्ध्न्यो भवति ॥

60. प् is substituted for the स् of शास्, वस् and घस् when it is preceded by an इण् vowel or a guttural.

Thus अन्वशिपत्, अन्वशिपताम्, अन्वशिपत्, the Aorist of शास्; the णि is replaced by अद् (III. 1. 56), and the आ changed to इ by VI. 4. 34. So also शिह्, शिह्वान् ॥ From वस् we have उचितः, उचितवान्, उचित्वा ॥ The Samprasāraṇa takes place by VI. 1. 15 as it belongs to yajādi class. From पस् we have जक्षत्, जक्षः in the Perfect. पस् is the substitute of अद् (II. 4. 40), the penultimate अ is elided by VI. 4. 98. So also अक्षत् in अक्षतमीमवन्त पितरः (Rig. I. 82. 2). This is the Aorist form of अद्, the पस् is substituted for अद् (II. 4. 37): the Aorist sign is elided by II. 4. 80.

BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 61]

षष्ठ RULE.

1627

This sūtra is made to cover cases not governed by the last sūtra, namely, where the स् is not an ādeśa. Though the स् in षस् is the स् of a substitute, yet it is not governed by the preceding aphorism, because the word आविश्वस्य there means 'the स् which is a substitute'. Here स् is not a substitute, but a portion of a substitute. The non-substitute षस् is not to be taken here: as it seldom occurs.

The word इण्कोः is understood here also. Therefore the rule would not apply to शास्ति, वसति and जघास ॥

स्तौतिण्योरेव पण्यभ्यासात् ॥ ६१ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्तौति-ण्योः, एव, पाणि, अभ्यासात् ॥

वृत्ति ॥ स्तोत्पर्यन्तानां च षण्मूते सति परतः अभ्यासादिष उत्तरस्य आविश्वसकारस्य मूढैर्न्यवेशो भवति ॥

61. प् is substituted for स after इ or उ in the reduplication of a Desiderative, if the स of सन् is changed to प्; but only in स्तु and in Causative of roots which in Dhātupāṭha begin with a प् ॥

This rule is confined to the Desideratives of स्तु and of स् beginning roots in the Causative, provided that the Desiderative sign स् is changed to प् ॥ The rule applies to the स् of the substitute, and not to the affix स् as there can be no such स् after a reduplicate syllable. Therefore स् means that स which replaces the प् of the roots.

Thus from स्तु we have तुष्टुपति ॥ Here the स of सन् is changed to प् by the last sūtra, and therefore so also after the reduplicate उ, the स of स्तु is changed to प् ॥

Of the Causatives of roots beginning with प् in Dhātupāṭha, we have सिपेवथिपति, सिपिञ्जथिपति, छुव्वापथिपति ॥ In this last, the प् is changed to उ by VII. 4. 67.

Though this प् change would have taken place by the previous sūtra (VIII. 3. 59), yet the separate enunciation of this rule indicates that this is a niyama aphorism—the प् change takes place only in these cases of स्तु and Causatives of Desideratives under the conditions mentioned in this sūtra, and no where else. Thus सिपिञ्जति from the root पिच् क्षरणे (Tud. 140). This is a root, which is exhibited in the Dhātupāṭha with a प्, therefore the form ought to have been सिपिञ्जति by VIII. 3. 59, but it is not so, because of the niyama of the present sūtra. So also छुष्टुपते from पृष्ट पाणिप्रसवे (Div. 24): and छुष्टुपति from प् प्रेरणे (Tud 115).

If this is a niyama rule by the very fact of its separate enunciation, what is then the necessity of using the word एव in the aphorism? Ans. इहतो-उपधारणायैष्; so that, the sūtra may mean "if स्तु and Causatives only, when षण् follows"? and not "if स्तु and Causatives when षण् only follows". In the

18

1628

षष्ठ RULE.

[ Bk. VIII. Ch. III. §. 61

latter view, we could not get the form तुदाब ; and the rule would have applied to सिसिअति also.

Why do we say “in the Desiderative ष”? So that the niyama may not be any where else. Had षणि not been used in the sūtra, the restriction would have been with regard to every affix, and the sūtra would have meant “if there is occasion of षष्ठ change after a reduplicate, it should take place only in the case of स्तु and the Causatives”. Therefore ष change would not have taken place in सिषेच, as it is not a Causative.

Q.—कौ विनतेऽनुरोधः? Why have we used the word षण् with ष, and not the word सन्? That is, what compulsion was there to exhibit the Desiderative affix सन्, in this changed form? The word विनत is the name given in the Prāti-sākhyas to ष and ण change.

Ans.—So that the restrictive rule may not apply to the अनिनत form of सन् ॥ As सुपुसति ॥ The सन् is here किन्तु by I. 2. 8, and there is vocalisation by VI. 1. 15. For had सनि been used in the sūtra, then the restriction would have been with regard to all Desideratives in general, whether the सन् was changed to ष or not. Therefore as there is restriction of VIII. 3. 59, in the case of सिसिअति where स is not changed to ष; so there would have been restriction in सुपुसते, the स could not have been changed to ष by VIII. 3. 59. Similarly in तिष्ठासति ॥

Q.—What is the necessity of exhibiting षण् with the anubandha ष? So that the rule should not apply to ष in general, but to the Desiderative affix ष only. As सुपुपिष इन्द्रम् ॥ This सुपुपिषे is the Perfect of स्वप्, the affix यास् is added as Chhandas irregularity instead of यल्; for यास् there is से, the affix is किन्तु by I. 2. 5, and so there is vocalisation by VI. 1. 15, and reduplication, and the augment इदृ is added by VII. 2. 13, the ए is changed to अस्, as सुपुपिषय इन्द्रं, the य is elided by VIII. 3. 19. Here after the reduplicate सु, the स is changed to ष, in पु by the general rule VIII. 3. 59, as the restriction of this sūtra does not apply in this case. But had ष in general been taken, then सुपुपिष has an affix ष, and therefore sūtra VIII. 3. 59, would have been restricted, and there would have been no change of सु to पु after the reduplicate, as it is not a causative. Hence षण् has been employed with an anubandha.

Why do we say ‘after a reduplicate’?

Ans.—So that this restriction may apply to that ष which would have been caused by the इ or उ of an abhyāsa, and not to that which would have been caused by an upasarga. As अनिषिषिअति, though without the Preposition, the form is सिसिअति ॥

Q.—No, this cannot be the reason, because the ष caused by the upasarga is considered as asiddha, and hence there would be no restriction.

BK. VIII. CH. III. § 63 ]

षष्ठ CHANGE.

1629

Ans.—Then we say, the abhyāsa is taken to be qualified by सन्, namely that abhyāsa which is caused by सन्, would give occasion to this rule and not any other abhyāsa. Therefore if a reduplication has been caused by यज्, and then पण्ड is added to it, then the restriction of the present sūtra will not apply, and पण्ड change will take place though the root may not be a Causative &c. Thus the यज् of स्वप् is सोपुष्य (VI. 1. 19), the Desiderative of this root is सोपुषिपते, with इद् augment, the elision of अ (VI. 4. 48) of य, the elision of य by VI. 4. 49.

Q.—No this also cannot be the reason: because the पण्ड change is antaranga, while the restriction niyama is Bahiranga. Therefore, the word abhyāsa is employed superfluously in the sūtra.

Ans.—The word abhyāsa is taken in the sūtra, so that the restriction may be with regard to that प which might have been caused by the इ or उ of the abhyāsa; and not to that प which might be occasioned by the इ or उ of a dhātu or verbal root. Thus मितिपिपति, अधीपिपति ॥ Here the root इ in the sense of बोधन, is turned to Desiderative with सन्; and by VI. 1. 2, the स is reduplicated, then by VII. 4. 79, the अ is changed to इ ॥ Thus इमिस; here by the force of the इ of the abhyāsa सि, the स is changed to प as इमिष; (VIII. 3. 59) then as the restriction of this sūtra does not apply, the root इ causes the पण्ड of the abhyāsa, as इमिष ॥ Had the word अभ्यसात् not been used in the sūtra, the स of abhyāsa could not have been changed to प, for then the sūtra would have meant “प is substituted for स, only in the case of स्तु and Causatives in the Desiderative पण्ड”; and as इमिष is not a Causative-Desiderative, the restriction would have applied.

सः स्विदिस्वदिसहीनां च ॥ ६२ ॥ पदानि ॥ सः, स्विदि-स्वदि-सहीनाम, च ॥
वृत्ति ॥ स्विदि स्वदि सहि इय्येतेषां न्यन्तानां सनि पभूते परतो ऽभ्यासादुत्तस्य सकारस्य सकारवेशो भवति ॥

62. स is substituted for the स् after the reduplicate of the पण्ड Desiderative of the Causatives of स्विद्, स्वद्, and सह ॥

The स substitute of स् debars the cerebral change. In other words, the स of these roots remains unchanged. As सिस्वदिपिपति, सिस्वादिपिपति and सिसाहिपिपति ॥

प्राक्सितादृश्यवाये ऽपि ॥ ६३ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्राक्, सितात्, अद्, व्यवाये, अपि ॥
वृत्ति ॥ सेवसितेति वक्ष्यति प्राक्सितसंशब्दानाधारित ऊर्ध्वमनुक्रमिष्यामस्तबाऽव्यवायेपि मूर्ध्न्यो भवति-
व्येवं तद्वैतिव्यमपिशव्यावनऽव्यवायेपि ॥

63. (The substitution of ष for स, to be taught hereafter, will take place) for all roots upto सित exclusive in

1630

पञ्च RULE.

[BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 65]

VIII. 3. 70, even when the augment अद् intervenes (between the स and the efficient letter).

The root सिद्ध् occurs in sūtra VIII. 3. 70. Thus VIII. 3. 65 teaches प change : as अभिपुणोति, परिपुणोति, विपुणोति, निपुणोति ॥ So also when अद् intervenes ; as अभ्युपुणोत्, पर्युपुणोत्, व्युपुणोत्, व्युपुणोत् ॥ The force of अपि is that the change takes place even when the augment अद् does not come, i. e. in cases other than the augment.

स्थादिष्वभ्यासेन चाभ्यासस्य ॥ ६७ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्थादिषु, अभ्यासेन, च, अभ्यासस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्राक् सितादिति वर्णते ॥ उपसर्गात्सुनोतीत्यत्र स्थासेनयवेषेति स्थादयस्तेषु स्थादिषु प्राक् सितसं-शब्दानाम् अभ्यासेन व्यपाये मूर्ध्नेभ्यो भवत्यभ्याससकारस्य च भवतीत्येवं वेदितव्यम् ॥

64. In स्था &c upto सिद्ध् exclusive (VIII. 3. 65 to VIII. 3. 70), this प substitution takes place then also, when the reduplicate intervenes, and the स of the reduplicate is also changed to प ॥

The words प्राक् सितात् are understood here also. The स्थादि roots are, स्था, सेनय &c in VIII. 3. 65 and ending with सेव in VIII. 3. 70. The sūtra consists of two sentences : (1) The पश्च takes place in स्था &c. even when a reduplicate intervenes ; (2) The स of the reduplicates of स्था &c. is changed to प ॥ The first is a vidhi rule, and the second is a niyama rule.

Thus परितद्यौ where the abhyāsa त intervenes. This applies even to roots other than those which have been taught with a प in the Dhātupātha. As अभिपिपेणविपति, परिपिपेणविपति (सेनया अभिपातुमिच्छन्ति). This applies moreover to reduplicates which end in अ, as अभितद्यौ ; here the स would not have been changed to प (by VIII. 3. 59) as it is not preceded by इ or उ ॥ Another raison d'être of this sūtra is that it prohibits पण् (VIII. 3. 61). As अभिपिपितति, परिपिपितति ॥

The word अभ्यासस्य is for the sake of niyama, as we have said above. स of स्था &c. and of no other roots is changed to प ॥ As अभिमुखुपति from पू-प्रेरणे with सव्, the augment is debarred by VII. 2. 12 : the root स is unchanged by the niyama prohibition of VIII. 3. 61 ; the reduplicate स remains unchanged by the restriction of the present sūtra.

उपसर्गात्सुनोतिसुवतिस्यतिस्तौतिस्तोमति स्थासेनयवेषि च सञ्जस्वजाम् ॥ ६५ ॥ पदानि ॥ उपसर्गात्, सुनोति-सुवति-स्थति-स्तौति-स्तोमति-स्था-सेनय-सेध-सिच-सञ्ज-स्वजाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपसर्गात्सुनोतिसुवतिस्यतिस्तौतिस्तोमति स्थासेनयवेषि च सञ्जस्वजाम् ॥ ६५ ॥ पदानि ॥ उपसर्गात्, सुनोति-सुवति-स्थति-स्तौति-स्तोमति-स्था-सेनय-सेध-सिच-सञ्ज-स्वजाम् ॥

(स्थति VII. 3. 71), स्तु (स्तौति VII. 3. 89), स्तुम् (स्तोमते), स्था, सेनय (Denominative), सिध् (सेधति), सिच्, सञ्ज् and सञ्ज् ॥

Thus अभिपुणोति, परिपुणोति, अभ्युपुणोत्, पर्युपुणोत् ॥ सुचति, अभिपुचति, परिपुचति, अभ्युपुचत्, पर्युपुचत् ॥ स्थति, अभिप्यति, परिप्यति, अभ्युप्यत्, पर्युप्यत् ॥ स्तौति, अभिष्टौति, परिष्टौति, अभ्युष्टौति ॥ स्तोमति, अभिष्टोमति, परिष्टोमति, अभ्युष्टोमति, पर्युष्टोमति ॥ स्था, अभिष्टास्यति, परिष्टास्यति, अभ्युष्टात्, पर्युष्टात्, अभिष्टो, परिष्टो ॥ सेनय, अभिष्टास्यति, परिष्टास्यति, अभ्युष्टास्यत्, पर्युष्टास्यत् ॥ अभिष्टास्यति, परिष्टास्यति ॥ सेध, अभिष्टास्यति, परिष्टास्यति, अभ्युष्टास्यत्, पर्युष्टास्यत् ॥ सिच्, अभिष्टास्यति, परिष्टास्यति, अभ्युष्टास्यत्, पर्युष्टास्यत्, अभिष्टास्यति, परिष्टास्यति ॥ सञ्ज्, अभिष्टास्यति, परिष्टास्यति, अभ्युष्टास्यत्, पर्युष्टास्यत्, अभिष्टास्यति, परिष्टास्यति ॥ सञ्ज्, अभिष्टास्यति, परिष्टास्यति, अभ्युष्टास्यत्, पर्युष्टास्यत्, अभिष्टास्यति ॥ सेष इति श्लोककरणनिदेशः सिध्यतिनिर्वृत्तयर्थः ॥ उपसर्गादिति, किम्? इधि सिञ्चति, मधु सिञ्चति, निगलाः ॥ सेचका अस्मादिशालिः सेचको देश इति ॥ नार्थे सिचेरुपसर्गः ॥ अभिसावकीयतीत्यत्रापि न सुनोति प्रति क्रियायोगः किं तर्हि सावकीये प्रति ॥ अभिसावयतीत्यत्र तु सुनोतिमेव प्रति क्रियायोगो न सावयतिमिति पश्यं भवति ॥

The root सिध् is exhibited in the sūtra as सेध with शप् vikaraṇa, thus debarring सिध्-सिध्यति ॥

Why do we say “after an upasarga”? Observe इधि सिञ्चति, मधु सिञ्चति (VIII. 3. 111). So निःसेचको देशः=निर्गता सेचका अस्माद् देशात् ॥ Here निः is not an Upasarga to सिच्, but to the noun सेचक ॥ Similarly in अभिसावकीयति, the upasarga अभि is not added to the root सु (सुनोति), but to the *third* derivative of सु (सुनोति). Namely, from सु we derive सावक with णुल्, and from सावक we form the Denominative root सावकीय with णुल्; and to this Denominative root अभि is added. The upasarga, however may be added to the root first, and then णुल् and णुल् added. In that case, the rule will apply. As अभिसावकीयति ॥ So also with the Causative, as अभिसावयति, for here the upasarga is added to the root सु and not to the causative form सावय ॥

The roots पुष्ट अभिषे belongs to Svādi class, पु प्रेरणे to Tudādi class, पोऽन्तकर्मणि to Divādi class, णुल् स्तुतो to Adādi class and णुल् स्तने, to Bhuādi Class. These have been shown in the sūtra in their declined form in order to indicate that the rule does not apply to their यङ् लुक्, as अभिसोषवाति ॥ See VII. 1. 6 for this rule of द्वित् exhibited roots. On the other hand, the roots सिच् &c. being not so exhibited, change their स in यङ् लुक् also, as अभिषेपिचीति ॥

The upasarga need not *end* with इ and उ for the purposes of this rule. Thus निष्पुणोति, तुष्पुणोति, where the upasarga is निस्तु and तुष् ॥

सदिरप्रेतः ॥ ६६ ॥ पदानि ॥ सदिः, अप्रतेः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सदेः सकाशस्य उपसर्गस्याभिमित्ताग्रतस्तरस्य मूर्धन्य आवेशो भवति ॥

66. The स of सद् is changed to प after an Upasarga having an ई or उ, but not after प्रति ॥

The word सदिः is in the first case, but has the force of genitive. Thus विपादति विपादति, न्यपीवत्, न्यपीवत् ॥ निपसाद, निपसाद ॥ The second स remains unchanged in the Perfect by VIII. 3. 118.

[BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 69]

Why do we say 'but not after प्रति'? Observe प्रतिसंदिति ॥ Prof. Bohlingk points out that the sūtra is संदेशतः as given by Sayānāchārya in his commentary on Rig Veda VI. 13. 1. Pāṇini, however, often uses the first case with the force of the Genitive, as in VIII. 3. 80.

स्तम्भः ॥ ६७ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्तम्भः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्तम्भः सकारस्य उपसर्गस्याश्रितादुत्तरस्य मूर्ध्न्य आविशो भवति ॥

67. The स of स्तम्भ is changed into प after an up-asarga, having an इ or उ ॥

Thus अभिष्टभाति । परिष्टभाति । अभ्यष्टभाति । पर्यष्टभाति । अभिष्टभाति । परिष्टभाति । The word अभिष्टः of the last sūtra is not to be read here. Hence we have forms like:—प्रतिष्टभाति । प्रत्यष्टभाति । प्रत्यस्तितष्टभाति ॥

अवाखालम्बनाविदूर्ययोः ॥ ६८ ॥ पदानि ॥ अवात्, च, आलम्बन-आविदूर्ययोः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ अवशब्दादुपसर्गादुत्तरस्य स्तम्भः सकारस्य मूर्ध्न्याविशो भवति । आलम्बनेयं आविदूर्यं च ॥

68. The स of स्तम्भ is changed into प after the preposition अव in the sense of 'support' and 'contiguity'.

The word आलम्बन means 'support, refuge, that upon which any thing depends or leans'. आविदूर्य means 'the state of not being विदूर or far off, i. e. to be contiguous'.

Thus अवष्टभ्यास्ते 'He remains leaning upon a staff' &c, अवष्टभ्य तिष्ठति ॥ So also in the sense of to be near, as अवष्टभ्या सेना 'the army near at hand'. अवष्टभ्या शरत् ॥ See V. 2. 13.

Why do we say 'when having the sense of support or contiguity'? Thus अवष्टभ्यो वृषलः शीतेन 'the Śūdra is afflicted with cold'.

The present sūtra is commenced in order to make the प change even while the preceding letter is not इ or उ ॥

वेश्य स्वनो भोजने ॥ ६९ ॥ पदानि ॥ वेः, च, स्वनः, भोजने ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वेश्यसर्गावशोत्तरस्य भोजनायै स्वनतः सकारस्य मूर्ध्न्याविशो भवति ॥

69. The प is substituted for the स of स्वन्, after वि and अव, when the sense is 'to smack while eating'.

Thus विख्यन्ति, व्यप्यन्ति, विख्याण, अवप्यन्ति, अवाप्यन्ति, अवप्याण ॥ That is, he makes sound while eating, he eats with a smack.

Why do we say 'when making a smacking sound in eating'? Observe विख्यन्ति घृक्: 'the drum sounds'.

71. The प-change may take place optionally in the सिव् and the rest (of the last sūtra), even when the augment अ intervenes between the prepositions परि, नि or वि and the verb.

The सिवादि are the four roots सिव् सह, स्तु and स्वंञ्, as well as the augment सुह् ॥ This is an example of ubhayatra-vibhāshā. वृत्तिः ॥ अनु वि परि आभि नि इयेतेभ्य उत्तरस्य स्यन्द्वेतप्राणिषु सकारस्य वा मूर्ध्न्योयेशो भवति ॥

72. प is optionally the substitute of the स of स्यन्द्व, after the prepositions अनु, वि, परि, अभि and नि, when the subject is not a living being.

The root स्यन्द्व प्रसवणे is anudātta. Thus अनुस्यन्द्वे । विण्यन्द्वे । परिण्यन्द्वे । अभिर्न्यन्द्वे । नित्यन्द्वे । अनुस्यन्द्वे । विण्यन्द्वे । परिन्यन्द्वे ।

1634

पल्लव CHANGE.

[BK VIII. CH. III §. 75]

Why do we say 'when the subject is not a living being'? Observe अनुस्यन्दे मत्स्य उक्ते ॥ The option of this sūtra will apply, when the subject is a compound of living and non-living beings. Thus अनुस्यन्देते or अनुस्यन्देते मत्स्योक्ते ॥ The subject here is a Dvandva compound, and it is not in the singular number because of II. 4. 6. The word अपाणिषु is a Paryudāsa and not a Prasajya-patishedha. If it be the latter sort of prohibition, then the force will be on the word *living*, and in a compound like मत्स्योक्ते, consisting of *living* and *non-living* beings, the prohibition will apply because it has a *living* being in it, and so there will be no पन्त ॥ In the other view, the force is on the word *non-living*, and because the compound contains a non-living being, therefore the option will be applied, and the presence of the living being along with it will be ignored.

The anuvṛtti of परि, नि and वि is understood here from VIII. 3. 70. So these words could well have been omitted from the sūtra, which might have then been अन्वभिर्भ्यांच् स्यन्देतेप्राणिषु, and by the force of च् we would draw in the anuvṛtti of परि &c.

वेः स्कन्देरनिष्ठायाम् ॥ ७३ ॥ पदानि ॥ वेः, स्कन्देः, अनिष्ठायाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वेष्टसर्गादुत्तरस्य स्कन्देः सकारस्य दुर्ज्ञेयो वा भवति अनिष्ठायाम् ॥

73. ष is optionally substituted for the स् of स्कन्द, after the preposition वि, but not in the participles in त and तवत् ॥

The root is स्कन्दिर् गति शोषणयोः ॥ Thus विक्कन्ता or विक्कन्ता, विक्कन्तुम् or विक्कन्तुम्, विक्कन्तव्यम् or विक्कन्तव्यम् ॥

Why do we say 'but not in the Nishṭhā'? Observe विक्कन्तः

परेश्व ॥ ७४ ॥ पदानि ॥ परेः, च् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ परिशब्दाचोत्तरस्य स्कन्देः सकारस्य वा दुर्ज्ञेयो भवति ॥

74. ष is optionally substituted for the स् of स्कन्द after the preposition परि every where.

Thus परिष्कन्ता or परिष्कन्ता, परिष्कन्तुम् or परिष्कन्तुम्, परिष्कन्तव्यम् or परिष्कन्तव्यम् ॥

The word परि could well have been included in the last sūtra as विपत्तिभ्यां स्कन्दे &c. The very fact that it has not been so included, indicates that the prohibition of अनिष्ठायाम् does not apply to it. Thus परिष्कन्तः or परिष्कन्तः ॥

परिष्कन्दः प्राच्यमरेतेषु ॥ ७५ ॥ पदानि ॥ परिष्कन्दः, प्राच्यमरेतेषु ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ परिष्कन्द इति दुर्ज्ञेयाभावो विपत्तिभ्यां प्राच्यमरेतेषु प्रयोगविषयेषु ॥

75. The word परिष्कन्द is used without the cerebral change in the country of Eastern Bharata.

BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 78 ] CEREBRAL CHANGE.

1635

This is an anomaly. The प required by the last sātra is prohibited. The other form is परिष्कन्दः ॥ The word परिष्कन्द is formed by the affix अच् or it is a Nishthā, the त being elided. The word भरत qualifies the word प्राच्य ॥

Prof. Bohlingk translates it “परिष्कन्द is seen in the usage of the Eastern People and the Bharata”. He bases his construction on the sātras II. 4. 66, and IV. 2. 113, where प्राच्यभरतेषु means “the Eastern People and Bharata”.

स्फुरतिस्फुल्लयोर्निर्विश्वः ॥ ७६ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्फुरति, स्फुल्लयोः, निस्, नि, विश्वः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्फुरतिस्फुल्लयोः सकारस्य निस् नि वि इयेतेभ्य उत्तरस्य वा मूर्धन्यादेशो भवति ॥

76. प is optionally substituted for the स of स्फुर and स्फुल् after the prepositions निस्, नि, and वि ॥

Thus निष्फुरति or निस्फुरति, निस्फुरति or निष्फुरति, विस्फुरति, विष्फुरति ॥ स्फुलति, निष्फुलति, निस्फुलति, निस्फुलति, विस्फुलति, विस्फुलति ॥

वेः स्कन्धातेनित्यम् ॥ ७७ ॥ पदानि ॥ वेः, स्कन्धातेः, नित्यं ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वेरतस्य स्कन्धातेः सकारस्य नित्यं मूर्धन्यादेशो भवति ॥

77. प is always substituted for the स of स्कन्ध, after the preposition वि ॥

Thus विष्कन्धाति, विष्कन्धित्वा, विष्कन्धितुम्, विष्कन्धितव्यम् ॥

इणः पीध्वंलुङ्गलिटां धोऽङ्गात् ॥ ७८ ॥ पदानि ॥ इणः, पीध्वं, लुङ्गलिटाम्, धः, अङ्गात् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मूर्धन्य इति वच्यते । इणन्तादङ्गात्परेषां पीध्वंलुङ्गलिटां यो धकारस्तस्य मूर्धन्यादेशो भवति ॥

78. The cerebral sound is substituted in the room of the ध of पीध्वम्, and of the Personal-endings of the Aorist and the Perfect, after a stem ending in इण् (a vowel other than अ).

The word ‘cerebral’ is understood here from VIII. 3. 55. Thus व्योपीडुम्, प्रोपीडुम् ॥ Aorist :—अव्योडुम्, अप्रोडुम् (VIII. 2. 25). Perfect : अक्रुड् ॥

Though the anuvritti of इण्कोः was current here from VIII. 3. 57, yet the repetition of the word इण् here indicates that the anuvritti of कु or the guttural ceases. As पसीध्वम्, यसीध्वम् ॥

Why do we say “the ध of पीध्वं, लुङ् and लिङ्”? Observe स्तुच्ये, अस्तुच्यम्, where the ध is of लङ् and लङ् ॥

Why do we say अङ्गात् ‘after a stem’? Observe परिवेवीध्वम्, from विष्कन्ध्यात्री of the Juhotyādi class. There is Guna of the reduplicate by VII. 4. 75, the स of सीधुद is elided by VII. 2. 79, and पीध्वम् here is made up of the प of the root विष्, and ईध्वम् the affix; therefore पीध्वं here is not after the anga परिवे वि, for the anga here is परिवे विष्, and ईध्वम् is the affix. This result could have been
