CEREBRAL CHANGE.

[BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 81]

obtained, without using the word अङ्गात् in the sutra, by the maxim अर्धवद् ग्रहणं नानर्थकस्य “a combination of letters capable of expressing a meaning, denotes that combination of letters in so far as it possesses that meaning, but it does not denote a combination void of meaning”.

विभाषेटः ॥ ७६ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, इटः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इणः परस्मादित उत्तरेषां पीप्यवल्लुविलां वा प्रकारस्तस्य मूर्धन्यादेशो भवति विभाषा ॥

79. The cerebral sound is optionally substituted for the ध of पीप्यम् and of the Aorist and the Perfect after the augment इट्, when the stem ends in इण् ॥

Thus लु+इट्+पीप्यम्=लविपीप्यम् or लविपीद्वम् so also पविपीप्यम् or पविपीद्वम् from पु ॥ Aorist:—अलविप्यम् or अलविद्वम् ॥ Perfect:—लुलुविप्ये or लुलुविद्वे ॥

The word इण् is understood here and it qualifies the word इट्, so that the stem should end in an इण् vowel which should be followed by the इट् augment and this letter should be followed by पीप्यम् and the ध beginning affixes of the Aorist and the Perfect. If the stem does not end in an इण् vowel, the rule will not apply; as आसिपीप्यम् from the root आस उपवेशने ॥

Then in the word उपविधीयेद्वे, will the cerebral change not take place by the option of this sutra or otherwise? This is from the root वीड् शये in the Perfect with the augment इट् (VII. 2. 13.), and युट् (by VI. 4. 63). Some say that as the augment युट् intervenes between the stem ending in ई (इण् vowel), and the augment इट्, therefore this rule will not apply and there will not be the optional इ ॥ Others hold that the anuvritti of अङ्गात् has ceased, and the anuvritti of इण् is only current, in this sutra, and there is no intervention and so there will be the optional change into इ ॥

समासेङ्गुलेः सङ्गः ॥ ८० ॥ पदानि ॥ समासे, अङ्गुलेः, सङ्गः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सङ्गसकारस्याङ्गुलैरुत्तरस्य मूर्धन्यादेशो भवति समासे ॥

80. प् is substituted for the स् of सङ्ग after the word अङ्गुलि in a compound.

Thus अङ्गुलिपङ्गः । अङ्गुलिपङ्गो यवागुः । अङ्गुलिपङ्गो गाः सादयति ॥ Why do we say in a compound? Observe अङ्गुले सङ्गं पदय ॥

The word सङ्गः is exhibited in the sutra in the nominative case. The force is here that of Genitive i. e. सङ्गस्य ॥

भीरोः स्थानम् ॥ ८१ ॥ पदानि ॥ भीरोः, स्थानम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्थानसकारस्य भीरोरुत्तरस्य मूर्धन्यादेशो भवति ॥

81. प् is substituted for the स् of स्थानं when preceded by भीरु in a compound.

Thus भीरुषानम् ॥ The word compound is understood here also; otherwise भीरो स्थानं पदय ॥

BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 85]

५ CHANGE.

1637

अग्नेः स्तुतस्तोमसोमाः ॥ ८२ ॥ पदानि ॥ अग्नेः, स्तुत, स्तोम, सोमाः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अग्निरुत्तरस्य स्तुत, स्तोम, सोम इत्यतेषां सकारस्य मूर्धन्यादिशो भवति समासे ॥

इटिः ॥ अग्निर्दीर्घात् सोमस्थैष्यते ॥

82. प् is substituted for the स् of स्तुत, स्तोम and सोम when preceded by अग्नि in a compound.

Thus अग्निदुत, अग्निटोमः, अग्नीषोमः ॥

*Ishti*:—The इ of अग्नि is lengthened before सोम and it is after such lengthened ई, that the स of सोम is changed to प्, otherwise not. As अग्निसोमी माणवकी ॥ So also अग्निसोमी तिष्ठतः (where 'agni' means fire, and 'soma' a kind of herb) 'the fire and the soma plant are here.'

When there is no compounding we have अग्ने सोमः ॥

The word अग्निदुत is formed by द्विषु, the *sacrifice* in which Agni is praised (स्तूयते) is so called. अग्निटोमः is also the name of a sacrifice: the first division (संस्था) of the Soma-yāga. अग्नीषोमः is a देवता-इन्द्रः so where there is no Devatā-Dvandva, the प् change will not take place. Thus where Agni and Soma are names of two boys, or where they refer to physical fire and herb. According to Āśvalāyana there is lengthening and प् change in the last case also, as अग्नीषोमी प्रणेष्यामि ॥

ज्योतिरायुषः स्तोमः ॥ ८३ ॥ पदानि ॥ ज्योतिः, आयुषः, स्तोमः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ज्योतिः आयुष इत्येताभ्यावुत्तरस्य स्तोमसकारस्य मूर्धन्यादिशो भवति समासे ॥

83. The स् of स्तोमः is changed to प् after ज्योतिः and आयुष in a compound.

As ज्योतिटोमः, आयुटोमः, but ज्योतिः स्तोमस्थैष्यते where there is no compounding.

मातृपितृभ्यां स्वसा ॥ ८४ ॥ पदानि ॥ मातृ, पितृभ्यां, स्वसा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मातृ पितृ इत्येताभ्यावुत्तरस्य स्वसुसकारस्य समासे मूर्धन्यादिशो भवति ॥

84. The स् of स्वस is changed to प् after मातृ and पितृ in a compound.

As मातृस्वसा, पितृस्वसा ॥ See VI. 3. 24.

मातुःपितृभ्यामन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ८५ ॥ पदानि ॥ मातुः, पितृभ्यां, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मातृ पितृ इत्येताभ्यावुत्तरस्य स्वसुसकारस्य न्यतरस्यां मूर्धन्यादिशो भवति समासे ॥

85. The स् of स्वस is optionally changed to प्, after मातृ and पितृ in a compound.

Thus मातुःस्वसा or मातुःस्वसा; पितुःस्वसा or पितुःस्वसा ॥ The word मातृ and पितृ end in र्, which is changed to visarga (See VIII. 2. 24). In fact, the word पितृ is so exhibited in the sutra itself, with a र्, the word मातुः therefore, by the rule of साङ्चर्य is also to be understood as a र् ending word.

Q.—Well, if this be so, when this र् is changed to a visarga, and the visarga changed to स् by VIII. 3. 36, then there would be no प् change?

1638

ष CHANGE.

[Bk. VIII. Ch. III. § 87]

Ans.—The ष change would take place both after the visarga-ending or स-ending words, on the maxim एकवैश्विकृतस्थानव्यावत् “That which has undergone a change in regard to one of its parts, is by no means, in consequence of this change, something else than what it was before the change had taken place”. Therefore, these words are taken to end in र्॥ For if they were taken to end in स्, then the rule would not apply when they ended in a visarga. If they be supposed to end in a visarga, then the form पितृभ्यांम with a र् before भ्याम् in the sutra is hard to explain.

The word समासे is understood here also. Therefore not here मातुः स्वसा when the words are used separately in a sentence.

अभिनिसस्तनः शब्दसंज्ञायाम् ॥ ५६ ॥ पदानि ॥ अभि-निसः, स्तनः, शब्दसंज्ञायाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अभि निस् इत्येतस्मादुत्तरस्य स्तनतिसकारस्य मूर्धन्यविषो भवति अन्यतरस्यां शब्दसंज्ञायां गम्य-मानायाम् ॥

86. The स् of स्तन् is optionally changed to ष् after the double preposition अभि निस्, when the word so formed is the name of a particular letter (i. e. visarga).

As अभिनिदानो वर्णः, अभिनिदानो विसर्जनीयः or अभिनिस्तानो वर्णः or विसर्जनीयः ॥ The compound preposition अभि-निस् causes this change, and not any one of them separately. Thus Āpastamba:—ब्रह्मं चतुरक्षरं वा नामपुनर्माख्यातोत्तरं दीर्घमि-निदान्तं, घोषवशान्तरन्तस्यम् “a name (nāma) should be such that it should consist of two-syllables or four-syllables, that its first portion should be a noun (nama-pūrva), and its second portion a verb (ākhyāta), that it should end in a long vowel (dirgha) or a visarga (abhinishtāna), that the first letter of such a noun should be a ghosha or sonant letter (ghosha-vad-ādi), and a semi-vowel (antastha) should be in the body of it.” Thus the names द्विविषोवा, वरिषोवा fulfill these conditions and are good names.

Why do we say “when it is the name of a particular letter”? Observe अभिनिस्तनति प्रवृत्तः ॥ The anuvṛtti of समासे ceases from this place.

उपसर्गप्रादुर्भ्यांमस्तिर्यचपरः ॥ ८७ ॥ पदानि ॥ उपसर्ग, प्रादुर्भ्यांम, अस्ति:, यचपरः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपसर्गस्याभिनिसाद्यादुतशब्दावोत्तरस्य यकारपरस्याचपरस्य चास्तिसकारस्य मूर्धन्यो भवति ॥

87. The स् of the verb अस् is changed to ष्, when it is followed by a vowel or य and is preceded by प्रादुः, or an upasarga having इ or उ in it.

The word यच् परः means ‘followed by य or अच्’ ॥ The word प्रादुः is an Indeclinable, meaning ‘evidently’.

Thus अभिषन्ति, निषन्ति, विषन्ति, प्रादुःषन्ति; अभिष्यात्, निष्यात्, विष्यात्, प्रादुःष्यात् ॥

BK. VIII. CH. III §. 88]

ष CHANGE.

1639

Why do we say “when preceded by an *Upasarga* having an इ or उ?”
Observe वांध्यात्, मधुध्यात् ॥ Why do we say ‘of the verb अस्’? Observe अनु-
सुतम्, विसुतम् ॥

Q.—How is there any occasion for the application of the rule here?
The context here relates to स, and the word “upasarga” qualifies that स, but
here the upasarga is not applied to स but to the *whole verb* स, therefore this is
no counter-example. In fact, what is the necessity of using the word अस् at
all in the sūtra: for even without it, the word ‘upasarga’ would qualify that
verb which consists of स only, and such a verb is अस्, with its अ elided and
no other verb? Nor is the employment of अस् necessary for प्रादु, for it comes
only in connection with the verbs क्, भू and अस् ॥

Ans.—All that you urge, is true, yet the following counter-example
should be given, as अनुसू, the son of Anusā will be आनुसेयः with इक् as it be-
longs to Subhrādi class. Thus अनुसू+इक्=आनुसू+एय=आनुसू+एय ॥ Here the
क is elided by VI. 4. 147. Now when क is elided, the स is the only verb-
element that remains, अनु is upasarga, and एय is affix; so that had अस् not
been taken in the sūtra, the rule would apply to this स also.

Why do we say “when it is followed by a vowel or य”? Observe
निस्तः, विस्तः, प्रादुस्तः ॥

सुविनिर्दुर्भ्यः सुपिसूतिसमाः ॥ ५५ ॥ पदानि ॥ सु, वि, निर्, दुर्भ्यः, सुपि,
सूति, समाः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सु वि निर् दुह इलेतेन्य उत्तरस्य सुपि सूति सम इलेतेनां सकारस्य मूढेन्यादेशो भवति ॥

Kārikā:—सुपेः पल्लं स्वपेर्मा मूढिसुव्यापति केन न ।

हलादिशेषात् सुपिरिष्टं पूर्वं प्रसारणम् ॥

स्थादीनां नियमो नात्र प्राक्सितादुत्तरः सुपि ।

अनर्थके विषुपुपः पुपिसूतो हिरण्यते ॥

88. The स of स्वप्, सूति, and सम is changed to प्
after सु, वि, निर् and दुह ॥

The word सुपि is exhibited in the sūtra as the form of स्वप् with voca-
lisation. Thus सुपुमः, निः पुमः दुः पुमः ॥ The word सूति is the किन ending form of स्;
the rule applies to this form only, as सुपूतिः, विघूतिः, निः पूर्ति and दुः पूर्तिः ॥ The
word सम also means the *noun* सम and not the verb सम स्तम वैकल्प्ये ॥ Thus
सुपमम्, विषमम्, निः पमम्, दुः पमम् ॥

Kārikā:—Why is पल्लं taught with regard to the सुप् form of स्वप्? Ans.
सुपेः पल्लं स्वपेर्मा मूढ, so that the पल्लं change should not take place in स्वप् form, as
विस्वप् and विस्वप्क् (III. 2. 172) ॥ Q. विसुव्यापति केन न? For what reason the
पल्लं change has not taken place in the reduplicate विसुव्याप, for here also in
the reduplicate, is the form सुप्, as विसुव्याप, and then by applying हलादिशेष rule,
the प् is elided, and एकदेशविकृतस्थानन्यत्वात् applies? Ans. हलादि शेषात् न सुपिः, we

reduplicate the form स्वप्, as विस्वप्स्वप् and then elide प्, as विस्वप्स्वप्, and then vocalise, as विस्वप्स्वप् so that there being no form सुप्, there is no पत्व ॥इह पूर्व प्रसारणं, in fact, the vocalisation takes place first, and then elision according to an ishti. See VI 1. 17. Otherwise, in स्वप् स्वप्, as प् is elided, प् would also have been elided. Why is the स् of विस्वप्स्वप् not changed to प् by VIII. 3. 64? स्यादीनां नियमो नाच प्राक् सितादुत्तरः सुपि, the rule VIII. 3. 64 does not apply, because that rule is confined only to verbs up to सित in VIII. 3. 70, while सुप् is after that verb. Moreover the प् of सुप् being elided, the mere सु is अनर्थक, and the maxim is अर्थवद् भङ्गे नानर्थकस्य ॥ Q. If this maxim is applied, how do you form विस्वप्स्वप्? Ans. अनर्थक विस्वप्स्वप्: सुपिभूतोऽहिरुच्यते, here the form सुप् is doubled, and not सुप् ॥ The root is first joined with the affix वि+स्वप्, then there is vocalisation विस्वप्, then there is प् change, as विस्वप्, then reduplication, as विस्वप्स्वप् ॥ Now पत्व being considered asiddha, the doubling should take place first? No, for we have already shown that for the purposes of doubling, the पत्व change is not asiddha (VIII. 2. 3 Vårt.)

Thus हरयः सेना अस्य=हरिषेणः, परितः सेना अस्य=परिषेणः, so also वारिषेणः, जानुषेणी॥ Why do we say 'followed by ष'? Observe हरिष्कृयम्॥ Why do we say 'when a Name'? Observe पृथ्वी सेना अस्य स=पृथुसेनो राजा (VI. 3. 34). Why do we say 'when the स is not preceded by ग'? 100 When the preceding word is the name of a Lunar mansion, the ष substitution for स under the above mentioned circumstances is optional.

Thus रोहिणिषेणः or रोहिणिसेनः, मरणिषेणः or मरणिसेनः॥ But not here शत-भिषक् सेनः were the preceded letter is ग॥ These two sūtras 99 and 100 are really Gaṇa-sūtras, being read in the मुपामादि Gaṇa. The author of Kāsikā has raised them to the rank of full sūtras.

All cerebral ष changes, when not referable to any specific rule, should be classified under this Sushāmādi gaṇa.

Q.—But this स would never have been changed to ष because of the prohibition in VIII. 3. III, how can you then give this counter-example?

Ans.—Though the स of the affix सात् is prohibited by VIII. 3. III, yet the counter-example is valid, because the स of the base सर्पिस् is also not changed. Why do we say 'of a Taddhita'? Observe सर्पिस्तरति ॥

Vart:—Prohibition must be stated of finite verbs before Taddhita affixes. As भिन्युस्तराम् । छिन्युस्तराम् ॥ These are the Potential third person plural of भिन्यु and छिन्यु with the augment याजुद्; the Taddhita affix तरप् is added by V. 3. 56, and आम् is added by V. 4. 11.

Vart:—Prohibition must be stated with regard to पुंस् as पुंस्यम् पुंस्ता ॥

102. ष is substituted for the स of निस before the verb तप् when the meaning is not that of 'repeatedly making red hot'.

The word असिवन means doing a thing repeatedly and here it means making it red-hot repeatedly. Thus निहपतिः सुवर्णम्=सकृत् अग्रिम् स्वर्गयति i. e. he puts the gold into fire only once.

Why do we say when not meaning repeatedly. Observe निस्तपति सुवर्ण सुवर्णकारः=पुनः पुनरपि स्वर्गयति ॥

In the sentences निहतं रक्षः, निहता अरातयः the change has taken place either as a Vedic irregularity or because the sense of repeatedness is not implied here.

The word युग्मन् here means the substitutes स्वम्, स्वाम्, ते, तव. As अभिद्वं, नामासीत् ॥ स्वा, अभिद्वा वर्जयामसि ॥ ते, अभिदे विभुमानय ॥ तव, अपृश्वमे सथिदव. ( Rig VIII. 43. 9 ) ॥ तत्, अभिद्विभुमानय, ( Rig X. 2. 4 ) ततश्च, व्यायाध्वि निष्ठतश्चः पु ॥ अन्तः-पारमिति किम्, नियमामनो विदाभूवमिस्तत्पुनराह जातवेदो विचर्षणिः ॥

Why do we say in the inner half of a stanza? Observe यन्मभात्मनो निन्दाभूवमि सत्पुनराह जातवेदो विचर्षणिः ॥ Here the word अभिः is at the end of the first stanza while तत् is at the beginning of the second stanza, therefore the स of अभिस is not in the middle of a stanza.

यजुष्येकेषाम् ॥ १०४ ॥ पदानि ॥ यजुषि, एकेषाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यजुषि विषये युग्मन्ततश्चः पु परत एकेषामाचार्याणां मतेन सकारस्य मूर्धन्यादेशो भवति ॥

107. In the opinion of some, the above change takes place in Yajurveda also.

Thus अभिर्मिद्वम् or अभिर्मिस्त्वम् । अभिद्वम् or अभिस्त्वम् । अभिद्वम् or अभिस्त्वम् । अभिर्मिष्टतश्चः or अभिर्मिस्ततश्चः ॥

स्तुतस्तोमयोऽछन्दसि ॥ १०५ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्तुतस्तोमयोः, छन्दसि ।

वृत्तिः ॥ एकेषामिति वर्तते । स्तुत स्तोम इत्येतयोः सकारस्य छन्दसि विषये मूर्धन्यादेशो भवति एकेषामाचार्याणां मतेन छन्दसिविषये ।

105. The स of स्तुत and स्तोम, in the Chhandas, is changed to ष in the opinion of some.

Thus भिर्मिष्टतस्य or भिर्मिस्तुतस्य, गोष्ठां पोष्ठशिनम् or गोष्ठां पोष्ठशिनम् ॥ This change would have taken place by the general rule contained in the next sutra VIII. 3. 106, the special mention of स्तुत and स्तोम here is a mere amplification. The word छन्दसि of this sutra governs the subsequent sutra also.

पूर्वपदात् ॥ १०६ ॥ पदानि ॥ पूर्वपदात् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पूर्वपदस्याभिमितादुत्तरस्य सकारस्य मूर्धन्यादेशो भवति छन्दसि विषये एकेषामाचार्याणां मतेन ।

106. In the Chhandas, according to some, स is changed to ष, when it stands in the beginning of a second word, preceded by a word ending in इ &c.

The words छन्दसि and एकेषां are both understood here. Thus द्विषन्धः or द्विसन्धिः, त्रिषन्धिः or त्रिसन्धिः; मधुज्ञानम् or मधुस्थानम्, द्विसाहस्रं चिन्वीत् or द्विसाहस्रं चिन्वीत् ॥

The word पूर्वपद here means the first member of a compound word as well as the prior word other than that in a compound. Thus त्रिःसङ्ग्रहत्वाय or त्रिःसङ्ग्रहत्वाय ॥

सुजः ॥ १०७ ॥ पदानि ॥ सुजः ।

वृत्तिः ॥ सुभिति निपात इह गृह्यते तस्य पूर्वपदस्याभिमितादुत्तरस्य मूर्धन्यादेशो भवति छन्दसि विषये ।

1646

एष CHANGE.

[BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 109]

107. The स of the Particle सु is changed to ष in the Chhandas, when preceded by another word having in it the change-effecting letter इ &c.

Thus अनी पु णः सखीनाम् (Rig. IV. 31. 3) ऊहं ऊ पु णः (Rig. I. 36. 13). The lengthening takes place by VI. 3. 134, and न changed to ण by VIII. 4. 27.

सनोतेरनः ॥ १०८ ॥ पदानि ॥ सनोतेः, अनः ।

वृत्तिः ॥ सनोतेरनकारान्तस्य सकारस्य मूर्धन्यादेशो भवति ।

108. The स of the verb सन्, when it loses its न, is changed to ष, under the same circumstances.

Thus गोषाः (Rig. IX. 2. 10), formed by the affix बिद (III. 2. 67), the न is elided by VI. 4. 41. So also नृषाः ॥

Why do we say 'when it loses its न'? Observe गोसनि वाचमुदीरयन् (Atharv. III. 20. 10). Here the affix is इन् (III. 2. 27). See however गोषाणि in Rig. VI. 53. 10.

Though this ष change would have taken place by VIII. 3. 106 also, the separate enumeration is for the sake of niyama or restriction. Some however read the word गोसनिः in the list of सवनानि words (VIII. 3. 110), and they hold that the proper counter-example is सिसानयिपति ॥ So also सिसनीः formed by adding किञ्च to the Derivative root सिसनिस, thus सिसनिस + किञ्च = सिसनिस (the अ is elided by VI. 4. 48) + 0. add सु, सिसनिस + स = सिसनिस + 0 [स is elided by VI. 1. 68. Now the final स (of the Desiderative affix सन्) is liable to be changed either to ष or to र (इ). The ष being asiddha, the इ change takes place.] = सिसनिस = सिसनीः (the lengthening is by VIII. 2. 76). Here the Desiderative affix सन् is not changed to ष, hence this word is not governed by VIII. 3. 61. This being the object of this sutra, there will be ष change in सिपाणयिपति in the Causative.

सहेः पूतनत्तौध्यां च ॥ १०९ ॥ पदानि ॥ सहेः पूतना-ऋताभ्यां, च ।

वृत्तिः ॥ पूतना ऋत इत्येताभ्यांश्चरस्य सहसिकारस्य मूर्धन्यादेशो भवति ।

109. The स of सह is changed to ष, after पूतना and ऋत ॥

Thus पूतनापाहम्, ऋतापाहम् ॥ Some divide this sutra into two; as (1) सहेः; (2) पूतनात्तौध्यां ॥ So that the rule may apply to ऋतीपहः also. The word ऋति is lengthened by VI. 3. 116, in sanhitā : and the ष change takes place in sanhitā only. Otherwise the form is ऋतिसहम् ॥ The word च 'and' in the sutra includes words other than those not mentioned in it. The word ऋतीपहः would be valid by this also.

BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 112 ]

षष CHANGE.

1647

न रपरसुपिसजिस्पृशिस्सुहिसवनादीनाम् ॥ ११० ॥ पदानि ॥ न, र-पर, सृपि, सृजि, स्पृशि, स्पृहि-सवनादीनाम् ।

वृत्तिः ॥ रेफरस्य सकारस्य सृपि सृजि स्पृशि स्पृहि सवनादीनां च मूर्ध्न्यो न भवति ।

110. The प् substitution does not take place if र follows the स, as well as in सृप, सृज, स्पृश स्पृह, and in सवन and the rest.

Thus विश्लेषिकायाः काण्डं जुहोति ॥ The word विश्लेषिक is formed by the affix ण्वल (III. 3. 109), विश्लेषः कथयति ॥ This word is from the root सृप्सु विश्लेष, the वृह is not added by VII. 2. 15 and the nasal is elided by VI. 4. 24. before the nisthha स ॥ सृपः—पुरा क्रूरस्य विसृपः ॥ The word विसृपः is formed by the affix कछुन् (III. 4. 17), सृजः—बाच्चो विसर्जनात् ॥ स्पृशः—दिग्विसृपम् ॥ स्पृहिः—निसृप् कथयति ॥

The following is a list of सवनादि words :—

1 सवने सवने, 2 सुते सुते, 3 सोने सोने, 4 सवनमुखे सवनमुखे, 5 किसः किसः (किस्यतीति किसः), 6 अनुसवनमनुसवनम्, 7 गोसनि गोसनिम्, 8 अश्वसनिमश्वसनिम् ॥ In some books this is the list 9 सवने सवने, 10 सवनमुखे सवनमुखे, 11 अनुसवनमनुसवनम् (अनुसवने २), 12 सजायां बृहस्पतिसवः, 13 शकुनिसवनम्, 14 सोने, सोने, 15 सुते सुते (सुते २), 16 संवत्सरे सवत्सरे, 17 विसं विसम्, 18 किसं किसम् (किसं किसम्), 19 मुसलं मुसलम् 20 गोसनिम्, 21 अश्वसनिम् ॥

सात्पदादयोः ॥ १११ ॥ पदानि ॥ सात्, पदादयोः ।

वृत्तिः ॥ साविति चैतस्य यङि परतो मूर्ध्न्यादेशो न भवति ।

111. The प् substitution does not take place in the affix सात् and for that स which stands at the beginning of a word.

Thus सात् here is the affix ordained by V. 4. 52, and it would have been changed to प् by VIII. 3. 59. The present sūtra prevents that. The Padādi स refers to those verbs which in the Dhātupāṭha are taught with a प्, and for which a स is substituted. This also is an exception to VIII. 3. 59. Thus अभिसात् । वधिसात् । मधुसात् ॥ So also with Padādi स as वधि सिञ्चति, मधु सिञ्चति ॥

सिचो यङि ॥ ११२ ॥ पदानि ॥ सिचः, यङि ।

वृत्तिः ॥ सिचः सकारस्य यङि परतो मूर्ध्न्यादेशो न भवति ।

112. The प् substitution does not take place in the स् of सिन् of the Intensive.

Thus सेचिच्यते and अभिसेचिच्यते ॥

Q.—The स of the reduplicate should be changed into प् by VIII. 3. 65, in अभिसेचिच्यते, and the स of the root should be changed into प् by VIII. 3. 64. Because सिन् is one of the roots taught in VIII. 3. 65, and therefore, as this

1648

पल्लव CHANGE.

[BK VIII. CH. III §. 116]

latter rule prevents the operation of VIII. 3. 111 i. e. पादादि स so far as it goes, so it would prevent also the operation of this rule and the form ought to be अभिषेक्षयेत्ति?

*Ans.*—The प ordained by VIII. 3. 65 prevents only the operation of पादादि स of VIII. 3. 111, and not the स of this rule. Therefore the present prohibition is of universal application.

Why do we say in the Intensive. Observe अभिषिपिशति ॥

सेधतेगेतौ ॥ ११३ ॥ पदानि ॥ सेधतः, गतौ ।

वृत्तिः ॥ गतौ वर्तमानस्य सेधतः सकारस्य मूर्धन्यादेशो न भवति ।

113. The स of the verb सेध is not changed to प when the meaning is that of moving.

Thus अभिसेधयति गाः, परिसेधयति गाः ॥ This is an exception to VIII. 3. 65.

Why do we say 'when meaning to drive'? Observe शिष्यमकार्यान्मति-षेधयति ॥ Here the sense is that of preventing or prohibiting.

प्रतिस्तन्धनिस्तन्धौ च ॥ ११४ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रतिस्तन्ध-निस्तन्धौ, च ।

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रतिस्तन्ध निस्तन्ध इत्येतौ मूर्धन्यप्रतिपधाय निपात्यते ।

114. The words प्रतिस्तन्ध and निस्तन्ध are anomalous.

In these words the स is not changed to प, though so required by VIII. 3. 67.

सोढः ॥ ११५ ॥ पदानि ॥ सोढः ।

वृत्तिः ॥ सहित्यं सोढमृतो गृह्यते तस्य सकारस्य मूर्धन्यादेशो न भवति ।

115. The स of सोढ form of the root सह is not changed to प ॥

As परिसोढः, परिसोढम्, परिसोढव्यम् ॥ This is an exception to VIII. 3. 70.

Why do we say 'when सह assumes the form of सोढ' ॥ Observe परि-पहते, विपहते ॥

स्तम्भुसिवुसहां चडि ॥ ११६ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्तम्भु-सिवु-सहाम्, चडि ।

वृत्तिः ॥ स्तम्भु सिवु सह इत्येतेषां चडि परतः सकारस्य मूर्धन्यादेशो न भवति ।

वर्त्तिकः ॥ स्तम्भु सिवुसहां चाड उपसर्गारिति वक्तव्यम् ।

116. The प change does not take place in the reduplicated Aorist of the roots स्तम्भ, सिव and सह ॥

The root स्तम्भ required प change by VIII. 3. 67, and the roots सिव and सह by VIII. 3. 70. Thus पर्यतस्तम्भम्, अभ्यतस्तम्भम् ॥ सिवः—पर्यसीपिवत्, न्यसीपिवत् ॥ सहः—पर्यसीपिहत्, न्यसीपिहत् ॥

BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 119]

षष्ठ RULE.

1649

*Vārt* :—This prohibition refers to the ष change that is caused by an Upasarga and not to the reduplicate change, as we have illustrated in the above example.

सुनोतेः स्वसनोः ॥ ११७ ॥ पदानि ॥ सुनोतेः, स्व-सनोः ।

वृत्तिः ॥ सुनोतेः सकारस्य मूर्धन्यादेशो न भवति । स्वसन्ति च परतः ।

117. स् of सु (सुनोति) is not changed to ष् in the Future, Conditional and Desiderative.

Thus :—अभिसोध्यति, परिसोध्यति, अभ्यसोध्यत्, पर्यसोध्यत् ॥

What example will you give under Desiderative? सुसुपति ॥ This is not a valid example, for by VIII. 3. 61, the reduplicate will not be changed here. Then we shall give the example अभिसुसुपति ॥ This is not also a proper example, for it is governed by the restrictive rule of VIII. 3. 64. Then this is the example अभिसुसुः, निःसुस् derived from the desiderative root अभिसुसुपति by the affix बिष् ॥ Here the desiderative affix सन् is not changed to ष् (VIII. 3. 61) and therefore the second स would have been changed to ष् as it comes after a reduplicate.

Why do we say before स्य and सन् ॥ Observe सुपाय ॥

सदिच्चञ्जोः परस्य लिटि ॥ ११८ ॥ पदानि ॥ सदि-च्चञ्जोः, परस्य, लिटि ।

वृत्तिः ॥ सदि-च्चञ्ज इत्येतयोर्द्वान्नोलिटि परतः सकारस्य परस्य मूर्धन्यो न भवति ।

118. The स् of सद् and च्चंज after the reduplicate in the Perfect is not changed to ष् ॥

In the Perfect, when these words are reduplicated, there are two स's, as ससाव and सस्वज ॥ After a preposition, the first स will be changed to ष, but not so the second. Thus अभिषसाव, परिषसाव, निषसाव, विषसाव, परिषस्वजः, परिषस्वजति, परिषस्वजिरे, अभिषस्वज ॥ The nasal of स्वज is elided though here, the लिट् affix is not किंतु, because it ends in a compound vowel (VI. 4. 24), (I. 2. 5 and 6).

The word स्वज does not occur in the sūtra, but has been inserted in it by the author of Kāśikā from the following Vārtika :—सदा लिटि प्रतिषेधे स्वजं रूपसंख्यानं कर्तव्यम् ॥

निव्यभिभ्योऽव्यवाये वा छन्दसि ॥ ११९ ॥ पदानि ॥ नि-वि-अभिभ्यः, अह-व्यवाये, वा, छन्दसि ।

वृत्तिः ॥ नि वि अभि इत्येतेभ्य उपसर्गेभ्य उत्तरस्य सकारस्याऽव्यवाये छन्दसि विषये मूर्धन्यादेशो न भवति वा ।

119. The ष is optionally substituted in the Chhandas after the prepositions नि, वि and अभि, when the augment अह intervenes.

1650

यत्र RULE.

[BK. VIII. CH. III. §. 119]

Thus नयपीत् or नसीदत् पिता नः; व्यपीत्; or व्यसीदत् पिता नः, अभ्यपीत् or अभ्यसीदत् ॥

The anuvritti of सद् and स्वंज्ञ is not to be read into this sutra. It is, in fact, a general rule and applies to verbs other than these two. As व्यस्तीत्, न्यदीत्, अभ्यदीत् or अभ्यस्तीत् ॥

ॐ ।

## अथ अष्टमाध्यायस्य चतुर्थः पादः ।

# BOOK EIGHTH.

# CHAPTER FOURTH.

रवाञ्च्यां नो णः समानपदे ॥ १ ॥ पदानि ॥ रवाञ्च्याम्, नः, णः, समानपदे ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ रैषपकाराभ्यामुत्तरस्य नकारस्य णकारादेशो भवति, समानपदस्थौ चैत्रिमित्तनिमित्तिनो भवतः ।
वात्तिकम् ॥ ऋवर्णोश्चेति वक्तव्यम् ॥

1. After र् and ष्, the ष् is the substitute of न्, when they occur as component letters of the same word.

These letters must be parts of the same pada or word, one being the 'occasion' for the application of the rule as regards the other. As आस्तीर्णम्, विस्तीर्णम्, अवगुर्णम् ॥ So also after ष्; as, कृष्णाति, पुष्णाति, मुष्णाति ॥

The letter ष् is included in this aphorism for the sake of subsequent sutras; for न् will be changed into ष् when preceded by ष् by rule 41 of this Chapter, as well.

Why do we say "when occurring in the same word?" Observe अग्नि-र्नयति, वायुर्नयति ॥

Vārt:—So also after the letter ऋ ॥ As तिसृणाम्, चतसृणाम्, मातृणाम्, पितृणाम् ॥

This vārtika may well be dispensed with: because the र् in the sutra is the common sound र् which we perceive both in र् and ऋ; and so the र् will denote both the vowel ऋ and the consonant र्. See contra. VIII. 2. 42. Obj. But if even this be so, the letter ऋ has three parts, its first part is a vowel, in the middle is the र् sound of a quarter mātrā, and a vowel sound at the end. This vowel-sound will intervene between the र्-sound and the subsequent न्, and will prevent the application of the sutra, hence the vārtika is valid?

Ans. This vowel-sound will be no intervention, because it will be included in the exception ऋ of the next sutra. Obj. The vowel-sound at the end of ऋ is not a full vowel of one mātrā, but is of half-mātrā, being only a fragment of ऋ, and hence is not included in the pratyāhāra ऋ, it has no separate

21

1652

ण CHANGE.

[Bk. VIII. Ch. IV. § 3]

स्थान or प्रवृत्त or homogeneity with any vowel. Hence this vowel-sound will prevent the application of this rule. Ans. The ण change, however, does take place in spite of such intervention of a fragment of a letter, as we know from the jñāpaka of VIII. 4. 39. In the kshubhnādi list there we find नूनमन as an exception, implying that न is generally changed to ण after such a fragmentary interposition. Or we may take नूनमन as a jñāpaka, that after the letter क् also the ण change takes place.

अहकुप्ताङ्गुन्मध्यवायेपि ॥ २ ॥ पदानि ॥ अह-कु-पु-आङ्-नुम-ध्यवाये, अपि ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ अह कु पु आङ् नुम इयेतैर्व्यवायेपि रेफपकाराभ्यामुत्तरस्य नकारस्य णकार आदिशो भवति ।

2. The substitute ण takes the place of न, even when a vowel, or य, व, ह or a guttural, or a labial, or the pre-position आ, or the augment नुम intervenes, causing separation.

The pratyāhāra अह stands for vowels and the letters ह य व र. Thus करणम्, हरणम्, किरिणा, गिरिणा, कुरुणा, गुरुणा &c.

The कु means all the gutturals, e. g. अक्रेण, मूर्खेण, गर्गेण, अर्पेण ॥

The पु means all the labials, e. g. इर्वेण, रेफेण, गर्गेण, चर्मेण, वर्मेण ॥

The आङ् means the particle आः e. g. पर्याणञ्चम् from न (VIII. 2. 34) निरा-णञ्चम् (cf VIII. 4. 14). The particle आ is a vowel and so included in अह pratyāhāra. Its specification in the sūtra shows that the restriction of the rule to the letters occurring in the same word, does not apply in the case of आङ्, in which case the rule applies to letters separated by another word.

So also when the anusvāra separates the letters e. g. वृहणम्, वृहणीयम् ॥

It is from the root वृहिवृङ्गी, the नुम is added, because the root is वृहिन (VII. 1. 58) and न् changed to anusvāra by VIII. 3. 24. Q. Well the intervention is here by Anusvāra and not नुम, why is then नुम taken in the sūtra?

The word नुम in the sūtra refers to anusvāra, and must be taken co-extensive with it. Otherwise the rule would not apply to words like वृहणं from वृहं वृहं हिंसाये ॥ Here the anusvāra is not the substitute of the augment नुम but an original anusvāra. Even where there is an augment नुम, but where it is not changed into anusvāra, the rule does not apply. As मेन्यनम्, मेन्यनीयम् from वृहिः श्रोणनायेः ॥

The rule will apply even when these letters are combined in any possible way, or occur singly. As अक्रेण, here a guttural and a vowel i. e. 2 letters come between र and न ॥ See VIII. 3. 58 in the case of ष ॥

पूर्वपदात्संशायामगः ॥ ३ ॥ पदानि ॥ पूर्वपदात्, संशायाम्, अगः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पूर्वपदस्याभिमितादुत्तरस्य नकारवर्जिताद् नकारस्य णकार आदिशो भवति संशायां विषये ।

3. So also, न् is replaced by ण, when the letter occasioning the substitution, occurs in the first member of a compound, and the whole compound is a Name, provided that the first member does not end with the letter ग ॥

BK. VIII. CH. IV §. 4]

ण CHANGE.

1653

As हुणसः, बाईणसः (a kind of antelope), खरणसः, धूर्पणखा ॥ See V. 4. 118 and IV. 1. 58.

Why do we say “when a Name”? Observe, चर्मनासिकः ॥

Why do we say when ‘not ending in the letter ण’? Observe; क्षणयनम् ॥

Some say, that this sūtra is a नियम or a restrictive rule, and not a विधि or original enunciation, so that the substitution takes place, only when the word is a *Name*, and not otherwise. A compound is one word or समानपद, though composed of two or more words or पद ॥ Therefore by VIII. 4. 11 the न will always be changed into ण when preceded by र or ष. But the present sūtra restricts its scope, to those cases only, when the compound denotes a *Name*, as not in चर्मनासिकः ॥ The word पूर्वपद is a relative term and connotes an उत्तरपद ॥ The present sūtra therefore applies to those cases where the र or ष is in the पूर्वपद, and न occurs in the उत्तरपद ॥ It therefore, does not apply to तादृश words, nor when both the letters occur in the पूर्वपद ॥ In the case of a Taddhita, there is a पूर्वपद, but there is no properly speaking उत्तरपद ॥ Thus खरपस्यापयं=खारपायणः (IV.1.99). Here the affix अयन is equivalent to अपयं, and खरप is the Pūrvapada. But the affix अयन not being a Pada, we cannot call it an uttara pada. Hence न will be changed into ण though खारपायण is not an Appellative but a generic term. So also मातृभोगाय हितः=मातृभोगीणः with ख affix. Similarly in करणविधः, the words र and न both occur in the Pūrvapada and are not affected by this rule, but by the general rule VIII. 4. 1. So also the proviso relating to ण, only prohibits the change of न into ण, but does not prohibit the restrictive character of this sūtra.

According to others, this sūtra is an original enunciation or a Vidhi rule, and not a Niyama rule. They say that the word समानपद in VIII. 4. 1 is equivalent to नित्यं पदं i. e. a word integral and indivisible into component words. In other words, समानपद means, a ‘simple-word’. The present sūtra therefore enunciates a new rule for a “compound-word”. For in a compound or समास, there being a division of पूर्वपद and an उत्तरपद, we cannot say that a compound is a समानपद or indivisible word. Hence this sūtra is a विधि ॥

The sūtra should be thus divided:—पूर्वपदात् संज्ञायाम् one sūtra, and अयः another. So that every rule relating to ण change would be debarred with regard to ण intervention.

वनं पुरगामिश्रकासिश्रकाशारिकाकोटराग्रेभ्यः ॥ ४ ॥ पदानि ॥ वनम्, पुरगा, मिश्रका-सिश्रका-शारिका-कोटराग्रेभ्यः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पूर्वपदात्संज्ञायामिति वच्यते । पुरगा मिश्रका सिश्रका शारिका कोटरा अये इत्येतेभ्यः पूर्वपदेभ्य उत्तरस्य वननकारस्य णकारविधो भवति संज्ञायां विधये ।

4. The न of वन, is changed into ण, when preceded by the words puragā, miśrakā, sidhrakā, śarikā, koṭarā, and

[ Bk. VIII. Ch. IV. §. 6

agre, as first members of the compound, and the whole compound is a name.

The words पूर्वपदात् and संज्ञायाम् of the last sūtra, are to be read into this aphorism. Thus पुरगावणम्, निश्चकावणम्, सिघ्रकावणम्, कोटरावणम्, अमेवणम् (II. 2. 31) शारिकावणम् ॥

The lengthening of the finals in the above is by VI. 3. 117. Though the word अमेवण is not a Name, yet the rule VI. 3. 9, applies to it and the case-affix is not elided, because it is so read in Rājadantādi list (II. 2. 31).

The substitution of ण for न would have taken place by the preceding rule. The separate enunciation of the rule with regard to the word वन, shows that this is a restrictive or नियम rule. The न of वन is changed into ण, when preceded by these words only and no other. Thus कुबेरवन्, शतधारवन्, असिपववन् ॥

प्रनिरन्तःशरेशु-लक्ष्य-प्रकार्य-खदिर-पीयू-शाञ्च्यो-संज्ञायामपि ॥ ५ ॥ पदानि ॥
प्र-निर-अन्तर-शर-इक्षु-प्रक्ष-आम्र-कार्य-खदिर-पीयू-शाञ्च्यः संज्ञायां, अपि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्र निर अन्तर शर इक्षु प्रक्ष आम्र कार्य खदिर पीयूशा इत्येत्य उत्तरस्य वननकारस्य संज्ञायाम् संज्ञायामपि णकारादेशो भवति ।

5. The न of वन is replaced by ण, even when the compound is not a Name, when it is preceded by the words pra, nir, antar, śara, ikshu, plaksha, āmra, kārshya, khadira, and pīyūkshā.

Thus प्रवणे यष्टम्; निर्वणे प्रतिधीयते, अन्तर्वणे, शरवणम्, इक्षुवणम्, प्रक्षवणम्, आम्रवणम्, कार्यवणम्, खदिरवणम् and पीयूशावणम् ॥

The words प्रवणं and निर्वणं are प्रादिः compounds. अन्तवणं is an Avyayī-bhāva in the sense of a case-affix. The rest are Genitive compounds.

विभाषीषधिवनस्पतिञ्च्यः ॥ ६ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा ओषधि-वनस्पतिञ्च्यः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ ओषधिवाचि यद्युर्वपत् वनस्पतिवाचि तत्स्याभिनिष्तादुत्तरस्य वननकारस्य णकार आदेशो भवति विभाषा ।

वार्तिकः ॥ द्वाशरञ्चशरेभ्य इति वक्तव्यम् ॥ वा० ॥ इरिकादिभ्यः प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥

Kārika फली वनस्पतिञ्च्यो वृक्षाः पुष्पफलोपगाः ।

ओषधः फलपाकान्ता लता गुणाभ्य वीहधः ॥

6. The न of वन is optionally replaced by ण, when the cause of change occurs in the first member of the compound and which denotes a perennial herb or a forest tree.

When the pūrvapada is a word denoting ओषधि or a perennial herb, or denoting a वनस्पति or a tree, and it has a change-producing letter, then the न of वन is replaced by ण ॥ This is an optional rule. Thus :—वृवविनम् or वृवविनम्;

मूर्खावणम् or मूर्खावणम् ॥ Here मूर्खा and मूर्खा are names of ओषधि ॥ Similarly शिरीष-वनं or शिरीषवणम्; बकरीवणं or बकरीवनं ॥

*Vārt*:—This rule applies when the first word is a dissyllabic or trisyllabic word. Therefore the change does not occur in देवदारुवनम्; भद्रदारुवनम् ॥

*Vārt*:—Prohibition should be stated with regard to the words हारका &c. As हरिकावनम्, तिमिरकावनम् ॥

Though there is a distinction, botanically speaking, between a वृक्ष and a वनस्पति also; yet in this sūtra, the word वनस्पति includes वृक्ष also.

*Kārika*:—Technically speaking वनस्पति is a tree that bears fruit apparently without a flower, as a fig tree udumbara. वृक्ष is a tree that bears both flower and fruit, ओषधि is an annual herb, that dies after the ripening of the fruit, and creepers and tubercles are called वीरुधः ॥

अहोऽदन्तात् ॥ ७ ॥ पदानि ॥ अहः, अदन्तात् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अघन्तं यमूर्खपर्वं तत्स्थाभिनिषादुत्तरस्याहो नकारस्य णकार आवेशो भवति ।

7. The ण is the substitute of न of अहन्, when it is preceded by a word ending in अ, having in it a letter capable of producing the change.

Thus पूर्वाह्नः “fore-noon”; अपराह्नः “after-noon”.

Why do we say “ending in अ”? Observe, निरहः, दुरहः ॥

The word अहः is substituted for अहन् by V. 4. 88. The word अहः being used in the sūtra as ending in अ, the rule does not apply to other words. Thus वीर्याह्नी बारत् ॥ The word अहः in the sūtra is in the nominative case, and should not be construed as the genitive of अहन्, because all sthānins are exhibited in Nominatives as, वनं (VIII. 4. 4), वाहनं (VIII. 4. 8), यानं &c. The compounding takes place by II. 2. 1, then is added the samāsānta affix टच् (V. 4. 91), and अहः substitution by V. 4. 88. The word वीर्याह्नी is a Bahuvrīhi compound and not a Tatpurusha, and hence the affix टच् does not apply to it. The feminine क्रीप् is added by IV. 1. 28, there is elision of अ of अहन् by VI. 4. 134.

वाहनमाहितात् ॥ ८ ॥ पदानि ॥ वाहनम्, आहितात् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आहितवाक्ति यमूर्खपर्वं तत्स्थाभिनिषादुत्तरस्य वाहननकारस्य णकार आवेशो भवति ।

Thus इक्षुवाहणम् ‘a sugar-cart’. बारवाहणम् “a reed-cart”. बर्मवाहणम् ‘a hay-cart’.

The thing which being placed on a cart is carried, is called आह्नि ॥

Why do we say “denoting the thing carried”. Observe शशिवाहणम् “a vehicle belonging to Dākshi”.

The word वाहन is formed by adding ल्यूट to वह, and lengthening of the penultimate is valid by the nipātana of this sūtra.

पानं देशे ॥ ९ ॥ पदानि ॥ पानम्, देशे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पाननकारस्य पूर्वपदस्थाश्रितितादुत्तरस्य देशाभिधानं नकार आदेशो भवति ।

The word पान is formed by the affix ल्यूट III. 3. 113. Thus क्षीरपाणा उशीनराः = क्षीरपाणं येषां 'the milk-drinking Usinaras'. सुरापाणाः प्राच्याः 'the wine-drinking Prāchyas'. सौवीरपाणा बाहूंकाः 'the sauvira-drinking Bāhlikas'. कषायपाणा गान्धाराः &c.

Why do we say "when denoting a country"? Observe दक्षिणानं the drink of the Dākshis.

The words उशीनर and the rest are applied to persons also through the medium of being country-names.

वृत्तिः ॥ वेत्ति वेत्ति । प्रतिपदिकान्ते नुभिर्मक्ती च यो नकारस्तस्य पूर्वपदस्थाश्रितितादुत्तरस्य वा नकार आदेशो भवति ।

11. Optionally ण is substituted for न when it stands at the end of a Nominal-stem (Prātipadika) or is the augment नुभ or is न of a case-affix, (when the cause of change occurs in the first member of the compound).

ण CHANGE.

1657

Thus, to take the case a प्रतिपदिकान्त first. मायवापिनी or मायवापिनी from मायवापिनु 'māsha-sowing' formed by णिनि under III. 2. 81.

To take the example of a नुम् augment मायवापाणि or मायवापानि, श्रीहिवापाणि or श्रीहिवापानि nom. pl. neut. The. augment नुम् is here added by VII. 1. 72 from मायान् वपयन्ति = मायवाप with कर्मिण अण्, the plural शि is added by VII. 1. 20, and then नुम् ॥

To take the विभक्ति or case-termination, मायवापेण or मायवापेन, श्रीहिवापेण or श्रीहिवापेन ॥

• The word प्रतिपदिकान्त means 'final in a Prātipadika'. But here it means 'final in a prātipadika which is a second member, of compound, the first member containing the cause of change'. Therefore the change does not take place in गर्भाणां भगिनी = गर्भभगिनी 'the sister of Garga'. But गर्भभगिनी if the word is derived from गर्भभग: 'the share of Garga', with the adjectival affix इन्द्र, feminine इनी, meaning, 'enjoying the share of Garga.' In this case, like the word मातृ-भोगीण: 'fit to be possessed by a mother': the change will invariably take place.

The word मायवापिणी or 'नी' is to be understood to have a final नृ, the affix being added afterwards in accordance with the following maxim :—(II. 2. 19). 'It should be stated that Gatis, Kārakas, and Upapadas are compounded with bases that end with krit-affixes, before a case termination or a feminine affix has been added to the latter' गतिकारकोपपदानां कृतिः सह समासवचनं प्राक् ध्रुवुस्तेः ॥

Therefore the composition takes place first with the word ending in the krit affix, as मायवापिनु (माय + वापिनु), and thus the second term वापिनु is a Prātipadika which ends in नृ, and so the rule is applied to it, when the feminine affix is added.

Similarly नुम् is not considered as the end portion of the second member of the compound, but as the end-portion of the full compound word.

Vārt:—Prohibition must be stated of the words युवा &c. As आर्ययुता (VI. 4. 133 vocalisation), क्षत्रिययुता ॥ प्रपक्वानि is a gati-samas, दीर्घायु शरण् ॥

एकाजुत्तरपदे णः ॥ १२ ॥ पदानि ॥ एकाच्, उत्तरपदे, णः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ एकाजुत्तरपदे यस्य स एकाजुत्तरपदः । तस्मिन्नेकाजुत्तरपदसमासे प्रतिपदिकान्तनुम्निमित्तिपु पूर्वपदस्थाभिमित्तातुत्तरस्थ नकारस्थ नकार आवेशो भवति ।

12. In a compound, the second member of which is a monosyllable, there is ण in the room of न of the second member, provided that the न is at the end of a prātipadika, or is the augment नुम्, or occurs in a vibhakti; and when the first member contains a cause of change.

Thus वृचहनी and वृचहण: 'the Vṛtra-killer'. क्षीरपाणि 'Drinkers of milk': धुरापाणि 'drinkers of wine': being examples of नुम् VII. 3. 88, क्षीरपेण and धुरापेण are examples of case-terminations.

[BK. VIII. CH. IV. §. 14]

Why the letter ण is repeated in this sūtra, while its anuvṛtti was understood from the context? It is repeated in order to show that this is not an optional rule, but an obligatory rule. In fact, it shows that the anuvṛtti of वा 'optional' ceases, and does not extend further.

कुमति च ॥ १३ ॥ पदानि ॥ कुमति, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कर्पणवति चोत्तरपदे प्रातिपदिकान्तदुच्चिभक्तिपु पूर्वपदस्याश्रितितादुत्तरस्य नकारस्य णकारादेशो भवति ।

13. In a compound, the second member of which contains a guttural, there is ण in the room of न, that follows anything which standing in the prior member is qualified to cause the change, provided the न be at the end of a prātipadika, or be the augment नुम, or occur in a vibhakti.

If the second part of a compound contains a letter of the class क्, the change is obligatory, even though the second part be not monosyllabic. As वस्त्रयुगिणी, वस्त्रयुगिणः, स्वर्गकामिणी, वृक्षगामिणी ॥ नुमः—वस्त्रयुगाणि, खरयुगाणि ॥ विभक्तिः—वस्त्रयुगेण, खरयुगेण ॥

The word वस्त्रयुगिणी is a compound of वस्त्र with युगिन् (the affix इति is added first to युग and then the word so formed is compounded with vastra). Thus the न becomes प्रातिपदिकान्त i.e. it becomes the final of a Nominal-stem, which stands as a second member in a compound.

उपसर्गादसमासेऽपि णोपदेशस्य ॥ १४ ॥ पदानि ॥ उपसर्गात्, अ-समासे, अपि, णोपदेशस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ण उपदेशे यस्यासौ णोपदेशः । णोपदेशस्य धातोयो नकारः तस्य उपसर्गस्याश्रितितादुत्तरस्य णकारादेशो भवति असमासेपि समासेपि ।

14. Of a root which has ण in its original enunciation, when it comes after a cause of such change standing in an upasarga, even though the word be not a samāsa, the न is changed into ण ॥

The word णोपदेश means a root which is enunciated in the Dhātupāṭha with an initial ण ॥ Thus प्रणमति 'he bows'. परिणमति, प्रणायकः 'a leader' परिणामकः &c.

Why do we say 'after an Upasarga'? Observe प्रणायकः=प्रगता नायका अस्माद् देशात् 'a country without a leader'. Here the word प्र is not an upasarga, but a mere nipāta. See I. 4. 57, 58 and 59. In fact, प्र is upasarga here with regard to गत understood, and not with regard to नी ॥

Why do we say 'even when it is not a compound?' Because by context, the anuvṛtti of the word पूर्वपद, which is current throughout this sub-

BK. VIII. CH. IV. §. 17 ]

जन्म CHANGE.

1659

division, would have been understood in this sūtra also, and the rule would have applied to samāsas only, for there only we have pūrvapada. By using the word असंगति it is shown that the adhikāra of pūrvapada ceases, and the rule applies to non-compounds also where there is no पूर्वपद ॥

Why do we say “having न in Upadeśa”? Observe मनवृत्ति, मनवृत्ति, मनवृत्ति ॥ For the root नः is recited in Dhātupāṭha with न ॥ There are eight such roots नः, नाः, नाः, नाः, नः, नः, नः ॥ See VI. I. 65.

हिनुमीना ॥ १५ ॥ पदानि ॥ हिनुमीना, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हिनु मीना इत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत

15. The न of हिनु and मीना is changed into ण, when coming after an upasarga containing in it a cause of change.

Thus प्रहिणाति, प्रहिणुतः, प्रमीणाति, प्रमीणीतः ॥ The root हि belongs to Svādi class of verbs and takes the vikaraṇa तु technically इतु; and the root मी belongs to Kṛyādi class which takes the vikaraṇa भा ॥ In the sūtra the verbs are shown with the vikaraṇas affixed. Under certain circumstances the forms of the vikaraṇa is changed from तु to मी and ना to मी, but the rule still applies, because the substitute of an अच् or vowel is like the principal. See I. I. 57.

आनि लोट् ॥ १६ ॥ पदानि ॥ आनि, लोट् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपसर्गादिति वर्तते । आनित्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्य

16. The न of आनि, the affix of the Imperative, 1st Person, is changed into ण when it follows a letter competent to cause such a change standing in an Upasarga.

The word आनि is the termination of the Imperative. Thus प्रबपाणि, प-रिबपाणि, प्रबपाणि, परिबपाणि ॥

Why do we say ‘the Imperative’? Observe प्रबपाणि मांसानि ॥ Here आनि is the neuter plural termination, and the word means प्रकृष्टा बपा बेधु, तानि ॥

According to Padamanjari, the employment of the word लोट् in the sūtra is redundant. For without it also आनि would have meant the Imperative affix, and not the Neuter termination, on the maxim of अयवेद् महणे &c. Moreover in the noun प्रबपाणि, प्र is not an upasarga at all, on the maxim बत् क्रियायुक्ताः प्राकृष्ट-स्तं प्रति गति-उपसर्ग-संज्ञे भवतः ॥

नेगैदनदपतपदधुमास्यतिहन्तियातिवातिद्रातिप्सातिवपतिवहतिशाम्यतिचिनोति दैन्धिषु च ॥ १७ ॥ पदानि ॥ नेः, गद-नद-पत-पद-धु-मा-स्यति-हन्ति-याति-याति-द्राति-प्साति-वपति-वहति-शाम्यति-चिनोति-दैन्धिषु, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ निरित्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्येत्य

17. The ण is the substitute of न of the prefix नि, following a cause for such change standing in an upasarga, when these verbs follow, gad 'to speak', nad 'to be happy', pat 'to fall', pad 'to go', the ghu verbs, mā 'to measure', sho 'to destroy', han 'to kill', yā 'to go', vā 'to blow', drā 'to flee', psā 'to eat', vap 'to weave', vah 'to bear', śam 'to be tranquil', chi 'to collect', and dih 'to anoint'.

Thus

[tbl-1.md](tbl-1.md)

[tbl-2.md](tbl-2.md)

[tbl-3.md](tbl-3.md)

शेषे विभाषाकखादावपान्तउपदेशे ॥ १८ ॥ पदानि ॥ शेषे, विभाषा, अकखादौ, अपान्ते, उपदेशे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नैरिति वर्तते उपसर्गादिति च । अककारखकारादिरपकारान्तच उपदेशे यो धातुः शेषस्तस्मिन्नरत उपसर्गस्याभिमितादुत्तरस्य नैनकारस्य विभाषा णकार आदेशो भवति ।

18. In the remaining verbs, optionally the न of नि is replaced by ण, when it is preceded by an upasarga competent to cause the change; provided that, in the original enunciation, the verb has not an initial क or ख, nor ends with ष ॥

The words नः and उपसर्गात् are understood in the sūtra. The word शेषे means verbs other than those mentioned last. Thus प्रणिपति or प्रणिपति, प्रणिमिति or प्रणिमिति ॥

BK. VIII. CH. IV. § 20 ]

जन्म CHANGE.

1661

Why do we say अकस्वातौ “not beginning with क or ख”? Observe प्रति
करोति, प्रतिपादति ॥ Here there is no change.

Why do we say अघान्तः “not ending in ख”? Observe प्रतिपिनति ॥

Why do we say उपदेशे “in original enunciation”? So that the prohibition may apply to forms like प्रतिपादक, प्रतिपादक, प्रतिपेक्ष्यति (VIII. 2. 41). Here
ककार &c, do not begin with क or ख nor does पिष् end with ख but with क (VIII.
2. 41) but in the Dhātupāṭha the verb क and खद् begin with क and ख and
पिष् ends with ख, and hence the rule will not apply. So also in प्रतिपेदा and
प्रतिपेक्ष्यति from the root विश्व ॥ Here though the verb now ends with ख by
VIII. 2. 36, yet in the original enunciation or Dhātupāṭha, it ends with ख ॥

अनितेः ॥ १६ ॥ पदानि ॥ अनितेः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अनितेनकारस्योपसर्गस्याश्रितमिचाडुत्तरस्य जकारादेशो भवति ।

19. The न of the verb अन् ‘to breathe’, is changed into ण, when preceded by an upasarga competent to produce the change.

Thus प्र+अनिति=प्राणिति ‘he breathes’. प्राणिति ॥ For हृद augment, see VII. 2. 76.

अन्तः ॥ २० ॥ पदानि ॥ अन्तः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपसर्गस्याश्रितमिचाडुत्तरस्यानितेनकारस्य पङ्क्ते वर्तमानस्य जकारादेशो भवति ।

20. The न of अन् is changed into ण, when it is preceded by an upasarga competent to produce the change, provided it occurs at the end of a pada.

As हे प्राण् ! हे प्राण् ! ॥ This rule is an exception to VIII. 4. 37 sub, by which final न् in a pada is not changed into ण ॥ The word अन्तः in the sūtra is to be understood to be equivalent to पङ्क्तः, and the rule applies when the word is in the vocative case.

According to some अन्तः is taken to be a part of the last sūtra, and has the meaning of ‘proximity’. That is the न is changed to ण, if the र is not separated from the न् by more than one letter. Therefore there is no change in परि+अनिति=पङ्क्तिनि ॥ In this view, another अन्त should be taken for the sake of final न्, in हे प्राण् ॥

According to others the form पङ्क्तिनि is valid, and they do not connect अन्तः with the last sūtra.

The word प्राण् is a किंचि formed word, and the न् final is not elided in the Vocative Singular because of the prohibition of VIII. 2. 8; in every other place, when the न् is padānta, it would be dropped; and therefore the illustration is given with Vocative singular, which alone satisfies the requirements of this sūtra.

1662

जन्म RULE.

[Bk. VIII. Ch. IV. § 23]

उभौ साभ्यासस्य ॥ २१ ॥ पदानि ॥ उभौ, साभ्यासस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ साभ्यासस्यानितेरुपसर्गस्याश्रितमितादुत्तरस्योभयोनेकारयोगकार आदिशो भवति ।

21. Both the न s are changed into ण in the reduplicated forms of the verb अन्, when preceded by an upasarga competent to cause the change.

Thus in the Desiderative प्राणिणिपति and Aorist of the Causative प्राणिणन्, and so also प्राणिणिपति and प्राणिणन् ॥

If the maxim पूर्ववर्त्तिरुद्धिमहिर्यचने be not applied here; then we have the following dilemma in, प्रानि+स+ति ॥ Here the affix सन् requires reduplication, and the present sutra requires ण change of न ॥ The णत्व being asiddha, the reduplication being made first, we have प्राणिनि+स+ति, and then the reduplicate ण intervenes between the cause प्र and the root-न् of नि, and so this न would not be changed to ण ॥ If however the above maxim be applied, we first apply the णत्व rule, as प्राणि+स+ति, and then reduplicate णि; and we get the form प्राणिणिपति even without this sutra.

If we could get this form by the application of the above maxim, where is the necessity of the present sutra? The sutra is necessary in order to indicate that the above maxim is *anitya* or not of universal application. And because it is *anitya*, that the form ओजवत् is evolved by reduplicating हन् (See VIII. 2. 1).

हन्तेरत्पूर्वस्य ॥ २२ ॥ पदानि ॥ हन्तेः,अत्,पूर्वस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अकारपूर्वस्य हन्तिनकारस्य उपसर्गस्याश्रितमितादुत्तरस्य णकार आदिशो भवति ।

22. The न, when preceded by अ, in the root हन्, is changed to ण, when the verb is preceded by a preposition competent to cause the change.

Thus प्रहण्यते, परिहण्यते, प्रहणनम्, परिहणनम् ॥

Why do we say अत्पूर्वस्य 'when preceded by अ'? When अ is elided, the change does not take place. As प्रहन्ति, परिहन्ति (VI. 4. 98, and VIII. 3. 54).

Why do we say अन् 'preceded by *short* अ'? Observe पर्यधानि and प्रधानि, the Aorist of हन् by the affix चिण् (III. 1. 60) प्रहन्+चिण्=प्रधन्+चिण् (VIII. 3. 54) = प्रधन्+चिण् (VIII. 2. 116) = प्रधानि 'he killed'. Here न being preceded by the long अ is not changed.

वमोवो ॥ २३ ॥ पदानि ॥ वमोः, वा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वकारनकारयोः परतो हन्तिनकारस्योपसर्गस्याश्रितमितादुत्तरस्य वा णकारादिशो भवति ।

23. Optionally when व or म follow, the न of *han* is changed to ण, when preceded by an upasarga competent to cause the change.

Thus प्रहण्वः, परिहण्वः, or प्रहन्: and परिहन्: प्रहण्मः or प्रहन्मः परिहण्मः or परिहन्मः ॥

This sutra enjoins an option in certain cases, where it would have been obligatory by the last rule.

BK. VIII. CH. IV. §. 26]

पल्लव RULE.

1663

अन्तरदेशे ॥ २४ ॥ पदानि ॥ अन्तर, अदेशे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अन्तःशब्दादुत्तरस्य हन्तिमकारस्याप्युपस्य णकारादेशो भवति ।

24. The न preceded by short अ of the root हन् is changed into ण, when the root follows the upasarga अन्तर, and the word does not mean a country.

Thus अन्तर्ह्यन्ते and अन्तर्ह्यन्ते ॥

Why do we say “when not meaning a country अदेश?” Observe अन्तर्ह्यन्ती देशः ॥

The phrase अतुपूर्वस्य “preceded by short अ” of sūtra 22 ante, is to be read into this sūtra also. Observe, अन्तर्ह्यन्ति ॥

Why do we say “short अ?” See, अन्तरधाति ॥ The word antar is an upasarga for the purposes of ण change, by the vārtika under I. 4. 65; therefore, it would have caused the ण change by VIII. 4. 22. The present sūtra is made, to show that the change takes place only then, when it does not mean a country.

अयनं च ॥ २५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अयनम्, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अन्तरदेशेऽपि वर्तते । अयननकारस्य चान्तः शब्दादुत्तरस्य णकारादेशो भवति ।

25. The न of अयन is changed to ण, when preceded by the word अन्तर, and the word does not denote a country.

Thus अन्तरयणं शोभनम् ॥ Why do we say “not denoting a country”? Observe अन्तरयनो देशः ॥ This ण change would have taken place by VIII. 4. 29, this special sūtra is for अदेश purposes. The word अयन is formed by लघुद added to अय or इण् ॥

छन्दस्युदवग्रहात् ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ छन्दसि, ऋत-अवग्रहात् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऋकारान्तादवग्रहात्पूर्वपदादुत्तरस्य णकारादेशो भवति छन्दसि विषये ।

26. In the Chhandas, न of a second term is changed into ण, when the prior term ends with a short ऋ even when there is an avagraha or hiatus between the two terms.

In the Veda, न becomes ण, after a ऋ, after which in Padapāṭha, the word appertaining to it is divided. Thus in Pada-pāṭha the words नृणाः &c, are separated, and are read as नृ, नृणाः ॥ The word अवग्रहते = विच्छिद्र पञ्चते, as in Pada-pāṭha. ऋतवग्रहात् means ‘after a short ऋ which is an avagraha’. The ऋ here, of course, means ‘a word ending in ऋ’, because ऋ alone cannot be a pūrvapada. The णत्व took place during saṇhitā, and in Pada reading this ण would not have remained, hence this sūtra.

Why have we used the word avagraha in the sūtra? Because we have already said that the word saṇhitā governs all sūtras of this chapter. So the न is changed to ण in the Saṇhitā state in these; and the ण is retained, when

1664

ण CHANGE.

[BK VIII. CH. IV §. 28]

in the state of avagraha. The word avagraha in the sūtra indicates the scope of the rule. The न is changed to ण after that क् only, which is capable of avagraha, namely that क् which stands at the end of a word (pada), and not that which is in the body of a word. Thus in नृमणाः, पितृयाणम्, the क् is capable of avagraha, as it is at the end of a word नृ or पितृ; but when it is not at the end of a word, it can never become avagraha, and will not produce the ण change.

The word पूर्वपश्चात् is understood here. The word अव्यह means a hiatus or separation. Thus पितृ याणम्, नृमणाः ॥ Here क् is अव्यह ॥ The change of न into ण is effected ordinarily then, when the terms, one containing the cause, and the other न, are in संहिता or conjunction. For the rules of Sandhi and the rules like these can apply only to words in sanhita. The present rule is an exception to it, and here, even when the words are not in संहिता, but there is an actual hiatus between the two, the change still takes place. The word संहिता of VIII. 2. 108, exerts regulating influence upto the end of the Book.

नभ धातुस्थोरुपुण्यः ॥ २७ ॥ पदानि ॥ नः, च, धातुस्थ, उरु, पुण्यः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नस् इत्येतस्य नकारस्य णकारादेशो भवति धातुस्थाविमितादुत्तरस्थोरुपश्चात्पुण्यश्च च्छन्तसि विधये ।

27. In the Chhandas, the न of (the Pronoun) नस् is changed into ण, when it comes after a root having a र or प or after the words उरु and पु (सु) ॥

Thus अनेन रक्षणः (Rig VII. 15. 13) 'O Agni! protect us'. शिक्षा णो अस्मिन् (Rig. VII. 32. 26) 'Teach us this'. उरु:—उरुणस्कृधि (Rig. VIII. 75. 11) पु—अभीषुणः सर्वानाम् (Rig IV. 31. 3). ऊर्ध्व ऊषुणः ऊतये (Rig. I. 36. 13).

The word नस् is here the pronoun नस्, which is the substitute, in certain cases, of अस्मिन् (VIII. 1. 21) and does not mean here the नस् substitute of नासिका ॥ In the next sūtra, however, both नस् are taken. धातुस्थ means 'that which exists in a dhātu', namely र and पु when occurring in a root. The word उरु means the word-form उरु; and पु means पुण्य, and is exhibited with प-change. It does not mean the affix पु of the Locative Plural. Therefore, not here इन्द्रो धता गृहेषु नः ॥ The word रक्षा is the 2nd Person singular, Imperative, the lengthening is by VI. 3. 135. The root शिक्षु has the sense of दान in the Veda. कृधी is 2nd Person sg. Imperative of कृ (VI. 4. 102), the visarga of नः is changed to सु by VIII. 3. 50. In अभिषु there is lengthening by VI. 3. 134: so also in ऊषुणः &c.

उपसर्गाद्वदुलम् ॥ २८ ॥ पदानि ॥ उपसर्गात्, वडुलम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपसर्गस्याविमितादुत्तरस्थ नसो नकारस्य णकारादेशो भवति ।

28. The न of नस् is changed diversely into ण, when it comes after an upasarga having a cause of change.

BK. VIII. CH. IV §. 30 ]

पल्लव RULE.

1665

Thus प्रणः शुद्धः; प्रणः प्रणो राजा ॥ The change does not sometime take, place, as, प्र नो दुःखतम् ॥

By force of the word बहुलम् the rule applies to secular literature also as distinguished from the Chhandas or sacred Vedic text. Thus प्रणः शुद्धः ॥ The word छन्दसि does not govern this sutra.

In प्रणः शुद्धम्, the word नसु is the substitute for नासिका and means 'nose'. See V. 4. 119.

This is not the sutra as given by Pāṇini. His sutra is उपसर्गान्नोत्तरः 'after an Upasarga, the न of नसु when not preceded by or followed by an ओ, is changed into ण्'. There being several objections to this rule, the above rule is substituted as an amendment, in the Mahābhāshya. For ओतुपरः may have two meanings:—(1) ओकारात् परः, that which comes after ओ; (2) ओकारः परोऽस्मात् that which is followed by ओ ॥ In both cases, the rule is objectionable. In the first case, the ण change would be required in प्रनो दुःखतम्; in the second case, there should be no ण change in प्रणोनिर्देवता ॥ In fact, we find in the Vedas प्रणः as well as प्रनः, so also प्रणो as well as प्रनो ॥ Hence the necessity of this amendment.

कृत्यचः ॥ २९ ॥ पदानि ॥ कृति, अच ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कृत्यो यो नकारो ऽच उत्तरस्योपसर्गस्याश्रितादुत्तरस्य णकारादेशो भवति ।
वार्तिकः ॥ कृत्यस्य णले निर्विण्णस्योपसंख्यानं कर्तव्यम् ।

29. The न of a Krit affix, preceded by a vowel, is changed into ण, when it follows an upasarga having the cause of change.

The following are the specific Krit affixes in which this change takes place:—अन ( यु ), मान ( शानच् &c VII. 2. 82 ), अनीय, ( III. 1. 96 ) अनि, ( III. 3. 111 ) इनि ( णिनि III. 2. 78 &c ) and the substitutes of निष्ठा ( VIII. 2. 42 ) ॥

Thus

[tbl-4.md](tbl-4.md)

Why do we say अचः ' preceded by a vowel ?' Observe प्रसुप्तः, परिमुप्तः the Nishthā of सुभु ॥ It is thus formed: सुभु + न = सुभु + न = सुभु + न ( VII. 2. 45, the root सुभु is read as सुभो कौटिल्ये in the dhatūpātha, having an indicatory ओ, thus giving scope to the rule ). सुभु + न = सुभु + न ( VIII. 2. 30 ) = सुभु ॥

Vārt:—The word निर्विण्णः should be enumerated in this place. As निर्विण्णोस्मि खलसंगेन ॥ निर्विण्णोस्मनवासेन ॥

णेविमावा ॥ ३० ॥ पदानि ॥ णेः, विमावा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ण्यन्ताद्यो विहितः कृत्यस्यः तत्स्यस्य नकारोपसर्गस्याश्रितादुत्तरस्य विमावा णकारादेशो भवति

1666

पञ्च RULE.

[ Bk. VIII. Ch. IV. § 32

30. The न of a Krit-affix ordained after a causative verb (प्यन्त), is optionally changed to ण्, when it comes after an upasarga having a cause of change.

Thus प्रयापणम् or प्रयापनम्, परियापणम् or परियापनम्, प्रयाप्यमाणम् or प्रयाप्यमानम्, प्रयापणीयम् or प्रयापनीयम्, अप्रयापणिः or अप्रयापनिः, प्रयापिणी or प्रयापिनी ॥

Why have we used the word विहितं 'ordained' in explaining the sūtra? Because the change takes place, even where the कृत affix does not follow directly after the affix णि; where a third affix such as यक् intervenes. As प्रयाप्यमाणम् ॥ The णि: being in the ablative, under the ordinary rule of interpretation (I. 1. 72), the krit-affix should come immediately after णि.

हलप्रेजुपधात् ॥ ३१ ॥ पदानि ॥ हलः, च, इच्-उपधात् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हलादिषो धातुरिजुपधस्तस्मात्परो यः कृत्स्नयः तत्स्थस्य नकारस्याच् उत्तरस्योपसर्गस्याभिमिच्छादुत्तरस्य विभाषा नकारादिषो भवति ॥

31. A krit-affix, coming after a verb, which begins with a consonant and has a penultimate इच् vowel, changes optionally its न, which is preceded by a vowel, into ण्, when it comes after an upasarga having a cause of change.

The phrase कृत्स्नः is understood here. Thus प्रकोपणम् or प्रकोपनम्, परिकोपणम् or परिकोपनम् ॥

Why do we say हलः 'beginning with a consonant'? Observe प्रेक्षणम् and प्रोक्षणम् where the change is obligatory, under VIII. 4. 29. These are from ईह चेदायाम् and ऊह वितर्के ॥

Why do we say इजुपधात् 'having a penultimate इच् vowel'? Observe प्रवपणम् and परिवपणम्; no option.

By the rule कृत्स्नः the change was obligatory, this rule makes it optional.

The न of the krit-affix must come after a vowel, otherwise there will be no change. See परिमुग्नः

The word हलः in the sūtra should be interpreted as हलादेः, and not as ordinarily 'after what ends in हल्' ॥ For an इजुपधा verb implies that it ends with a consonant, and so the employment of the word हलः in the text would have been useless had it meant हलन्तात् ॥

इजादेः सन्नुमः ॥ ३२ ॥ पदानि ॥ इजादेः, सन्नुमः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इजादेः सन्नुमः हलन्ताद्वातोर्विहितो यः कृत्स्नयस्य नकारस्योपसर्गस्याभिमिच्छादुत्तरस्य नकारे भवति ॥

32. A krit-affix ordained after a verb beginning with an इच् vowel, having the augment नुम् in it, and ending

BK. VIII. CH. IV. §. 34 ]

CEREBRAL CHANGE.

1667

with a consonant, changes its न into ण, when preceded by an upasarga having in it the cause of change.

The word हलः of the last sūtra is understood here. But contrary to the construction put upon it in the last sūtra, here it means हलन्तात्, by the natural rule of construction as given in I. 1. 72. We must interpret it so here, because it is impossible for an इजादि root to commence with a हलः while to have done so in the last aphorism would have been redundant.

Thus प्रेङ्गुणम्, परेङ्गुणम् from इखि गत्यर्थः; the तुम् is added because it is इदित् ॥ प्रेङ्गुणम्, परेङ्गुणम्, प्रेङ्गुणम् परेङ्गुणम् ॥ In उष्म पूरणे the nasal is part of the root. The rule will not apply to प्रेन्ननम्, because तुम् here means the anusvāra generally ( VIII. 4. 2 ) though the change would have been valid by the general rule, ( VIII. 4. 29 ) this sūtra makes a नियम or restriction. That is, only in the case of इजादि सतुम् verbs the change takes place, not in other सतुम् verbs. Thus प्रेङ्गुणम्, परेङ्गुणम् from the root मणि सर्पणे ॥

This rule does not affect rule VIII. 4. 30, relating to ण्यन्त verbs, for those verbs cannot be said to end with a consonant. Moreover, we have used the word विहितः in explaining the sūtra, in order to indicate this fact, that the krit-affix must be ordained after a consonant-ending verb. In the case of causative verbs, the krit-affix is ordained after a vowel-ending ( णि ) verb, and the vowel is elided after the adding of the affix. So that before the adding of the affix, the verb did not end in a consonant.

वा निसनिश्चनिन्दाम् ॥ ३३ ॥ पदानि ॥ वा, निस-निश्च-निन्दाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपसर्गादितिवर्तते । निस निश्च निन्द इत्येतेषां नकारस्योपसर्गस्याभिमिचादुत्तरस्य वा णकारा-देशो भवति ।

33. The न of निस निश्च and निन्द is changed to ण optionally, when preceded by an upasarga having in it a cause of change.

Thus प्रणिसनम् or प्रनिसनम्, प्रणिक्षणम् or प्रनिक्षणम्, प्रणिन्वनम् or प्रनिन्वनम् ॥

These verbs are written with ण in the Dhātupāṭha, and therefore by rule VIII. 4. 14 ante, the change of न into ण would have been obligatory. The present sūtra makes it optional. The root णिसि means 'to kiss', णिसि रोषणे, and णिसि कृत्स्नायाम् ॥

न भाभूयुकमिगमिष्यायिवेपाम् ॥ ३४ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, भा-भू-पू-कमि-गमि-व्यायि-वेपाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भा दीप्तौ भू सत्तायाम् पू पयने कमि कान्तौ गमि गतौ व्यायि वृद्धौ वेप कम्पने इत्येतेषामुपस-र्गस्याभिमिचादुत्तरस्य कृत्स्नस्य नकारस्य णकारादेशो न भवति ।

पार्त्तिकम् ॥ ण्यन्तानां भावीनामुपसंख्यानं कर्त्तव्यम् ।

34. The न of a krit-affix is not changed to ण, though preceded by an upasarga having in it a cause of change,

23

1668

ण CHANGE.

[ Bk. VIII. Ch. IV. §. 36

when the affix is added to the following verbs: भा 'to shine', भू 'to be', पू 'to purify', कमि 'to be brilliant', गमि 'to go', प्यायि 'to increase', बेप 'to shake'.

This rule is an exception to VIII. 4. 29. Thus :—

भा प्रभानम्, परिभानम् भू प्रभवनम्, परिभवनम् पू प्रपवनम्, परिपवनम् ॥

*Ishti*:—The verb पूम् is to be taken and not the verb पूह् ॥ In the case of the latter the change is obligatory, as, प्रपवर्ण सोमस्य ॥

कमि प्रक्रमनम् परिक्रमनम् ॥ गमि प्रगमनम् परिगमनम् ॥

प्यायि प्रप्यायनम्, परिप्यायनम् ॥ बेप प्रपवेनम्, परिवेपनम् ॥

*Vārt*:—The above roots, even when in the Causative, do not change the न of their krit-affix. As प्रभापनम्, परिभापनम् ॥

पात्पदान्तात् ॥ ३५ ॥ पदानि ॥ पात्, पदान्तात् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पकारान्तादुत्तरस्य नकारस्य नकारविद्यो न भवति ।

35. After a पू final in a Pada, the न is not changed to पू ॥

Thus निप्यानम्, दुष्प्यानम्; the visarga is changed to पू here by VIII. 3. 41. The rule VIII. 4. 29 is debarred. सर्पिप्यानम् (is a genitive compound contra II. 2. 14). So also वज्रप्यानम् (II. 1. 32). The प is in these two by VIII. 3. 45, and VIII. 4. 10 is debarred.

Why do we say 'पात् after a पू?' Observe निर्णयः ॥

Why do we say पदान्तात् 'final in a Pada'? Observe कृष्णाति, पुष्णाति ॥ The word पदान्त is equivalent to पेते अन्त or Locative Tatpurusha; and does not mean final of a Pada. Therefore the rule does not apply here. सुसर्पिष्केण (ins. sg.) सुसर्जुष्केण ॥ Here the क is added by V. 4. 154. शोभनं सर्पिरस्य = सुसर्पिष्क (a Bahuvrihi). The प is by VIII. 3. 39. Before the affix क, the word सुसर्पिष् is a Pada (I. 4. 17), and thus स (प) is final of a Pada: but it is not final of a preceding member followed by another Pada. The rule, in fact, applies to compounds, the प being final in the first term.

नशेः पान्तस्य ॥ ३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ नशेः, पान्तस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नशेः पकारान्तस्य नकारविद्यो न भवति ।

36. पू is not the substitute of the verb नश 'to destroy', when ending in पू ॥

When the पू is changed to पू in नश, the न of नश is not changed. Thus प्रनहः, परिनहः ॥ The तुष ordained by VII. 1. 60, is elided by VI. 4. 24, and पू changed पू by VIII. 2. 36.

Why do we say पान्तस्य? Observe प्रणश्यति, परिणश्यति ॥ The word भन्त is taken in order that the prohibition may apply to words like प्रनहः, which did end with पू though the प has been changed by other rules, and is no longer visible. For here the पू of नश is changed to पू by VIII. 2. 36, and then this पू is changed to क by VIII. 2. 41; and the तुष is added by VII. 1. 60.

BK. VIII. CH. IV. §. 40 ]

ण CHANGE.

1669

पदान्तस्य ॥ ३७ ॥ पदानि ॥ पदान्तस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पदान्तो यो नकारस्तस्य नकारविषो न भवति ।

37. Of a न final in a Pada, ण is not the substitute.

Thus वृक्षान्, प्रक्षान्, शरीरन्, गिरित् ॥

पदव्ययायेपि ॥ ३८ ॥ पदानि ॥ पदव्ययाये, अपि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पदेन व्ययायेपि सति निमित्तनिमित्तिनोर्नकारस्य नकारविषो न भवति ।

वार्तिकम् ॥ पदव्ययाये उत्तदितइति वक्तव्यम् ।

38. The न् is not changed to ण् when a Pada intervenes between the cause of the change and the word containing the न ॥

The word पदव्ययाय is a compound meaning पदेन व्ययाय 'separated by a Pada'. Thus मापकुम्भवापेन, चतुरङ्गयोगेन, प्रायवन्दम्, पर्यवन्दम्, प्रागलयामः, परिगलयामः ॥ Here the Padas कुम्भ, भङ्ग, भव &c, intervening, the change does not take place.

*Vārti:*—It should be stated when there is separation by a Pada, except in a Taddhita. Prohibition does not apply to words like आङ्ग्लोमयेण, शुष्कगोमयेण ॥ Here गो takes the affix मयद् by IV. 3. 145, and the word गो is a Pada by I. 4. 17, and it intervenes between मय and the first word. The author of Mahābhāshya however does not approve of this Vārtika. According to him the word पदव्ययाय means पदे व्ययाय ॥

शुभ्नादिषु च ॥ ३९ ॥ पदानि ॥ शुभ्नादिषु, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शुभ्ना इत्येवनादिषु शक्षेषु नकारस्य नकारविषो न भवति ।

39. The ण् is not the substitute of न् in the words kshubhna &c.

The 'not' of sūtra 34 is to be read into this. Thus शुभ्नाति, so also in शुभ्नीतः, शुभ्नन्ति, the substitutes of भङ्ग being like the principal I. 1. 57.

So नूनमनः where the change was called for by VIII. 4. 3, and VIII. 4. 26.

नन्दिन्, नन्दन and नगर when second members in a compound, denoting a name, as, हरिनन्दी, हरिनन्दनः, गिरिनगरः ॥

The word नून when taking the Intensive affix यङ्ग, as, नरीनृत्यते ॥

नून, नूनति also belongs to this class. नर्नन, गहन, नन्दन, निषेध, निवास, अग्नि and अग्नि when used as second terms in a compound. As, परिनर्ननम्, परिगहनम्, which required change by VIII. 4. 3. So परिनन्दनम् contrary to VIII. 4. 14. शरनिषेधः, शरनिवास, शराग्निः, हर्मायुः ॥ All these are Names.

After the word आचार्य there is no change, as, आचार्यभोगीनः, आचार्यानी ॥

हरिका, तिमिर, समीर, कुबेर and हरि and कर्मी followed by वन do not cause change in the न of वन when the compound is a Name. This is an आकृतिगणः ॥

स्तोः इचुना इचुः ॥ ४० ॥ पदानि ॥ स्तोः, इचुना, इचुः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शकारचवर्गोऽयं संनिपति शकारचवर्गोऽयं भवतः ।

40. The letters स and the dentals when coming in contact with श and the palatals, are changed to श and palatals respectively.

The rule of यथासंख्य does not apply here with regard to first part स्तो इचुना ॥ The स in contact with श is changed to श but it is also so changed when in contact with letters of च class. Similarly letters of त class coming in contact with श or a letter of च class, are changed to च class. The rule of यथासंख्य, however, applies to the substitutes, namely स is changed to श, and तु to चु ॥

1st. स in contact with शः as, वृक्षस् + श्वे = वृक्षश्वेते, so also वृक्षश्वेते ॥

2nd. स in contact with चुः—as, वृक्षस् + चिनोति = वृक्षचिनोति, वृक्षचिनोति, वृक्षश्वा-

श्यति, वृक्षश्वा-श्यति ॥

3rd. तु with शः—अग्निचित् + श्वे = अग्निचित्-श्वेते, so सोमसुच्येते ॥

4th. तु with चुः—अग्निचित् + चिनोति = अग्निचित्-चिनोति, so also सोमसुच्यचिनोति, अग्निचित्-श्वायति, अग्निचित्-श्वायति, अग्निचित्-श्वाकारम्, सोमसुच्यायति, सोमसुच्य-कारम्, अग्निचित्-श्वाकारः, सोमसुच्य-कारः ॥ Similarly मस्य gives मञ्जति, the स is changed to इ by इल्लोजश्व श्वश् VIII. 4. 53, and then this इ is changed to a palatal i. e. to इ here; and इ obtained by जश् rule is not considered asiddha here. See VIII. 2. 3. So also from मस्य we have मञ्जति ॥

5th. चकार followed by तकारः as, यज + न (III. 3. 90) = यज + अ = यजः, याच् + न = याच्-भा ॥ In fact the instrumental case इचुना shows that the mere contact of स and तु with श and चु is enough to induce the change, whether स्तु is followed by इचु, or इचु be followed by स्तु ॥ Other examples of mere contact are :—

5th.(a) स followed by चु is changed into शः as, मस्य + नि = मस्य + श + नि (III. 1. 77, VI. 1. 16) = मस्य + नि = मस्य + नि = (VIII. 4. 53) = मस्य-जति ॥ Similarly मस्य forms मञ्जति, ब्रथ forms वृथति ॥

The aphorism शात् (VIII. 4. 44) which prohibits the change of तु into चु when following the letter श, indicates by implication that the rule of mutual correspondence according to the order of enumeration (I. 3. 10) does not hold good here.

Had the sutra been स्तो श्वोः इचुः i. e. instead of instrumental, had there been the locative case, then the rule would not have applied to cases covered by the fifth clause.

छुना छुः ॥ ४१ ॥ पदानि ॥ छुना, छुः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सकारचवर्गोऽयं पकारचवर्गोऽयं संनिपति पकारचवर्गोऽयं भवतः ।

BK. VIII. CH. IV. §. 43]

PALATAL CHANGE.

1671

41. The letters स and dentals in contact with प and cerebrals, are changed into प and cerebrals respectively.

The word स्तोः is to be read into the sūtra. Here also there is absence of mutual correspondence according to the order of enumeration.

(1) स with प as, वृक्षस् + पण्डे = वृक्षषण्डे; वृक्षषण्डे ॥

(2) स with दु, as, वृक्षस् + दीकते = वृक्षदीकते, वृक्षषण्डे; वृक्षदीकते and वृक्षषण्डे ॥

(3) तु with प as पेष + ता = पेइहा, पेदुम्, पेइह्यम्, कृपीट, कृपीहा: (Atmane, Aorist 2nd per dual).

(4) तु with दु, as, अग्निचित् + दीकते = अग्निचिददीकते, सोमसुददीकते, अग्निचिदङ्कारः, अग्निचित्रूद्दीनः, अग्निचिददीकते, अग्निचिण्णकार, सोमसुदङ्कारः, सोमसुदद्दीनः, सोमसुददीकते, सोमसुदङ्कारः ॥

The root अदृट अतिक्रमणहिंसयोः, and अदृड अभियोगे, are read in the Dhātupātha with त् and द् penultimate, in order that when the affix क्विप् is added to them, the final द and ड being elided by संयोगात् rule, the derivatives will be अदृ and अदृ ending in त् and द् ॥ Another reason is that the sūtra VI. 1. 3, should apply to their reduplicate. In these roots the त and द are changed, as अदृटति and अदृडति ॥

न पदान्ताद्वीरनाम् ॥ ४२ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, पदान्तात्, दोः, अनाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पदान्ताद्वीरनाद्वीरनाम् स्तोः दुर्लभं न भवति नामित्येतदृशीयित्वा ।

वार्तिकम् ॥ अनाम्नवतिनगरीणामिति वक्तव्यम् ।

42. After दु final in a Pada, the change of a dental (स्तु) to a cerebral (दु), does not take place, except in the case of the affix नाम ॥

Thus खलिद् + सादि = खलिद्सादि, मधुलिद्सादि, खलिद्सरति, मधुलिद्सरति ॥

Why do we say पदान्तात् 'final in a Pada'? Observe ईद + ते = ईद + दे = ईदते ॥

Why do we say दोः 'after दु'? Observe सर्विष् + तमम् = सर्विदमम् ॥

Why do we say अनाम् 'except in the case of the affix nām'? Observe पद + नाम = पण्डाम् ॥ This exception is very inadequate. Hence the following

Vārī:—It should be stated rather that नवति and नगरी as well as नाम are not prevented from undergoing the cerebral change. As, पण्डाम् 'of six', पण्डावति: ninety-six, and पण्डागरी 'six cities'.

तोः पि ॥ ४३ ॥ पदानि ॥ तोः, पि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सर्वस्य पकारे यदुक्ते नत्र भवति ।

43. In the room of तु there is not a cerebral substitute, when प follows.

The word न is to be read into the aphorism. As, अग्निचित् + पण्डे = अग्निचित्पण्डे ॥ भवान्पण्डे, महान्पण्डे ॥

REDUPLICATION.

[BK. VIII. CH. IV. § 47]

शात् ॥ ४४ ॥ पदानि ॥ शात् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शकारादुत्तरस्य तवर्गस्य यदुक्तं तत्र भवति ।

44. In the room of तु there is not a palatal substitute, when श precedes.

The words न and तोः are understood here. This is an exception to VIII. 4. 40. Thus, प्रच्छ + न (III. 3. 90) = प्रध + न (VI. 4. 19) = प्रधः, विधः &c.

यरोनुनासिकेनुनासिको वा ॥ ४५ ॥ पदानि ॥ यरः, अनुनासिकं, अनुनासिकः, वा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यरः पदान्तस्यानुनासिकं परतो यानुनासिकादेशो भवति ।

वार्तिकम् ॥ यरोनुनासिकं प्रत्यये भाषायां नित्यवचनं कर्तव्यम् ।

45. In the room of a यर letter (every consonant except ह final) in a Pada, when a Nasal follows, there is optionally a Nasal substitute.

The word पदान्त is understood here. Thus वाक् + नयति = वाग्रयति or वाङ्मययति, अग्निचिद्रययति or अग्निचिन्नयति, विद्वन्नयति or विद्वन्नयति, खलिनययति or खलिङ्गयति ॥

Why do we say 'final in a Pada'? Observe, वेद + नि = वेधि ॥ Here there is no option. So also शुभाति ॥

*Vārt* :—When it is a pratyaya or affix that follows, the nasalisation is obligatory in the secular language. Thus वाक् + माचम् = वाङ्माचम्, कियन्माचम् ॥ It is, however, only before the affixes मय and माच that the change is obligatory, and not before every affix beginning with a nasal.

अचो रहाभ्यां द्वे ॥ ४६ ॥ पदानि ॥ अचः, रहाभ्यां, द्वे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अच उत्तरो यो रेफहकारो ताभ्यादुत्तरस्य यरो द्वे भवतः ।

46. There is reduplication of यर, i. e. all the consonants except ह, after the letters र and ह following a vowel.

The word यर of last sūtra is understood here. According to others, the वा is also understood, and this is an optional rule. Thus अङ्कः, मङ्कः, ब्रह्मा, अपहृदुते ॥

Why do we say अचः 'following a vowel'? Observe हृदुते, ह्यलयति ॥

अनचि च ॥ ४७ ॥ पदानि ॥ अन्, अचि, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अच उत्तरस्य यरो द्वे भवतो ऽनचि परतः ।

वार्तिकम् ॥ यणो मयो द्वे भवत इति वक्तव्यम् ।

वा० ॥ शरः खयो द्वे भवत इति वक्तव्यम् । वा० ॥ अवसाने च यरो द्वे भवतः इति वक्तव्यम् ।

47. When a vowel does not follow, there is reduplication of यर (all the consonants except ह), after a vowel.

The words अचः and यरः are understood here.

BK. VIII. CH. IV §. 50]

REDUPLICATION.

1673

Thus इधि+अच=इधु+अच (VI. I. 77)=इधु+अच इधु+अच (VIII. 4. 53)=इधु, so also मद्धु ॥

Why do we say अचः “after a vowel?” Observe सितम्, सातम् ॥

Vārt:—यणो मयो द्वे भवतः ॥ This Vārtika may be interpreted in two ways. First taking यणः as ablative and मयः as genitive. “The letters of the pratyāhāra मय are reduplicated after यण letters.” उल्का, बाल्मीकः ॥ Secondly taking यणः as genitive, and मयः as ablative. “The letters यण are reduplicated after मय letters”. As इधु, मयबु ॥

Vārt:—शरः खयो द्वे भवतः ॥ This is also similarly explained in two ways. 1st “There is reduplication of खय letters, after a sibilant for शर letters”. as स्थाल, स्थात. Secondly. ‘There is reduplication of a sibilant (शर letters), after खय letters, ss, वत्सरः, अप्सराः ॥

Vārt:—अवसाने च यरो द्वे भवतः ॥ There is reduplication of यर when a Pause ensues. As वाक्, त्वक्, पट्ट, तत्त &c.

These reduplications are curiosities, rather than practicalities.

नादिन्याकोशे पुत्रस्य ॥ ५८ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, आदिनी, आकोशे, पुत्रस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आदिनी परत आकोशे गम्यमाने पुत्रशब्दस्य न द्वे भवतः ।

वात्तिकम् ॥ तत्परे चेति वक्तव्यम् । वा० ॥ वा हतजग्धपरद्वति वक्तव्यम् ।

वा० ॥ चयो द्वितीयाः शरि पौष्करसादिः ।

48. There is not reduplication of the letters of ‘putra’, when the word ādinī follows, the sense being that of reviling or cursing.

This debars the reduplication required by the last sūtra. Thus पुत्रादिनी त्वमसि पापे “O sinful one! thou art eater of thy own son”. Here the word पुत्रादिनी is used simply as an abusive epithet. But when a fact is described, and the word is not used as an abuse or आकोश, the reduplication takes place. Thus पुत्रादिनी व्याघ्री ‘a kind of tigress, that eats up her young ones’. =शिष्टुमारी व्याघ्री ॥

Vārt:—So also when पुत्र is followed by पुत्रादिनी ॥ As पुत्र पुत्रादिनी त्वमसि पापे ॥ So also पुत्रपौषादिनी ॥

Vārt:—Optionally so when the words हत and जग्ध follow. As पुत्रहती or पुत्रहती, पुत्रजग्धी or पुत्रजग्धी ॥

Vārt:—According to the option of Āchārya Paushkarasādi, the letters of खय pratyāhāra are replaced by the second letters of their class, when followed by a sibilant (a letter of शर pratyāhāra).

As वत्सः becomes वधुसः अशरम् becomes अशरम् and अप्सरा becomes अफसरा ॥
