शरोचि ॥ ४६ ॥ पदानि ॥ शरः, अचि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शरोचि परतो न दे भवतः ।

49. There are not two in the room of a sibilant (शर), when a vowel follows.

The word न is to be read into the sūtra. This debars the application of rule 46 ante. Thus कर्पति, वर्षति, आकर्षः, अक्षदर्शः ॥

Why do we say अचि 'when a vowel follows? Observe हृदयते ॥

त्रिभूतिषु शाकटायनस्य ॥ ५० ॥ पदानि ॥ त्रिभूतिषु, शाकटायनस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ त्रिभूतिषु वर्णेषु संयुक्तेषु शाकटायनस्याचार्यस्य मतेन न भवति ।

50. According to the option of Śākatāyana, the doubling does not take place when the conjunct consonants are three or more in number.

As इन्द्रः, चन्द्रः, इन्द्रः, राष्ट्रम्, धाट्टम् ॥

सर्वैत्र शाकल्यस्य ॥ ५१ ॥ पदानि ॥ सर्वैत्र, शाकल्यस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शाकल्याचार्यस्य मतेन सर्वैत्र द्विवेचनं न भवति ।

51. According to the opinion of Śākalya, there is reduplication no where.

As अर्कः, मर्कः, ब्रह्मः, अपहृदते ॥

दीर्घोदाचार्याणाम् ॥ ५२ ॥ पदानि ॥ दीर्घोत, आचार्याणाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दीर्घोतुत्तरस्याचार्याणां मतेन न भवति ।

52. According to the opinion of all Teachers, there is no doubling after a long vowel.

As वानम्, वानम्, वानम्, वानम् ॥

इलां जडशशि ॥ ५३ ॥ पदानि ॥ इलाम्, जश्, इशि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इलां स्थाने जशादेशो भवति इशि परतः ।

53. In the room of इल् letters, there is substitution of जश् letters, when इश् letters follow.

A mute letter is changed to a sonant non-aspirate mute, when a sonant mute follows it.

This is the well-known rule of softening the hard letters. Thus लम्+ ता=लम्, so also लम्+ लम्+ लम्+ ; रोम्या, रोम्युम्, रोम्यव्यम् ; बोद्धा, बोद्धुम्, बोद्धव्यम् ॥

Why do we say इशि, 'when a jhas follows'? Observe इन्द्रः, इन्द्रः, इन्द्रः ॥

अभ्यासे चर्च ॥ ५४ ॥ पदानि ॥ अभ्यासे, चर्, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अभ्यासे वर्त्तमानानां इलां चरादेशो भवति चकाराऽजम् ।

54. The चर् is also the substitute of इल् letters occurring in a reduplicate syllable, as well as जश् ॥

In a reduplicate syllable, a sonant non-aspirate (जश्) as well as a surd non aspirate (चर्) is the substitute of a Mute letter. By applying the rule of

BK. VIII. CH. IV §. 57 ]

चर CHANGE.

1675

'nearest in place (I. 1. 50), we find that sonant non-aspirate (जश्) is the substitute of all sonants; and is the substitute of all surds. In other words all aspirate letters become non-aspirate. The word जश् has been drawn into the sutra by the word च 'also'.

Thus चिखनिपति ॥ Here सत् (Desiderative), is added to the root खत्, the ख is changed to छ by VII. 4. 62, and this aspirate छ is now changed to non-aspirate by the present sutra. चिच्छिपति, दिङ्कारयिपति, तिघ्रासति, पिफकारयिपति, बुभुपति, जिपसति, डुबोकिपति ॥

If there is चर् (non-aspirate surd) in the original, it will remain of course unchanged. As, चिचीपति, दिठीकिपति, तितनिपति ॥

The original जश् also remains unchanged. Thus जिजनिपति, बुभुपे, इबे, विङ्ये ॥ Or to be more accurate a चर् is replaced by a चर् and a जश् by a जश् letter.

खरि च ॥ ५५ ॥ पदानि ॥ खरि, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ खरि च परतो झलां चरादेशो भवति ।

55. In the room of झल्, there is the substitute चर्, when खर् follows.

A sonant non-aspirate mute is the substitute of a mute, when a surd mute or a sibilant follows. The words झलां and चरः are supplied from the last sutra. Thus भेद्+ता=भेत्ता, भेत्तुम्, भेत्तव्यम्; युयुप्+सते=युयुत्सते; आरिप्सते, आलिप्सते from रम् and लम्, the इस् is added by VII. 4. 54, in the room of अ of रम् and लम्, and we have रिस्स् and लिस्स् then the first स is elided by VIII. 2. 29.

वावसाने ॥ ५६ ॥ पदानि ॥ वा, अवसाने ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ झलां चरिति वर्तते । अवसाने वर्तनानानां झलां वा चरादेशो भवति ।

56. The चर् is optionally the substitute of a झल् that occurs in a Pause.

The words भलां चर् is understood in the sutra. A sonant or a surd non-aspirate may stand as final in a Pause: but not an aspirate consonant. By VIII. 2. 39, a non-aspirate sonant can only stand in a final position. This ordains that a non-aspirate surd may also stand as the final, when there is Pause. Thus वाक् or वाग्, लक् or लम्, भलिङ् or भलिङ्, विङ्गु or विङ्गु ॥

अणोप्रगृह्यस्यानुनासिकः ॥ ५७ ॥ पदानि ॥ अणः, अप्रगृह्यस्य, अनुनासिकः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अणः अप्रगृह्यसज्ञस्यावसाने वर्तनाने वानुनासिकादेशो भवति ।

57. The anunāsika is optionally the substitute of an अण् vowel which occurs in a Pause, and is not a Pragrihya.

अ, इ and व, short and long, may, when final in a Pause, be pronounced as nasals, provided that they are not Pragrihya (I. 1. 11 &c.) The अण् here

24

1676

SEMI-VOWEL CHANGE.

[BK. VIII. CH. IV. §. 60]

is a Pratyāhāra with the first ण् ॥ Thus इधिं or इधि, मधुं or मधु, कुमारीं or कुमारीं ॥

Why do we say 'of an अण् vowel?' Observe, कर्तुं, हर्तुं ॥

Why do we say 'which is not a pragrihya'? Observe अग्नी, वायु which are pragrihya by I. I. II.

अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः ॥ ५८ ॥ पदानि ॥ अनुस्वारस्य, ययि, परसवर्णः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ अनुस्वारस्य ययि परतः परसवर्ण आविशो भवति ।

58. In the room of anusvāra, when यय follows, a letter homogeneous with the latter is substituted.

Thus शङ्किता, शङ्कितुम्, शङ्कितव्यम्, उच्छिता, कुण्डिता, नन्दिता, कम्पिता &c. These are from roots शाकि शङ्कायाम्, उच्छि उच्छे, कुण्डिते, दुन्दि सङ्गृही, कपि चले ॥ Here तुव् is added because they are उदित्, and this न् becomes anusvāra by VIII. 3. 24, and this anusvāra is changed to ङ् when followed by a guttural क् &c, to म् when followed by a palatal च &c, and so on to ण्, न् and म् ॥

Why do we say when यय follows? Observe आकंस्थते, आचिकंस्थते ॥

In कुर्वन्ति, वृषन्ति, the न् is not changed into ण्, though required by VIII. 4. 2. Because the ण्व् is asiddha, and therefore by the prior rule VIII. 3. 24, the न् is first changed into anusvāra (VIII. 2. 1). That anusvāra is again changed into न् by the present rule, न् being homogeneous with त् ॥ This change again being असिद्ध as if it had never taken place (VIII. 2. 1), the ण् is never substituted for न् ॥

वा पदान्तस्य ॥ ५९ ॥ पदानि ॥ वा, पदान्तस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पदान्तस्यानुस्वारस्य ययि परतो वा परसवर्णविषो भवति ।

59. In the room of anusvāra final in a Pada, the substitution of a letter homogeneous with the latter is optional.

Thus तं कथं चित्रपक्षं उयमानं नभःस्थं पुरुषोऽवधीत् or तङ्ग्यञ्चित्रपक्षण्डयमाननभःस्थपुरुषोऽवधीत् ॥

तोऽपि ॥ ६० ॥ पदानि ॥ तोः, णि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तदग्नस्य लकारे परतः परसवर्णविषो भवति ।

60. In the room of तु (a dental) when the letter ण् follows, one homogeneous with the latter is substituted.

Thus अग्निचित् + लुनाति = अग्निचिल्लुनाति, सोमसुल्लुनाति; भवान् + लुनाति = भवान् - लुनाति, महल्लुनाति ॥ Here त् has been changed to pure ण्, while the dento-nasal न् is changed to a nasal ण् ॥

उदः खास्तम्भोः पूर्वस्य ॥ ६१ ॥ पदानि ॥ उदः, खा स्तम्भोः, पूर्वस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उद उत्तरयोः स्था स्तम्भ इत्येतयोः पूर्वसवर्णविषो भवति ।

वार्तिकम् ॥ उदः पूर्वसवर्णत्वे स्कन्देऽष्टन्दस्युपसंख्यानम् ।

वा० ॥ रोमे चेति वक्तव्यम् ।

BK. VIII. CH. IV. §. 64 ]

CONSONANTAL CHANGE.

1677

61. After उद्, in the room of the स of sthā and stambha, the substitute is a letter belonging to the class of the prior (i. e. a dental is substituted for this स) ॥

As उद्+स्थाता=उद्+ध्याता=उद्+धाता (VIII. 4. 65)=उद्+धाता (VIII. 4. 55)=उत्थाता, उत्थातुम्, उत्थातव्यम् ॥ So also with स्तम्भ, as, उत्तम्भिता, उत्तम्भितुम् &c. (See I. 1. 67 and 54).

Why do we say of स्था and स्तम्भ? Compare उत्थात ॥

Vārt:—In the Vedas, the above substitution takes place in the case of स्कन्द preceded by उद् ॥ As, अये दूरदुक्कन्दः ॥

Vārt:—So also when it means a disease. As उत्कन्दको नाम रोगः ॥ Or this form may have been derived from the root कन्द, and not स्कन्द ॥

इयो होन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ६२ ॥ पदानि ॥ इयः, हः, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इय उत्तरस्य हकारस्य पूर्वसवर्णवेशो भवति अन्यतरस्याम् ।

62. In the room of the letter ह, after (a sonant Mute) there is optionally a letter homogeneous with the prior.

The pratyāhāra इय includes all Mutes. But practically sonant Mutes are only taken here.

As वाक्+हसति=वाग्यसति or वाग् हसति, खलिङ् हसति or हसति, भिमिचिन् भसति or हसति, चिट्ठु भसति or हसति, सोमसुद् भसति or सोमसुद् हसति ॥

Why do we say इयः 'after a sonant Mute?' Observe प्राह् हसति, भवान् हसति ॥

दाइछोटि ॥ ६३ ॥ पदानि ॥ दाः, छः, अदि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इय इति वच्यते । अन्यतरस्यामिति च । इय उत्तरस्य शकारस्यादि परतइछकारवेशो भवति अन्यतरस्याम् ।

वात्तिकम् ॥ छत्वममीति वक्तव्यम् ।

63. In the room of श preceded by a surd Mute, there is optionally the letter छ् when a vowel or य, व or र follows such श ॥

Though इय means all Mutes, the rule, however, applies to surd mutes. The words इय and अन्यतरस्यां are to be read into the sūtra. Thus वाक्+शेते=वाक्छते or शेते ॥ अभिमिच्छते or अभिमिचिन् शेते, खलिङ् शेते or छेते, चिट्ठुछेते or शेते ॥

Vārt:—It should rather be stated when a letter of अम् pratyāhāra follows. The sūtra only gives अद् letters, the vārtika adds the letters ल, and the nasals. Thus तत् ग्लोकेन=तत् ग्लोकेन, तच्छमभुणा ॥

हलो यमां यमि लोपः ॥ ६४ ॥ पदानि ॥ हलः, यमाम्, यमि, लोपः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हल उत्तरेषां यमां यमि परतो लोपो भवति अन्यतरस्याम् ।

1678

ELISION.

[ Bk. VIII. Ch. IV. §. 65

64. After a consonant, the following semi-vowel or a nasal is elided optionally, when the same letters follow it.

The word अन्यतरस्याम् should be read into the sūtra. Thus शब्दया or शब्द्या, the middle य् being elided. In शब्दया there are two य्, one of the affix (III. 3. 99); and the second of अयङ्ग (VII. 4. 22), and the third arises by doubling (VIII. 4. 47). आविल्य (formed by doubling य् by the Vārtika under 47 ante), or आविल्य 'son of Aditi'. In आविल्य there are two य्, one of ण्य् (IV. 1. 85), and the second arises by doubling.

Similarly आविल्य देवता अस्य स्थाली पाकस्य=आविल्याः ॥ Then by VIII. 4. 47, there is a third य्, as आविल्य ॥ Here also we may elide the one middle य् or both the middle य्'s. Thus आविल्यः or आविल्यः ॥

Why do we say हलः 'preceded by a consonant'? Observe असम् when य् is preceded by a vowel.

Why do we say यमाम् 'of यम् letters'? Observe असमिः, अर्थम् (V. 4. 25) where य् is not य् ॥

Why do we say यमि 'when यम् follows'? Observe शार्ङ्गम् here ङ् is not followed by a यम् ॥

झरो झरि सवर्णे ॥ ६५ ॥ पदानि ॥ झरः, झरि, सवर्णे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हल उत्तरस्य झरो झरि सवर्णे परतो लोपी भवति अन्यतरस्याम् ।

65. A Mute or Sibilant (झर) preceded by a consonant and followed by a homogeneous mute or sibilant, is optionally elided.

The word हलः is understood. Thus मत्तम्, अवत्तम् have three त, namely, one त substituted for आ by VII. 4. 47, the second त resulting from the change of व to त by चत्व् change, the third त is that of the affix. A fourth arises by doubling (VIII. 4. 47) of these four, one or two middle ones may be dropped. मस्तत्त् here are four तs. A fifth may be added by doubling, and by this rule, one, two or three of them may be elided. मस्त्+वा+क्त=मस्त्+दत्त+त (VII. 4. 47) the word मस्त् being treated as an Upasarga (I. 4. 59, vārt)=मस्तत्त् ॥

Why do we say झरः 'of a jhar'? Compare शार्ङ्गम्, here ङ् which is not a झर is not elided, though it is followed by a झर letter. Why do we say झरि 'followed by a jhar'? See प्रियपञ्चः ॥ This is a Bahuvṛhi compound=प्रियाः पञ्चास्य ॥ The word प्रिय stands first in the compound under II. 2. 35. (vārt). The full word is प्रियपञ्चम्, the अ is elided by VI. 4. 134, and we have प्रियपञ्चम्; and then this य् becomes a palatal अ ॥ Here य् is preceded by a हल् letter, and itself is a झर, and is followed by a homogeneous

ACCENT.

1679

letter ञ्, but as ञ् is not झर्, the ञ् is not elided. The elided ञ is not considered sthanivat, and so ञ is considered to be *immediately* followed by ञ् ॥

Why do we say सवर्ण 'when a homogeneous jhar follows'? Observe तर्पु, तर्पम् &c, where प and ञ are not homogeneous.

By using the word सवर्ण, the rule of mutual correspondence (I. 3. 10) is avoided. Had the rule been झरो झरि the rule of mutual correspondence according to order of enumeration would have applied, and the forms शिण्डि शिण्डि could not have been evolved by the elision of ञ before ञ ॥ For the evolution of these forms see the commentary under I. 1. 58. These are the Imperative 2nd Person Singular of शिष् and पिष् ॥ The ञ of ञम् is elided by VI. 4. 111: the ञि is changed to ञि by VI. 4. 101, the ञ् is changed to ञ् by VIII. 4. 53, the ञ् of ञम् is changed to anusvāra by VIII. 3. 24; this anusvāra is again changed to ञ् by VIII. 4. 58; the ञ is changed to ञ्, and by the present rule, the preceding ञ् is elided before this ञ ॥

उदात्तादुत्वात्तस्य स्वरितः ॥ ६६ ॥ पदानि ॥ उदात्तात्, अनुदात्तस्य, स्वरितः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ उदात्तादुत्वात्तस्य स्वरितादेशो भवति ।

66. The Svarita is the substitute of an Anudatta vowel which follows an Udatta vowel.

Thus अभिम्+ईले=अभिमिले ॥ Here ई which was अनुदात्त by rule VIII. 1. 28, becomes svarita by the present rule, as it comes after the udatta ई of agni.

So also गोर्य्यः, वैलस्यः ॥ Here यम् is added by IV. 1. 105, and being भिम् the words are first acute. The final is anudatta, which becomes svarita. So also वैलति and पेइति, the शप् and लिप् are anudatta, the root is accented, the ञ of शप् becomes svarita.

The rule VI. 1. 158, does not change this svarita into an Anudatta, because for the purposes of that rule, the present rule is अभिम्, or as if it had not taken place (VIII. 2. 1). Therefore both the udatta and the svarita accent are heard.

नोदात्तस्वरितोदयमगोर्यकाइयपगालवानाम् ॥ ६७ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, उदात्त-स्वरित-उदयम्, अ-गोर्य-काइयप-गालवानाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उदात्तोदयस्य स्वरितोदयस्य चातुदात्तस्य स्वरितो न भवति अगोर्यकाइयपगालवानामाचार्याणां मतिन ॥ उदात्तोदयः=उदा.तपरः ।

67 All prohibit the above substitution of svarita, except the Acharyās Gārgya, Kāsyapa and Gālava; when an udatta or a svarita follows the anudatta.

This debars the preceding rule. That anudatta which is *followed* by an Udatta is उदात्तोदयः or उदात्तपरः ॥ The word उदय means पर in the terminology of ancient Grammarians. That anudatta which is *followed* by a svarita is called स्वरितोदयः ॥ These are Bahuvṛhi compounds. Thus उदात्तोदयः—गोर्य-

1680

ACCENT.

[BK VIII. CH. IV §. 68]

स्त्वं, वैष्णव स्त्वं ॥ The word स्त्वं is first acute by लिङ् accent, before this udatta, the य of these words does not become svarita. So with स्वरितोऽयः—गौर्यः कं वैष्णवः कं ॥ The word कः is svarita being formed by the लिङ् affix अत (V. 3. 12); before this svarita the preceding य does not become svarita.

Why do we say “except in the opinion of Gārgya, Kāśyapa and Gālava”? Observe गौर्यः कं, गौर्यस्त्वं ॥ According to their opinion, the svarita change does take place.

The employment of the longer word उदय instead of the shorter word पर is for the sake of auspiciousness, for the Book has approached the end. The very utterance of the word उदय is auspicious. All sacred works commence with an auspicious word, have an auspicious word in the middle, and end with an auspicious word. Thus Pāṇini commences his sūtra with the auspicious word वृद्भिः ‘increase’ (in Sūtra I. 1. 1): has the word शिव ‘the well-wisher’ in the middle (IV. 4. 143), and उदय at the end.

The mention of the names of those several Āchāryas is for the sake of showing respect (pujārtham).

अ अ इति ॥ इट ॥ पदानि ॥ अ, अ, इति ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ एकोष विवृतो उपरः संवृतस्त्वं विवृतस्य संवृतः क्रियते । अकारो विवृतः संवृतो भवति ।

68. The अ which was considered to be open (विवृत) in all the preceding operations of this Grammar, is now made contracted (संवृत) ॥

The first अ is here विवृत or open; the second is संवृत or contracted. The open अ is now changed to contracted अ ॥ “In actual use the organ in the enunciation of the short अ is contracted; but it is considered to be open only, as in the case of the other vowels, when the vowel अ is in the state of taking part in some operation of Grammar. The reason for this is, that if the short अ were held to differ from the long अ in this respect, the homogeneousness mentioned in I. 1. 9, would not be found to exist between them, and the operation of the rules depending upon that homogeneousness would be debarred. In order to restore the short अ to its natural rights, thus infringed throughout the Ashtādhyāyi, Pāṇini with oracular brevity in his closing aphorism gives the injunction अ अ; which is interpreted to signify—Let short अ be held to have its organ of utterance contracted, now that we have reached the end of the work in which it was necessary to regard it as being otherwise”. (Dr. Ballantyne).

Thus वृक्षः, प्रक्षः ॥ In this Grammar, the अ is regarded open or vivrita, when operations are performed with it; but in actual pronunciation it is contracted. The long अ and the pluta अः ३ are not meant to be included here in the open short अ; therefore those two are not contracted by this rule. Only

भ भ

the *short* भ consisting of *one* *mātra*, with *its* various modifications is to be taken here. In other words the *six* shorts भ are only taken here, namely भँ, भ, भँ, भँ, भँ, भँ॥ For these six short open भs, there are substituted six contracted corresponding भs See 1. 1. 9.
